Initially created: 2025-11-23T03:23:59.437+09:00 by CH Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into $lang.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.
Input text:

p.seg: Once, the Tathāgata was in the Gǐshéjué Shān,
with the great Arhats, Āruò Jiāochénrú,
Móhē Jiāshè, and countless others,
expounding the Great Vehicle True Sutra,
named Immeasurable Meaning (Wúliángyì).
At that time, precious flowers rained down, spreading and filling the area,
the light of wisdom manifested auspicious signs, illuminating the hidden and obvious,
the entire Buddha world experienced six kinds of tremors,
all humans and devas gained what they had never had before,
all rejoiced and praised,
thinking this sutra to be the secret treasury of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas,
divine and unfathomable,
vast and difficult to name,
therefore rescuing those drowning in the currents of stagnation,
saving those lost in the darkness of their nature,
its merits vast and boundless.
Tracing its origins,
it began in Zhúqián (India) and flowed to Zhèndàn (China).
Starting with the Śramaṇa Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jìn Dynasty, who first translated it,
named *Zhèng Fǎ Huá*;
later, the Tripiṭaka Master Jūmóluóshí of Qiūcí in the Eastern Jìn Dynasty re-translated it,
named *Miàofǎ Liánhuā*;
and the one translated by the Śramaṇa Shénà Jípūduō from Tiānzhú (India) in the Suí Dynasty,
was also named *Miàofǎ*.
Although the three sutras have overlapping and mutually explaining texts and principles,
only the Tripiṭaka Master alone grasped its essence.
However, as time has passed, there have been errors,
without correction, gradually leading to much doubt,
therefore, I have specially collated and revised it,
and ordered it to be engraved and printed to spread its transmission.
Alas!
The Tathāgata, pitying all sentient beings with various natures,
various desires,
various practices,
various memories, thoughts, and discriminations,
entangled for kalpas without any hope of escape,
therefore appeared in the world for this great event,
expounding the wonderful meaning,
creating extraordinary expedient means,
so that all can be liberated and transcend to attain Right Enlightenment,
this is truly a ferry for crossing the sea and a torch for illuminating the darkness.
Good men,
good women,
all sentient beings,
who can uphold with sincerity, recite, wear, and reverently prostrate and make offerings,
will immediately be separated from all suffering and distress,
remove all karmic obstacles,
and resolve all the calamities of birth and death.
It is like hunger finding food,
like thirst finding drink,
like cold finding fire,
like heat finding coolness,
like poverty finding treasure,
like sickness finding a doctor,
like a child finding its mother,
like crossing finding a boat,
its comfort and joy,
are beyond words.
Alas!
The Dao cannot be embodied without a sutra,
the Dharma cannot be transmitted without a sutra.
Through the sutra, seek the Dharma,
through the Dharma, realize the Dao,
then you will know that the meaning of this sutra is pure, subtle, and the most rare and wonderful.
Those who follow it will attain health and peace,
and all kinds of good roots will be completely fulfilled,
like a lotus flower emerging from the water, not stained by mud,
and immediately attain the emptiness of the five skandhas,
and the purity of the six senses,
and quickly ascend to supreme goodness to achieve Right Enlightenment, which is not difficult.
If one is stubborn and attached,
willing to fall and extinguish good roots,
then one will suffer in miserable realms,
and cycle through the realms of birth and death,
how can there be an end to it?
Although the paths of good and evil are chosen by people,
doing good brings fortune,
doing evil brings misfortune,
the karmic consequences in the visible and invisible realms are accurate to the smallest degree.
Those who observe this sutra,
should be cautious!
Should strive!
The 17th day of the 4th month of the 18th year of Yǒnglè.
Shì Dàoxuān of the Zhōngnán Shān of Táng describes the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*
as embodying the fundamental essence of all Buddhas descending and manifesting.
It was conceived in Great Xia (India),
emerging after a thousand years.
Transmitted east to Zhèndàn (China),
for more than three hundred years.
During the Yǒngkāng era of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn Dynasty,
the Bodhisattva Zhú Fǎhù of Qīngmén, Dūnhuáng in Cháng'ān,
first translated this sutra,
named *Zhèng Fǎ Huá*.
During the Lóng'ān era of Emperor Ān of the Eastern Jìn Dynasty,
in the Hóngshǐ period of the Later Qín,
the Śramaṇa Jūmóluóshí of Qiūcí translated this sutra for the second time,
named *Miàofǎ Liánhuā*.
During the Rénshòu period of the Suí Dynasty,
the Śramaṇa Shénà Jípūduō from Northern Tiānzhú (India) at Dàxīngshàn Temple translated it later,
with the same name *Miàofǎ*.
The three sutras overlap,
with mutually explaining texts and meanings.
What was valued at the time,
was all based on the Qín version.
As for other branches and chapters,
separate verses,
there were some circulated,
as detailed in the historical records,
therefore, I will not describe them.
For spiritual manifestations descend from the spiritual peak,
without a great sage, there is no way to initiate transformation;
where transformation reaches,
without past affinities, there is no way to guide the mind.
Therefore, in the celestial garden, the teaching was completed,
with distinctions between the capacities of small and great;
at the Jīnhé (Golden River), the destiny was entrusted,
with doctrines differentiated into provisional and complete.
Is it not that the teachings were given according to the times,
and there is no need to examine its elevated assembly.
It is known that the five thousand who withdrew,
were to advance those of arrogance and sloth;
the five hundred who received predictions,
all revered the traces of secret transformation.
Therefore, emitting light and manifesting auspicious signs,
opened the source of teaching through requests;
emerging from samadhi and proclaiming virtues,
elucidated the vast strategy of the Buddha's wisdom.
The decaying house allows entry into the path of the Great Vehicle,
the phantom city guides those of past affinities without falling away,
the jewel tied in the robe clarifies the constant presence of Buddha-nature,
digging a well reveals the multiple ways to enlightenment.
The words and meanings are clear,
and the metaphors are distant.
If not for the Great Compassion that saves all,
rescuing those drowning in the currents of stagnation;
and the utmost compassionate mind,
saving those lost in the darkness of their nature.
From the Hàn Dynasty to the Táng Dynasty, more than six hundred years,
and totaling more than four thousand scrolls of various texts,
there is no sutra that has been more widely received and upheld than this one.
It must be that the faculties and the teaching correspond,
together with the remaining dust of superior wisdom;
hearing it with deep respect,
all are the remaining merits of King Awesome Sound.
Therefore, at the beginning of the sutra,
I have written a preface to summarize it.
Hoping to purify the six senses early,
and rely on the auspicious assembly of the Compassionate One;
quickly accomplish the Four Virtues,
and strive towards the profound plans of the Land of Bliss.
Praise and blessings are endless,
and will be passed on to future generations forever.
So be it.
The first volume of the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jūmóluóshí of Qiūcí Kingdom of the Later Qín by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was dwelling on Gǐshéjué Mountain in the city of Wángshěchéng,
together with a great assembly of twelve thousand Bhikṣus,
all of whom were Arhats,
their defilements exhausted,
no longer having afflictions,
having attained their own benefit,
having exhausted all bonds,
their minds at ease.
Their names were: Āruò Jiāochénrú,
Móhē Jiāshè,
Yōlóupínluó Jiāshè,
Gāyé Jiāshè,
Nátí Jiāshè,
Shèlìfú,
Dàmùqiánlián,
Móhē Jiāzhān yán,
Ānóulóutú,
Jiébīnnuó,
Jiāofánbōtí,
Lí Pótā,
Bìlíngqié Pósuō,
Bójūluó,
Móhē Jūchīluó,
Nánduó,
Sūntuóluó Nánduó,
Fùlóunà Míduōluónízǐ,
Xūpútí,
Ānán,
Luóhóuluó.
Such were the great Arhats known to the assembly.
There were also two thousand people still learning and beyond learning.
Mahāpajāpatī Bhikṣunī, together with her retinue of six thousand people.
The Bhikṣunī Yéshūtuóluó, mother of Luóhóuluó,
was also with her retinue.
Eighty thousand Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas,
all irreversible in Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi;
all having obtained dhāraṇīs;
delighting in eloquent discourse,
turning the irreversible Dharma wheel;
having made offerings to countless hundreds of thousands of Buddhas,
having planted roots of virtue in the presence of all the Buddhas,
constantly praised by all the Buddhas;
cultivating themselves with compassion,
well-entered into the wisdom of the Buddhas;
understanding great wisdom,
having reached the other shore;
their names universally heard in countless worlds,
able to deliver countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings.
Their names are: Wénshūshīlì Púsà,
Guānshìyīn Púsà,
Dé Dàshì Púsà,
Cháng Jīngjìn Púsà,
Bù Xiūxī Púsà,
Bǎo Zhǎng Púsà,
Yàowáng Púsà,
Yǒng Shī Púsà,
Bǎo Yuè Púsà,
Yuèguāng Púsà,
Mǎnyuè Púsà,
Dàlì Púsà,
Wúliàng Lì Púsà,
Yuè Sānjiè Púsà,
Bátuó Póluó Púsà,
Mílè Púsà,
Bǎo Jī Púsà,
Dǎoshī Púsà,
Eighty thousand Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas, such as these, were all present.
At that time, Shì Tí Huán Yīn, together with his retinue of twenty thousand devaputras, was present.
Also present were Naming Yuè Tiānzǐ,
Pǔ Xiāng Tiānzǐ,
Bǎo Guāng Tiānzǐ,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
together with their retinues of ten thousand devaputras.
Zìzài Tiānzǐ,
Dà Zìzài Tiānzǐ,
together with their retinues of thirty thousand devaputras.
The lord of the Sahā world,
Brahmā-rāja—
Shī Qì Dà Fàn,
Guāngmíng Dà Fàn, and others,
together with their retinues of twelve thousand devaputras.
There were eight Nāga-rājas—
Nánduó Nāga-rāja,
Bátuó Nánduó Nāga-rāja,
Suōjiāluó Nāga-rāja,
Héxiūjí Nāga-rāja,
Déchājiā Nāga-rāja,
Ānà Pó Dáduō Nāga-rāja,
Mónàsī Nāga-rāja,
Yōubōluó Nāga-rāja, and others,
each together with their respective retinues of several hundred thousand.
There were four Kinnara-rājas—
Fǎ Jǐnnàluó-rāja,
Miào Fǎ Jǐnnàluó-rāja,
Dà Fǎ Jǐnnàluó-rāja,
Chí Fǎ Jǐnnàluó-rāja,
each together with their respective retinues of several hundred thousand.
There were four Gandharva-rājas—
Lè Qiántuópó-rāja,
Lè Yīn Qiántuópó-rāja,
Měi Qiántuópó-rāja,
Měi Yīn Qiántuópó-rāja,
each together with their respective retinues of several hundred thousand.
There were four Asura-rājas—
Pózhì Āxiūluó-rāja,
Qiáluóqiān Tuó Āxiūluó-rāja,
Pímózhìduōluó Āxiūluó-rāja,
Luóhóu Āxiūluó-rāja,
each together with their respective retinues of several hundred thousand.
There were four Garuḍa-rājas—
Dà Wēidé Jiālóuluó-rāja,
Dà Shēn Jiālóuluó-rāja,
Dà Mǎn Jiālóuluó-rāja,
Rúyì Jiālóuluó-rāja,
each together with their respective retinues of several hundred thousand.
Wèitíxīzǐ Āshéshì-rāja,
together with a retinue of several hundred thousand, was present.
Each paid homage at the Buddha's feet and withdrew to sit on one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
surrounded by the four assemblies,
was being offered to, revered,
honored, and praised.
For the sake of the Bodhisattvas, he was expounding a Mahāyāna sūtra,
named Immeasurable Meanings,
teaching the Bodhisattva dharma,
protected and念by the Buddhas.
After the Buddha had spoken this sūtra,
he sat in the lotus position,
and entered into the Samādhi of the Abode of Immeasurable Meanings.
His body and mind were unmoving.
At that time, the heavens rained Maṇḍārava flowers,
Mahā-Maṇḍārava flowers,
Mañjuṣaka flowers,
Mahā-Mañjuṣaka flowers,
and scattered them upon the Buddha and the great assembly.
The Buddha-worlds everywhere shook in six ways.
At that time, in the assembly, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans,
as well as the various lesser kings and cakravartin-rājas,
all these great assemblies, having obtained what they had never had before,
joyfully joined their palms and single-mindedly gazed at the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha emitted a white hair-curl light from between his eyebrows,
illuminating eighteen thousand worlds to the east,
without exception, universally,
down to Avīci hell,
and up to Akanistha heaven.
In this world, they completely saw the sentient beings of the six realms in those lands,
and also saw the Buddhas present in those lands,
and heard the sūtras and dharmas spoken by the Buddhas.
They also saw the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās in those lands, all those who cultivated practice and attained the Path.
Furthermore, they saw the Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas, with various conditions, various beliefs and understandings, and various appearances, practicing the Bodhisattva Path.
Furthermore, they saw the Buddhas who had entered parinirvāṇa.
Furthermore, they saw that after the Buddhas had entered parinirvāṇa, they erected seven-jeweled stūpas with the Buddha's śarīra.
At that time, Mílè Púsà had this thought:
"Now the World-Honored One is manifesting miraculous signs.
What is the cause and condition for this auspicious sign?
Now the Buddha World-Honored One has entered into samādhi.
This is inconceivable, a rare and unusual event.
Whom should I ask about this?
Who is able to answer?"
And again, he had this thought:
"This Wénshūshīlì, the son of the Dharma King,
has already personally drawn near to and made offerings to countless Buddhas of the past.
He must surely have seen this rare and unusual sign.
I shall now ask him."
At that time, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and the various devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits,
all had this thought:
"This sign of the Buddha's light and spiritual power,
whom should we ask about it now?"
At that time, Mílè Púsà, desiring to resolve his own doubts,
and also observing the minds of the four assemblies: bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and the assemblies of the various devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits,
then asked Wénshūshīlì, saying:
"What is the cause and condition for this auspicious sign of spiritual power,
emitting great light, illuminating eighteen thousand lands to the east,
completely seeing the adornments of those Buddha-lands?"
Thereupon, Mílè Púsà, desiring to restate this meaning,
asked in verse, saying:
"Wénshūshīlì!
For what reason does the Guide,
from the white hair-curl between his eyebrows, emit great light that universally illuminates?
Raining Maṇḍārava flowers, Mañjuṣaka flowers,
with sandalwood fragrance, delighting the hearts of the assembly?
Due to these causes and conditions, the earth is entirely adorned and purified,
and this world shakes in six ways.
At this time, the fourfold assembly, all rejoice,
their bodies and minds are joyful,
having obtained what they had never had before.
The light between his eyebrows illuminates the eastern direction,
eighteen thousand lands, all like gold in color,
from Avīci hell,
up to the Summit of Existence.
Within these worlds,
the beings of the six paths,
where their births and deaths lead them,
their karmic conditions of good and evil,
the beauty and ugliness of the retributions they receive,
all this is completely seen here.
Also, we behold all the Buddhas,
the Holy Lords, the Lions,
expounding the sūtras,
subtle and unsurpassed.
Their voices are pure and clear,
emitting gentle and soft sounds,
teaching the Bodhisattvas,
countless billions,
their Brahma-sounds deep and wondrous,
causing people to delight in hearing them.
In each of their respective worlds,
they expound the Correct Dharma, with various causes and conditions.
With immeasurable metaphors, they illuminate the Buddha-Dharma,
enlightening sentient beings.
If people encounter suffering, detesting old age, sickness, and death,
for them, they expound nirvāṇa, the end of all suffering.
If people have blessings,
having previously made offerings to Buddhas,
aspiring to seek the supreme Dharma,
for them, they expound Pratyekabuddhahood.
If there are Buddha-sons,
cultivating various practices,
seeking unsurpassed wisdom,
for them, they expound the Pure Path.
Wénshūshīlì!
I, dwelling here,
see and hear such things, and thousands of billions of other things,
so many,
that I shall now briefly speak of them."
I saw in that land,
*héng shā* Bodhisattvas,
using various causes and conditions,
to seek the Buddha-way.
Some practice giving,
gold, silver, coral,
pearls, *mó ní*,
*chē qú*, agate,
diamonds, and various treasures,
servants, vehicles,
jeweled ornaments, and palanquins,
joyfully giving them away.
They dedicate the merit to the Buddha-way,
wishing to obtain this vehicle,
the foremost in the triple world,
praised by all the Buddhas.
Some Bodhisattvas,
give away four-horse jeweled carriages,
with railings, flower canopies,
and adorned finials.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
giving away their own flesh, hands, and feet,
as well as wives and children,
seeking the unsurpassed way.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
gladly giving away their heads, eyes, and bodies,
seeking the wisdom of the Buddha.
*Wénshūshīlì*!
I saw various kings, going to the Buddha's place,
asking about the unsurpassed way,
then abandoning their pleasant lands, palaces, and concubines,
shaving off their beards and hair,
and donning the Dharma robes.
Some saw Bodhisattvas, acting as *bǐqiū*,
dwelling alone in quiet places,
delighting in reciting scriptures.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas, brave and diligent,
entering deep mountains,
contemplating the Buddha-way.
Again, some have abandoned desire,
constantly dwelling in emptiness and leisure,
deeply cultivating *chán* concentration,
attaining the five supernormal powers.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
sitting in *chán*, joining their palms,
using thousands of verses,
to praise the Dharma Kings.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
profound in wisdom and firm in resolve,
able to question all the Buddhas,
hearing and receiving everything.
Again, I saw Buddha-sons,
complete with *dìng* and *huì*,
using boundless metaphors,
to speak the Dharma for the masses.
Joyfully speaking the Dharma,
transforming all Bodhisattvas,
breaking the demon armies,
and striking the Dharma drum.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
silent and at ease,
respected by *tiān* and *lóng*,
not taking it as a joy.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
emitting light in the forests,
saving those suffering in hell,
causing them to enter the Buddha-way.
Again, I saw Buddha-sons,
never sleeping,
walking in the forests,
diligently seeking the Buddha-way.
Again, I saw those upholding the precepts,
with flawless deportment,
pure like a precious pearl,
seeking the Buddha-way.
Again, I saw Buddha-sons,
abiding in the power of patience,
arrogant people, cursing and beating them,
all of which they could endure,
seeking the Buddha-way.
Again, I saw Bodhisattvas,
apart from all play and laughter,
and foolish relatives,
drawing near to the wise,
wholeheartedly eliminating disturbances,
collecting their thoughts in the mountains and forests,
for hundreds of millions of years,
seeking the Buddha-way.
Some saw Bodhisattvas, offering delicious food and drink, hundreds of kinds of soups and medicines,
to the Buddha and the *sēng*.
Famous clothes and fine garments, worth tens of millions,
or priceless garments,
offered to the Buddha and the *sēng*.
Hundreds of millions of kinds of *zhāntán* treasure houses,
wonderful bedding,
offered to the Buddha and the *sēng*.
Pure gardens and forests,
with flourishing flowers and fruits, flowing springs and bathing ponds,
offered to the Buddha and the *sēng*.
Such offerings, various and subtle,
joyfully without weariness,
seeking the unsurpassed way.
Some Bodhisattvas,
speak the Dharma of quiet extinction,
teaching and instructing in various ways, countless sentient beings.
Some saw Bodhisattvas,
contemplating the nature of all *fǎ*,
like empty space.
Without two forms,
again I saw Buddha-sons,
with minds unattached,
using this wonderful wisdom,
seeking the unsurpassed way.
*Wénshūshīlì*!
Again, there are Bodhisattvas,
after the Buddha's extinction,
making offerings to the *shèlì*.
Again, I saw Buddha-sons,
building various pagodas and temples,
as numerous as *héng shā*,
adorning the lands,
the treasure pagodas were tall and exquisite,
five thousand *yóuxún* in height,
with length and width equal,
two thousand *yóuxún*.
Each pagoda and temple,
had a thousand banners and streamers,
pearl-interlaced, dew-drenched canopies,
and jeweled bells chiming harmoniously.
All *tiān*, *lóng*, gods,
humans, and non-humans,
with incense, flowers, music and dance,
constantly made offerings.
*Wénshūshīlì*!
All the Buddha-sons and others,
for the sake of offering to the *shèlì*,
adorning the pagodas and temples,
the lands naturally,
became especially wonderful,
like the *tiān* tree king,
its flowers blooming.
The Buddha emitted a ray of light,
I and the assembly,
saw this land,
with its various wonderful features.
The Buddhas' divine power,
and wisdom are rare and wonderful,
emitting a pure light,
illuminating immeasurable lands.
We saw this,
and gained what we had never had before.
Buddha-son *Wénshū*!
May you resolve the doubts of the assembly.
The four assemblies admire and look up to,
you and me.
Why does the World-Honored One,
emit this light?
Buddha-son, answer at this time,
resolve our doubts and make us happy.
What benefit is there,
in emitting this light?
The Buddha sits at the *dàochǎng*, the wonderful Dharma attained, is He about to speak of this?
Or is He about to bestow a prediction?
To show all the Buddha-lands,
adorned with various treasures and purity,
and to see all the Buddhas,
this is no small matter.
*Wénshū*, you should know,
the four assemblies, *lóng* and gods,
are gazing at you,
to hear what you will say.
At that time, *Wénshūshīlì* spoke to *Mílè* Bodhisattva-Mahasattva and all the great beings,
virtuous men, and others: "As I contemplate, today the Buddha-World Honored One
intends to speak the Great Dharma,
rain the Great Dharma rain,
blow the Great Dharma conch,
strike the Great Dharma drum,
expound the Great Dharma meaning.
All virtuous men!
In the past, I have seen such an auspicious sign with all the Buddhas;
after emitting such light, they then spoke the Great Dharma. After emitting such light, they then spoke the Great Dharma.
Therefore, you should know,
the Buddha emitting light now is also like this,
wishing to enable sentient beings to hear and know the Dharma that is difficult to believe in all the worlds,
therefore, He manifests this auspicious sign.
"All virtuous men!
As in the past, immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable *ā sēng qí* kalpas ago,
at that time there was a Buddha,
named *Rìyuè Dēngmíng Rúlái*,
Worthy of Offerings, Universally Aware,
Perfect in Conduct and Understanding, Well-Gone, Understanding of the World, Unsurpassed One,
Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Men, Buddha, World-Honored One,
expounding the Proper Dharma,
good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end,
its meaning profound and far-reaching,
its language skillful,
pure and unmixed,
possessing the marks of pure and white Brahma-conduct.
For those seeking *shēngwén*,
he spoke the Four Noble Truths,
delivering them from birth, old age, sickness, and death, ultimately reaching *nièpán*;
for those seeking *pìzhīfó*,
he spoke the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination;
for all *púsà*,
he spoke the Six *bōluómì*,
enabling them to attain *ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí*, achieving complete omniscience.
"Furthermore, there was a Buddha
also named Rìyuè Dēngmíng;
furthermore, there was a Buddha
also named Rìyuè Dēngmíng.
Thus, twenty thousand Buddhas
all shared the same name,
named Rìyuè Dēngmíng,
and also shared the same surname,
surnamed Pōluóduò.
Mílè, you should know

how much less a Three Vehicle.
Shèlìfú!
The Buddhas appear in the evil world of the Five Turbidities,
namely, the turbidity of the *kalpa*, the turbidity of afflictions, the turbidity of sentient beings, the turbidity of views, and the turbidity of life.
Thus, Shèlìfú!
In times of the turbidity of the *kalpa*,
the defilements of sentient beings are heavy,
they are stingy and jealous, and accomplish all kinds of unwholesome roots;
therefore, the Buddhas use the power of expedient means
to differentiate and speak of the Three Vehicles within the One Buddha Vehicle.
Shèlìfú!
If my disciples claim to be Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas,
and do not hear or know that the Buddhas and Tathāgatas only teach and transform Bodhisattvas,
they are not disciples of the Buddha,
nor are they Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas.
"Furthermore, Shèlìfú!
Those *bhikṣus* and *bhikṣunīs*
who claim to have attained Arhatship,
that this is their last body, and that they will ultimately attain *nirvāṇa*,
and therefore no longer aspire to Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi,
know that all such people are arrogant.
Why is this?
If there are *bhikṣus* who have truly attained Arhatship,
it is impossible for them not to believe in this Dharma.
Except after the Buddha's extinction, when there is no Buddha present.
Why is this?
After the Buddha's extinction,
it is difficult to find people who can receive, uphold, read, recite, and understand the meaning of such sūtras.
If they encounter another Buddha,
they will be able to resolve this Dharma.
Shèlìfú!
You should wholeheartedly believe, understand, receive, and uphold the Buddha's words.
The words of the Buddhas and Tathāgatas are not false;
there is no other vehicle, only the One Buddha Vehicle."
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
*Bhikṣus* and *bhikṣunīs*,
who harbor arrogance,
*Upāsakas* who are proud,
*Upāsikās* who do not believe,
Such four assemblies,
Their number is five thousand,
Not seeing their own faults,
Having deficiencies in precepts,
Protecting their blemishes.
These of small wisdom have left,
The dregs and chaff of the assembly,
Due to the Buddha's majestic virtue, they departed,
These people have little merit,
Not capable of receiving this Dharma.
This assembly has no branches and leaves,
Only those who are pure and true.
Shèlìfú, listen carefully!
The Dharma attained by the Buddhas,
With immeasurable expedient power,
Is spoken for sentient beings.
Sentient beings' thoughts,
Various paths they practice,
Different desires and natures,
Good and evil deeds of past lives.
The Buddha knows all this,
With various causes, parables,
Eloquent words, and expedient power,
Causing all to rejoice.
Sometimes speaking of *sūtras*,
*Gāthās* and past events,
Birth stories, unprecedented things,
Also speaking of causes and conditions,
Parables, and *Geyas*,
*Upadeśa* sūtras.
Those of dull faculties delight in small Dharmas,
Grasping at birth and death,
Toward countless Buddhas,
Not practicing the profound and wonderful path,
Troubled and disturbed by various sufferings,
For them, *nirvāṇa* is spoken.
I establish these expedient means,
To enable them to enter the Buddha's wisdom,
I have never said to you,
That you will attain Buddhahood.
The reason I have not spoken of it,
Is because the time had not yet come,
Now is the right time,
To definitely speak of the Great Vehicle.
These nine divisions of Dharma of mine,
Are spoken in accordance with sentient beings,
Entering the Great Vehicle is the basis,
Therefore, this sūtra is spoken.
Those sons of the Buddha with pure hearts,
Gentle and with sharp faculties,
In the presence of countless Buddhas,
Practice the profound and wonderful path.
For these sons of the Buddha,
This Great Vehicle sūtra is spoken,
I predict that such people,
In the future will attain Buddhahood,
With deep minds contemplating the Buddha,
Practicing and upholding pure precepts.
These, hearing they will attain Buddhahood,
Are filled with great joy throughout their bodies,
The Buddha knows their thoughts and actions,
Therefore, the Great Vehicle is spoken for them.
Whether *śrāvakas* or Bodhisattvas,
Hearing the Dharma I speak,
Even a single verse,
Will undoubtedly attain Buddhahood.
Within the Buddha lands of the ten directions,
there is only the One Vehicle Dharma,
neither two nor three.
Except for the Buddha’s expedient teachings,
using only provisional names
to guide sentient beings,
therefore, the Buddhas appear in the world
to speak of the Buddha's wisdom.
Only this one fact is real;
the other two are not true.
Ultimately, I will not use the Small Vehicle
to deliver sentient beings.
The Buddha himself abides in the Great Vehicle,
according to the Dharma he has attained,
adorned with the power of *dìng* (concentration) and *huì* (wisdom),
using this to deliver sentient beings.
Having personally realized the unsurpassed Way,
the Great Vehicle is the Dharma of equality.
If I were to transform even one person
with the Small Vehicle,
then I would be falling into stinginess and greed.
This would be impossible.
If people believe and take refuge in the Buddha,
the *Rúlái* (Tathāgata) does not deceive,
and has no intention of greed or jealousy,
cutting off evil from within all dharmas.
Therefore, the Buddha in the ten directions
is uniquely without fear.
I adorn myself with marks,
and my light illuminates the world.
Honored by countless beings,
I speak of the seal of true reality.
*Shèlìfú*, you should know
that I originally made a vow
to cause all beings
to be no different from me.
As I wished in the past,
now it is fulfilled;
I transform all sentient beings,
causing them all to enter the Buddha Way.
If I encounter sentient beings,
I will teach them all the Buddha Way.
But the unwise become confused,
deluded and not receptive to teachings.
I know these sentient beings have never cultivated roots of goodness;
they are firmly attached to the five desires,
and suffering arises from foolish love.
Through the causes and conditions of various desires,
they fall into the three evil paths,
revolving in the six realms,
fully experiencing all kinds of bitter poisons.
From the minuscule form of conception,
they constantly grow in every lifetime.
People of little virtue and scant blessings
are oppressed by all kinds of suffering,
entering the dense forest of deviant views,
such as existence and non-existence.
Relying on these views,
they are complete with sixty-two,
deeply attached to false and illusory dharmas,
firmly holding onto them, unwilling to relinquish them.
Arrogant and conceited,
deceitful and insincere in heart,
for millions and billions of *jié* (kalpas),
they do not hear the name of the Buddha,
nor do they hear the Proper Dharma.
Such people are difficult to deliver.
Therefore, *Shèlìfú*!
I establish expedient means,
speaking of the path to the exhaustion of suffering,
showing them *nièpán* (nirvana).
Although I speak of *nièpán* (nirvana),
it is also not true extinction.
All dharmas from the beginning
constantly have the characteristic of quiescence and extinction.
When Buddha's children have practiced the Way,
in the future, they will become Buddhas.
I have the power of expedient means
to reveal and teach the Three Vehicles Dharma.
All the World Honored Ones
speak of the One Vehicle Way.
Now, all of you in this great assembly
should dispel your doubts.
The words of the Buddhas are not different;
there is only one, not two Vehicles.
In the countless past *jié* (kalpas),
immeasurable Buddhas have entered extinction,
hundreds, thousands, millions of kinds,
their numbers beyond measure.
Those World Honored Ones,
through various causes, conditions, and metaphors,
and countless expedient powers,
expounded the characteristics of all dharmas.
Those World Honored Ones,
all spoke of the One Vehicle Dharma,
transforming immeasurable sentient beings,
causing them to enter the Buddha Way.
Moreover, the Great Holy Lords,
knowing the desires of all the world, gods, humans, and sentient beings,
further use different expedient means
to assist in revealing the foremost meaning.
If there are sentient beings
who encounter past Buddhas,
if they hear the Dharma and give alms,
or uphold precepts and practice forbearance,
diligence, meditation, wisdom, etc.,
cultivating various blessings and wisdom.
Such people
have all become Buddhas.
After the Buddhas have entered extinction,
if people are kind and gentle-hearted,
such sentient beings
have all become Buddhas.
After the Buddhas have entered extinction,
those who make offerings to the *shèlì* (śarīra),
erecting billions of kinds of pagodas,
of gold, silver, crystal,
agate, and *mǎnǎo* (carnelian),
rose, *liúlí* (lapis lazuli), and pearl,
pure, vast, and adorned,
decorating all the pagodas.
Or some erect stone temples,
of sandalwood and *chénshuǐ* (aloe wood),
cypress and other materials,
bricks, tiles, mud, earth, etc.
If in the wilderness,
they pile up earth to make a Buddha temple,
even a child at play
piling up sand to make a Buddha pagoda,
such people
have all become Buddhas.
If people for the sake of the Buddha
establish various images,
carving and sculpting various forms,
they have all become Buddhas.
Or made of the seven treasures,
*tōushí* (brass), red and white copper,
pewter and lead,
iron, wood, and clay,
or with glue and lacquer cloth,
adorning and making Buddha images,
such people have all become Buddhas.
Painting Buddha images,
with the marks of a hundred blessings adorning them,
whether doing it themselves or causing others to do it,
they have all become Buddhas.
Even a child at play,
with grass, wood, or a brush,
or with a fingernail,
drawing and making a Buddha image,
such people
gradually accumulate merit and virtue,
complete with great compassion,
they have all become Buddhas.
Only transforming the *púsà* (bodhisattvas),
delivering countless beings.
If people at pagodas, temples,
precious images, and painted images,
with flowers, incense, banners, and canopies, reverently make offerings.
If they cause people to make music,
beating drums, blowing horns and conches,
flutes, *qín* (zithers), *kōnghóu* (harps),
*pípá* (lutes), *náo* (cymbals), and bronze cymbals,
such wonderful sounds,
all used to make offerings.
Or with joyful hearts,
singing praises of the Buddha’s virtues,
even a small sound,
they have all become Buddhas.
If people with scattered minds,
even with a single flower,
make offerings to a painted image,
they will gradually see countless Buddhas.
Or some people bow in worship,
or simply put their palms together,
even raising a single hand,
or slightly lowering their heads,
using this to make offerings to images,
they will gradually see immeasurable Buddhas,
realize the unsurpassed Way themselves,
widely deliver countless beings,
and enter *nièpán* (nirvana) without remainder,
like a fire extinguished when the firewood is exhausted.
If people with scattered minds
enter a pagoda or temple,
and once recite “*Námó Fó*” (Namo Buddha),
they will all become Buddhas.
Regarding all the past Buddhas,
whether they were in the world or have entered extinction,
if anyone hears this Dharma,
they have all become Buddhas.
Future all World-Honored Ones,
their number is immeasurable,
these all Tathāgatas and so on,
also expediently preach the Dharma.
All the Tathāgatas,
with immeasurable expedient means,
deliver all sentient beings,
and cause them to enter the Buddha's undefiled wisdom.
If there are those who hear the Dharma,
there is not one who will not become a Buddha.
All Buddhas' original vows,
the Buddha-path I practice,
universally wishing all sentient beings,
to also attain this path together.
Future world all Buddhas,
although they preach hundreds, thousands, and billions,
countless all Dharma-gates,
in reality it is for the One Vehicle.
All Buddhas, the Two-legged Honored Ones,
know that the Dharma is always without inherent nature,
the Buddha-seed arises from conditions,
therefore they preach the One Vehicle.
This Dharma abides in the Dharma-position,
the world's characteristics constantly abide,
having known this in the Bodhi-Maṇḍa,
the Guide expediently preaches.
Those offered to by gods and humans, the Buddhas of the ten directions in the present,
their number like the sands of the Gaṅgā,
appear in the world,
for the sake of the peace and security of sentient beings,
they also preach such Dharma.
Knowing the foremost quiescence and extinction,
because of the power of expedient means,
although they show various paths,
in reality it is for the Buddha-Vehicle.
Knowing all sentient beings' conduct,
what their deepest hearts contemplate,
the karma they practiced in the past,
their desire-nature, vigor-power,
and the sharpness or dullness of their faculties,
with various causes and conditions,
parables, and also words,
they preach according to what is appropriate.
Now I am also like this,
for the sake of the peace and security of sentient beings,
with various Dharma-gates,
I proclaim and reveal the Buddha-path.
I, with the power of wisdom,
know sentient beings' nature and desires,
expediently preach various Dharmas,
causing them all to obtain joy.
Shèlìfú, you should know!
I, with the Buddha-eye, observe,
seeing sentient beings in the six paths,
poor, without fortune and wisdom,
entering the dangerous path of birth and death,
the succession of suffering unceasing,
deeply attached to the five desires,
like the yak cherishing its tail,
with craving and love they conceal themselves,
blind and unseeing.
Not seeking the Buddha of Great Power,
as well as the Dharma of severing suffering,
deeply entering into various heterodox views,
using suffering-desire to abandon suffering,
for the sake of these sentient beings,
I then arouse great compassion.
I first sat at the Bodhi-Maṇḍa,
contemplating the trees and also walking back and forth,
within three seven-day periods,
contemplating such matters as these,
the wisdom I obtained,
is subtle, wonderful, and foremost.
Sentient beings' faculties are dull,
attached to pleasure, blinded by delusion,
such kinds as these,
how can they be delivered?
At that time, all Brahma Kings,
and all Śakra, Lord of Gods,
the Four Heavenly Kings who protect the world,
and also Mahāśiva,
along with other all heavenly hosts,
retinues of hundreds of thousands and millions,
respectfully joining their palms in reverence,
requested me to turn the Dharma-wheel.
I then thought to myself:
'If I only praise the Buddha-Vehicle,
sentient beings are submerged in suffering,
unable to believe in this Dharma;
because they break the Dharma and do not believe,
they will fall into the three evil paths.
I would rather not preach the Dharma,
and quickly enter into Nirvāṇa.'
Then recalling the Buddhas of the past, the power of expedient means they practiced,
the path I have now attained,
I should also preach the Three Vehicles. '
When this thought arose,
the Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared,
with Brahma-sounds comforting me:
'Excellent, Shìjiāmóuní!
The foremost Guide,
having attained this unsurpassed Dharma,
following all the Buddhas,
and using the power of expedient means.
We have also all attained,
the most wondrous foremost Dharma,
for the sake of all sentient beings,
differentiating and preaching the Three Vehicles.
Those of little wisdom delight in the Small Dharma,
and do not believe that they can become Buddhas,
therefore with expedient means,
we differentiate and preach the various fruits.
Although we preach the Three Vehicles,
it is only for teaching Bodhisattvas. '
Shèlìfú, you should know!
I heard the Holy Lion's,
deep, pure, subtle sound,
joyfully praising Namo Buddha.
Again, I thought thus:
'I have emerged into a turbid, evil world,
as all the Buddhas have preached,
I will also follow and accord.'
Having contemplated this matter,
I then proceeded to Bōluónài.
The characteristic of all Dharmas is quiescent extinction,
which cannot be expressed in words,
with the power of expedient means,
I preached for the five Bhikṣus.
This is called turning the Dharma-wheel,
then there was the sound of Nirvāṇa,
and also Arhats,
names differentiating Dharma and Sangha.
From long distant kalpas in the past,
praising and showing the Dharma of Nirvāṇa,
the suffering of birth and death is forever exhausted,
I have always preached thus.
Shèlìfú, you should know!
I see Buddha-sons and so on,
those whose aspiration is to seek the Buddha-path, immeasurable thousands, millions, and billions,
all with respectful hearts,
all come to the Buddha's place,
having once heard from all the Buddhas,
the Dharma preached with expedient means.
I then had this thought:
'The reason why the Tathāgata appears,
is for the sake of preaching the Buddha-wisdom,
now is precisely the time.'
Shèlìfú, you should know!
Those of dull faculties and little wisdom,
attached to characteristics and arrogant,
are unable to believe in this Dharma.
Now I am joyful and without fear,
among all the Bodhisattvas,
honestly abandoning expedient means,
only preaching the unsurpassed path.
Bodhisattvas who hear this Dharma,
doubts and nets are all already removed,
the twelve hundred Arhats,
will all also become Buddhas.
Like the Buddhas of the three times,
the proper form of preaching the Dharma,
I am now also like this,
preaching the Dharma without differentiation.
The Buddhas' arising in the world,
from afar, encountering them is difficult,
even if they appear in the world,
to preach this Dharma is again difficult.
For immeasurable countless kalpas,
to hear this Dharma is also difficult,
those who can listen to this Dharma,
such people are also again difficult.
It is like the *udumbara* flower,
which all love and delight in,
rare among gods and humans,
only appearing once in a while. Those who hear the Dharma, joyfully praise,
even if they utter just one word,
then it is already considered offering,
to all the Buddhas of the three times,
such people are extremely rare,
more so than the *udumbara* flower.
You all should not have doubts,
I am the Dharma-King of all Dharmas,
universally announcing to all the great assemblies,
only with the One Vehicle Path,
do I teach and transform all Bodhisattvas,
without Śrāvaka disciples.
You all, Śhèlìfú,
Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas,
should know this wondrous Dharma,
The Secret Essentials of all Buddhas.
Because of the five turbid and evil ages,
they only delight in attachment to various desires;
beings such as these
ultimately do not seek the Buddha-way.
In the evil age of the future,
upon hearing the Buddha speak of the One Vehicle,
they are confused and do not believe and accept it,
destroying the Dharma and falling into evil paths.
Those who are ashamed and pure,
and who aspire to the Buddha-way,
for the sake of such as these,
widely praise the One Vehicle path.
Shèlìfú, you should know!
The Dharma of all Buddhas is thus:
using myriad billions of expedient means,
they preach the Dharma according to what is suitable;
those who do not study and learn
cannot understand this.
Since you and others already know
that the Buddhas are the teachers of the world,
and are skilled in expedient means,
there should be no more doubts;
generate great joy in your hearts,
and know that you will become Buddhas."
《Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng》One
《Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng》 Scroll Two
Tripiṭaka Master from the country of Qiūcí in the Later Qín Dynasty,
Jūmóluóshí, respectfully translated by Imperial Decree
At that time, Shèlìfú leapt up with joy,
immediately rose, joined his palms, and gazed up at the Venerable Countenance,
and said to the Buddha:
"Now, having heard this Dharma-sound from the World-Honored One,
my heart is filled with courage and joy, attaining what I never had before.
What is the reason for this?
In the past, I heard such a Dharma from the Buddha,
and saw various Bodhisattvas receive predictions of becoming Buddhas,
but we were not included in these matters,
and I felt deeply grieved, missing out on the immeasurable knowledge and vision of the Tathāgata.
World-Honored One!
I often dwell alone in the mountains and forests, under trees,
whether sitting or walking,
and I always think thus:
'We all enter the Dharma-nature together,
how is it that the Tathāgata uses the Lesser Vehicle Dharma to save and deliver us?
This is our fault, not the World-Honored One's.
What is the reason for this?
If we had awaited the explanation of the causes and conditions for accomplishing Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi,
we would certainly have been delivered by the Great Vehicle.
However, we did not understand the expedient means and teachings given according to what was suitable;
upon first hearing the Buddha's Dharma, we immediately believed, accepted, contemplated, and attained realization.'
World-Honored One!
From the past until now, day and night, I have always reproached myself,
but now, having heard the Dharma that I have never heard before from the Buddha,
I have cut off all doubts and regrets;
my body and mind are at ease, and I have quickly attained peace and tranquility.
Today I know that I am truly a Buddha-son,
born from the Buddha's mouth, born from the transformation of the Dharma,
and have obtained a share of the Buddha's Dharma."
At that time, Shèlìfú
wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
I have heard this Dharma-sound,
and attained what I never had before,
my heart is filled with great joy,
and all doubts have been removed.
In the past, I received the Buddha's teaching,
not missing out on the Great Vehicle;
the Buddha's voice is very rare,
able to remove the afflictions of sentient beings;
I have already attained the exhaustion of outflows,
and hearing this also removes sorrow and affliction.
I dwell in mountain valleys,
or under forest trees;
whether sitting or walking,
I constantly contemplate this matter,
alas, deeply reproaching myself:
how could I deceive myself?
We are also Buddha-sons,
together entering the outflow-less Dharma,
but we were unable in the future
to expound the unsurpassed Way.
The golden thirty-two,
the ten powers and all the liberations,
all within one Dharma,
but I did not attain this;
the eighty minor marks,
the eighteen unshared qualities,
such merits as these,
I have already lost them all.
When I walk alone,
I see the Buddha in the great assembly,
his name is heard throughout the ten directions,
extensively benefiting sentient beings.
Thinking that I have lost this benefit,
I have deceived and deluded myself.
I constantly, day and night,
always contemplate this matter,
wanting to ask the World-Honored One,
whether I have lost it or not?
I often see the World-Honored One
praising the Bodhisattvas;
because of this, day and night,
I ponder such matters.
Now I hear the Buddha's voice,
preaching the Dharma according to what is suitable,
the outflow-less, difficult-to-conceive Dharma,
leading all to the Bodhimaṇḍa.
I was originally attached to wrong views,
being a teacher of various Brahmins;
the World-Honored One knew my mind,
removed my wrong views, and spoke of Nirvāṇa.
I completely eliminated wrong views,
and attained realization in the empty Dharma;
at that time, I thought to myself,
that I had attained extinction;
but now I realize for myself
that it is not true extinction.
If I attain Buddhahood,
possessing the thirty-two marks,
and the multitudes of devas, humans, and Yakshas,
and dragons and deities, etc., respectfully venerate me,
only then can it be said
that I have eternally exhausted and extinguished without remainder.
In the great assembly, the Buddha
said that I will become a Buddha;
hearing such a Dharma-sound,
all doubts and regrets have already been removed.
When I first heard what the Buddha said,
I was greatly astonished and doubtful in my heart,
wondering if a demon had become a Buddha
to disturb my mind?
The Buddha, with various causes,
similes, and skillful words, spoke,
his mind as peaceful as the ocean;
I heard and my net of doubts was cut.
The Buddha spoke of the past,
of immeasurable Buddhas who have passed into extinction,
abiding in expedient means,
they also all preached this Dharma.
The Buddhas of the present and future,
their number is immeasurable;
they also use various expedient means to expound such a Dharma.
Now, the World-Honored One,
from birth and leaving the household,
attaining the Way and turning the Dharma-wheel,
also preaches with expedient means.
The World-Honored One speaks of the true Way;
Māra has no such thing.
Because of this, I am certain
that it is not a demon who has become a Buddha.
Because I was caught in a net of doubts,
I thought it was done by a demon;
hearing the Buddha's gentle voice,
deep, far-reaching, and very subtle,
expounding the pure Dharma,
my heart is greatly joyful,
doubts and regrets have been eternally exhausted,
and I abide in true wisdom.
I will certainly become a Buddha,
revered by devas and humans,
turning the unsurpassed Dharma-wheel,
teaching and transforming various Bodhisattvas."

At that time, the Buddha told Shèlìfú: "Now, in this great assembly of devas, humans, *Śrāmaṇas*, and Brahmins, etc., I say that in the past, in the presence of two hundred million Buddhas, for the sake of the unsurpassed Way, I constantly taught and transformed you, and you also followed me in learning and studying for a long time. Because I skillfully guided you with expedient means, you were born in my Dharma. Shèlìfú! In the past, I taught you to aspire to the Buddha-way, but you have now forgotten everything and claim to have already attained extinction. Now, I want to remind you of the path you originally vowed to follow, and for the sake of the *Śrāvakas*, I am speaking this Great Vehicle Sutra, named the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower, which teaches the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas and is protected and remembered by the Buddhas."
Shèlìfú!
In a future age, after limitless, boundless, inconceivable *kalpas*,
you will make offerings to a great many tens of millions of Buddhas,
uphold and maintain the Right Dharma,
perfect the path practiced by the Bodhisattvas,
and will attain Buddhahood,
named Huāguāng Rúlái, *Arhat*, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadaṃyasārathi, Śāstā Devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat.
The country will be named Lígòu;
its land will be level, pure, adorned,
peaceful, prosperous, and joyful, with flourishing devas and humans.
Lapis lazuli will be the earth, with eight intersecting paths,
and golden ropes will mark the boundaries.
Beside each path will be rows of seven-jeweled trees, always with flowers and fruits.
Huāguāng Rúlái will also teach and transform sentient beings with the Three Vehicles.
Shèlìfú!
When that Buddha appears, although it will not be an evil age,
because of his original vow, he will preach the Three Vehicle Dharma.
The *kalpa* will be named Great Jewel Adornment.
Why is it called Great Jewel Adornment?
Because in that country, the Bodhisattvas are considered the great jewels.
Those Bodhisattvas will be limitless, boundless, inconceivable,
beyond what can be reached by calculation and analogy;
no one can know them except with the Buddha's wisdom.
When they want to walk, jewel flowers will support their feet.
These bodhisattvas were not newly aspiring;
all had long cultivated virtuous roots,
in the presence of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas, purely cultivating Brahma-conduct,
and were constantly praised by all the Buddhas.
They constantly cultivated the Buddha-wisdom, possessed great supernatural powers,
were skilled in knowing the gateways to all dharmas,
were honest and without falsehood, and their will and mindfulness were firm and steadfast.
Such bodhisattvas filled that land.
Shèlìfú!
The lifespan of Buddha Huāguāng was twelve small kalpas,
excluding the time when he was a prince and had not yet become a Buddha.
The lifespan of the people in that land was eight small kalpas.
After twelve small kalpas, Huāguāng Tathāgata
bestowed the prediction of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi upon Bodhisattva Jiānmǎn.
He told the bhikshus:
"This Bodhisattva Jiānmǎn will be the next to become a Buddha,
named Huázú Ānxíng, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-Saṃbuddha.
His Buddha-land will also be like this."
"Shèlìfú!
After the Parinirvāṇa of this Buddha Huāguāng,
the True Dharma will abide in the world for thirty-two small kalpas,
and the Semblance Dharma will also abide in the world for thirty-two small kalpas."
At that time, the World-Honored One,
desiring to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
Shèlìfú in a future life,
will become a Buddha, universally wise and honored,
named Huāguāng,
and will liberate immeasurable beings.
He will make offerings to countless Buddhas,
fully practicing the bodhisattva conduct,
perfecting the ten powers and other merits,
and attain the unsurpassed Path.
After immeasurable kalpas have passed,
the kalpa will be named Great Treasure Adornment,
the world will be named Free from Filth,
pure and without blemishes.
It will be paved with lapis lazuli,
with golden ropes marking the paths,
and trees of seven treasures with various colors,
will constantly bear flowers, fruits, and seeds.
The bodhisattvas of that land,
their will and mindfulness are always steadfast,
and the supernatural power pāramitās,
are all fully possessed.
In the presence of countless Buddhas,
they have well learned the bodhisattva path,
such great beings as these,
are transformed by Buddha Huāguāng.
When the Buddha was a prince,
he abandoned the kingdom and worldly glory,
and in his very last life,
he renounced home life and attained Buddhahood.
Buddha Huāguāng abided in the world,
for twelve small kalpas,
and the population of that land,
had a lifespan of eight small kalpas.
After the Buddha's Parinirvāṇa,
the True Dharma abided in the world,
for thirty-two small kalpas,
extensively liberating all beings.
After the True Dharma has perished,
the Semblance Dharma will last for thirty-two,
and the relics will widely spread,
receiving offerings from gods and humans everywhere.
The deeds of Buddha Huāguāng,
all these things will be just like this,
that two-legged honored one,
is supremely victorious and without equal.
That is you yourself,
you should rejoice and celebrate.
At that time, the fourfold assembly,
bhikshus, bhikshunis, upāsakas, upāsikās,
and the great assemblies of gods, nāgas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, etc.,
seeing Shèlìfú receiving the prediction of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi in the Buddha's presence,
were greatly joyful and danced immeasurably,
each taking off their upper garments,
to offer to the Buddha.
Shì Tí Huán Yīn, Brahma Kings, etc.,
with countless devaputras,
also used celestial fine garments, celestial *mandārava* flowers, *mahāmandārava* flowers, etc.,
to make offerings to the Buddha—
the scattered celestial garments remained in empty space,
and spun around by themselves;
hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of celestial musical instruments,
played together in empty space at the same time,
raining down multitudes of celestial flowers— and spoke these words:
"In the past, the Buddha first turned the Dharma wheel in Bōluónèi,
now he turns again the unsurpassed and greatest Dharma wheel."
At that time, the devaputras,
desiring to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
In the past in Bōluónèi,
you turned the four noble truths Dharma wheel,
separately explaining all dharmas,
the arising and ceasing of the five aggregates.
Now you turn again the most wonderful,
unsurpassed great Dharma wheel,
this Dharma is extremely profound and subtle,
few are able to believe it.
We, from long ago,
have frequently heard the World-Honored One speak,
but have never heard such, deeply wondrous unsurpassed Dharma.
The World-Honored One speaks this Dharma,
and we all rejoice accordingly.
The greatly wise Shèlìfú,
now receives the honored prediction,
we also, just like this,
will certainly attain Buddhahood.
In all the worlds,
the most honored, there is no higher,
the Buddha path is inconceivable,
expediently and appropriately taught.
All the meritorious deeds that I have,
in this life, or past lives,
and seeing the Buddha's merits,
I completely dedicate towards the Buddha Path.
At that time, Shèlìfú said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
I now have no more doubts or regrets,
and have personally received the prediction of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi in the Buddha's presence.
These twelve hundred and fifty who have mastery over their minds,
formerly dwelled in the stage of learners,
and the Buddha constantly taught them, saying:
'My Dharma can depart from birth, old age, sickness, and death, ultimately reaching Nirvāṇa.'
These learners and non-learners,
each with their own views of departing from self-views and views of being and non-being, etc.,
thought they had attained Nirvāṇa;
but now, in the presence of the World-Honored One, hearing what they have never heard before, they all fall into doubt.
Excellent, World-Honored One!
May you, for the sake of the fourfold assembly, explain the causes and conditions, causing them to depart from doubt and regret."
At that time, the Buddha told Shèlìfú:
Did I not say before: 'All the Buddha World-Honored Ones
use various causes and conditions, parables, and skillful means of language to teach the Dharma,
all for the sake of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi?'
All these teachings are for the sake of transforming bodhisattvas.
Yet, Shèlìfú!
Now I will again use a parable to further clarify this meaning,
for those with wisdom can understand through parables.
Shèlìfú!
If in a country, town, or village, there is a great elder,
who is old and frail, with immeasurable wealth,
possessing many fields, houses, and servants.
His house is vast and spacious,
with only one gate,
and many people,
one hundred, two hundred, or even five hundred people,
living within it.
The halls and pavilions are dilapidated, the walls are crumbling,
the pillars are decayed at the roots, the beams are tilting and dangerous,
and suddenly, at the same time, a fire breaks out all around, burning the house.
The elder's sons,
perhaps ten, twenty, or even thirty,
are in this house.
The elder, seeing this great fire arising from all four sides,
is greatly alarmed and thinks to himself:
'Although I can safely escape from this burning gate,
my sons, within the burning house, are fond of playing and enjoying themselves,
unaware and unknowing, neither alarmed nor afraid,
the fire approaches their bodies, the pain is intensely personal,
but their minds are not weary of it, and they have no intention of seeking to leave.'
Shèlìfú!
This elder thinks to himself:
'I have strength in my arms and hands,
I should use a garment or a table to carry them out of the house.'
He further considers:
'This house has only one gate,
and it is also narrow and small.
My sons are young and inexperienced,
attached to their play areas,
and may fall and be burned by the fire.
I should tell them about the terrifying nature of this situation,
that this house is already burning, and they should quickly leave at once,
lest they be burned and harmed by the fire.'
Having made this decision,
as he had thought, he fully informs his sons,
'You must quickly leave!'
Although the father is compassionate and gently coaxes and persuades them,
the sons, fond of playing and enjoying themselves, are unwilling to believe and accept,
are neither alarmed nor afraid, and have no intention of leaving;
and also do not know what is fire? What is the house?
What is loss?
They only run around playing, looking at their father.
At that time, the elder thinks to himself:
'This house is already being burned by a great fire,
and if I and my sons do not leave immediately,
we will certainly be consumed by it.
I must now devise a skillful means to enable my sons to escape this harm.'
The father knew that his sons each had different preferences for various precious and wondrous objects, and they would surely be delighted by them,
so he told them:
"The things you like to play with are rare and hard to obtain.
If you don't take them, you will surely regret it later.
All kinds of sheep carts, deer carts, and ox carts are now outside the gate, for you to play with."
You should quickly come out of this burning house.
Whatever you want, I will give it to you."
At that time, the sons heard their father's description
of the precious objects, which suited their desires,
so their hearts were filled with courage, and they pushed and shoved each other,
rushing to get out of the burning house.
At that time, the elder
saw that all his sons had safely come out
and were sitting in an open space at the crossroads,
without any obstacles.
His heart was peaceful, and he rejoiced with great joy.
Then the sons said to their father:
"Father, the playthings that you promised,
the sheep carts, deer carts, and ox carts, we hope you will give them to us now."
Shèlìfú!
At that time, the elder gave each of his sons a large cart,
which was tall and wide, decorated with many jewels,
surrounded by railings, and hung with bells on all four sides.
Moreover, on top of it was stretched a canopy,
also adorned with rare and precious jewels,
with jeweled ropes intertwined and hanging flower tassels,
with layers of soft cushions and embroidered pillows placed inside.
It was drawn by white oxen,
whose skin was pure and clean, whose bodies were beautiful and strong, with great strength,
walking steadily and smoothly, as swift as the wind,
and attended by many servants.
Why is this so?
Because this great elder had immeasurable wealth,
and all kinds of treasures were filled to overflowing,
and he thought to himself:
"My wealth is boundless.
I should not give inferior small carts to my sons.
These young children are all my sons,
and my love for them is impartial.
I have such seven-jeweled great carts, countless in number,
and I should give them to each of them equally,
without discrimination. Why is this so?
Because what I have is enough to supply a whole country
and still not be exhausted,
let alone my sons!"
At that time, the sons each rode in a great cart, which was something they had never had before
and had not expected.
"Shèlìfú!
What do you think?
Did this elder deceive his sons by giving them precious great carts?"
Shèlìfú said:
"No, World Honored One!
This elder only wanted his sons to escape the fire,
preserving their lives, so it was not a deception.
Why?
If they preserve their lives,
it is as if they have already obtained playthings,
all the more so if he uses expedient means to rescue them from the burning house.
World Honored One!
If this elder did not even give them the smallest cart,
it would still not be a deception.
Why?
Because the elder first intended:
'I will use expedient means to get my sons out.'
Because of this reason, there is no deception.
All the more so when the elder knows that his wealth is boundless and wants to benefit his sons by giving them all great carts."
The Buddha told Shèlìfú:
"Excellent, excellent!
As you say.
Shèlìfú!
The Thus Come One is also like this,
being the father of all beings in the world.
From all fears, decline, worries, ignorance, and darkness,
eternally exhausted without remainder,
and completely accomplished with immeasurable knowledge, vision, power, and fearlessness,
having great divine power and the power of wisdom,
fully endowed with expedient means and the Perfection of Wisdom,
with great kindness and great compassion, constantly without weariness,
always seeking good deeds, benefiting all,
and being born in the decaying, burning house of the Triple World,
to liberate sentient beings from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, suffering, ignorance, darkness, and the fire of the three poisons,
teaching them to attain Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
Seeing sentient beings being consumed by birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, and suffering,
and also suffering various kinds of suffering because of the wealth and benefit of the five desires;
also because of craving and pursuit, they presently suffer all kinds of suffering,
and later they will suffer the suffering of hells, animals, and hungry ghosts;
if they are born in the heavens or in the human realm,
they suffer from poverty and hardship, the suffering of separation from loved ones, and the suffering of encountering enemies,
and so on, all kinds of suffering.
Sentient beings are submerged in it,
rejoicing and playing,
unaware, unknowing, not surprised, not afraid,
and not developing aversion or seeking liberation.
In this burning house of the Triple World, they run east and west,
and although they encounter great suffering, they do not consider it a problem.
Shèlìfú!
Seeing this, the Buddha then thought:
'I am the father of all sentient beings.
I should rescue them from suffering and difficulty,
and give them immeasurable and boundless Buddha wisdom and joy,
so that they may play in it.'
Shèlìfú!
The Thus Come One further thought:
'If I only rely on divine power and the power of wisdom,
abandoning expedient means,
and praise the Thus Come One's knowledge, vision, power, and fearlessness to all sentient beings,
sentient beings will not be able to attain liberation through this. Why is this so?
These sentient beings have not escaped birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, and suffering,
and are being burned by the burning house of the Triple World;
how can they understand the wisdom of the Buddha?'
Shèlìfú!
Like that elder,
although he has strong arms and hands, he does not use them,
but only uses diligent expedient means
to earnestly rescue his sons from the burning house,
and then gives them each precious great carts.
The Thus Come One is also like this,
although having power and fearlessness,
he does not use them,
but only uses wisdom and expedient means to rescue sentient beings from the burning house of the Triple World,
explaining the Three Vehicles—the Śrāvakayāna, the Pratyekabuddhayāna, and the Buddhayāna—
and saying:
'You should not delight in dwelling in the burning house of the Triple World.
Do not be greedy for the coarse and base forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tactile sensations.
If you cling to them and generate love, you will be burned.
Quickly escape the Triple World,
and you will attain the Three Vehicles—the Śrāvakayāna, the Pratyekabuddhayāna, and the Buddhayāna.
I now guarantee this matter for you,
and it will never be in vain.
You should only diligently cultivate and advance.'
The Thus Come One uses these expedient means to encourage and advance sentient beings,
and further says:
'You should know
that these Three Vehicle teachings are all praised by the sages,
free, unattached, and without reliance or seeking.
Riding these Three Vehicles,
with the undefiled roots, powers, factors of enlightenment, paths, dhyāna, liberation, samādhi, etc.,
you can entertain yourselves,
and then attain immeasurable peace and happiness.'
Shèlìfú!
If there are sentient beings who have innate wisdom,
hear the Dharma from the Buddha, the World Honored One, believe and accept it,
and diligently advance, desiring to quickly escape the Triple World,
seeking Nirvāṇa for themselves,
this is called the Śrāvakayāna,
like those sons who sought the sheep cart to escape the burning house;
if there are sentient beings
who hear the Dharma from the Buddha, the World Honored One, believe and accept it,
and diligently advance, seeking natural wisdom,
delighting in solitude and tranquility,
deeply understanding the conditions of all dharmas,
this is called the Pratyekabuddhayāna,
like those sons who sought the deer cart to escape the burning house;
if there are sentient beings
who hear the Dharma from the Buddha, the World Honored One, believe and accept it,
and diligently cultivate and advance,
seeking all-knowing wisdom, Buddha wisdom, natural wisdom, teacherless wisdom, the Thus Come One's knowledge, vision, power, and fearlessness,
having compassion and bringing peace and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings,
benefiting gods and humans, liberating all,
this is called the Mahāyāna,
and because Bodhisattvas seek this vehicle, they are called Mahāsattvas,
like those sons who sought the ox cart to escape the burning house.
Shèlìfú!
Like that elder, seeing that his sons had safely escaped the burning house and reached a place of fearlessness,
and reflecting that his wealth was immeasurable, he equally gave great carts to all his sons.
The Thus Come One is also like this,
being the father of all sentient beings.

If he sees immeasurable millions of billions of sentient beings, through the Buddha's teachings, escape the suffering of the Triple World, the fearful and dangerous paths, and attain the joy of Nirvāṇa,
"Then the Thus Come One will think:
'I have immeasurable and boundless wisdom, power, fearlessness, and other Buddha Dharma treasures.
These sentient beings are all my sons.
I will equally give them the Mahāyāna,
not allowing anyone to attain extinction alone,
but all attaining extinction through the Thus Come One's extinction.'
These sentient beings who have escaped the Triple World
will all be given the means of entertainment of the Buddhas' dhyāna, liberation, etc.,
all being of one form, one kind, praised by the sages,
capable of generating pure, wonderful, and supreme joy.
Shèlìfú! Like that elder, he first used the three carts to entice and guide his sons,
and then only gave them great carts, adorned with precious objects, safe, secure, and supreme;
yet that elder had no fault of deception.
The Thus Come One is also like this,
without any deception,
first explaining the Three Vehicles to guide sentient beings,
and then only liberating them with the Mahāyāna.
Why is this so?
Because the Thus Come One has immeasurable wisdom, power, fearlessness, and treasures of all Dharmas,
capable of giving the Dharma of the Mahāyāna to all sentient beings,
but they are not all able to receive it completely.
"Shèlìfú!
Because of this reason,
you should know that through the power of the Buddhas' expedient means,
in one Buddha Vehicle, they separately explain the three."
The Buddha, desiring to restate this meaning,
spoke the following verses:
For example, an elder
has a large house,
which is old and dilapidated,
and moreover, extremely decayed.
The halls and houses are dangerously high,
the pillar roots are crumbling and rotten,
the beams and rafters are leaning,
the foundations and steps are collapsing,
the walls are crumbling and cracking,
the mud plaster is peeling off,
the thatched roof is falling in disarray,
the rafters and purlins are misaligned,
the surrounding barriers are crooked,
and all is filled with filth and impurity.
living within.
Owls, vultures, eagles,
crows, magpies, doves, and pigeons,
salamanders, venomous snakes, scorpions,
centipedes, millipedes,
geckos, house centipedes,
apes, civets, and mice,
all sorts of vile creatures
crisscross and run about.
Excrement and urine stink,
impurities overflow,
dung beetles and other insects
gather on it.
chew and trample,
gnawing on dead corpses,
bones and flesh scattered about.
Because of this, packs of dogs
compete to seize and snatch,
starving, emaciated, and panicked,
seeking food everywhere.
They fight and snap,
growling and barking,
making the house terrifying,
in such a state of decay.
Everywhere there are
*chīmèi wǎngliǎng*,
*yèchā* ogres,
eating human flesh.
Various kinds of venomous insects,
all sorts of vile birds and beasts,
conceive and give birth,
each hiding and protecting their own.
*Yèchā* compete to come
and snatch them to eat.
Having eaten their fill,
their evil intentions grow stronger,
the sounds of fighting
are truly terrifying.
*Jiūpántú*＝*chá*
ghost,
squats on a mound of earth,
or sometimes leaves the ground,
one or two *chǐ*,
wandering back and forth,
freely frolicking,
seizing dogs by their hind legs,
slamming them to the ground until they lose their voices,
pressing their feet on their necks,
enjoying scaring the dogs.
their bodies tall and large,
naked, black, and thin,
constantly dwelling within,
emitting loud, evil sounds,
shouting and begging for food.
Again there are ghosts,
their throats like needles.
Again there are ghosts,
their heads like ox heads,
sometimes eating human flesh,
or again devouring dogs,
their hair disheveled and messy,
destructive, fierce, and dangerous,
driven by hunger and thirst,
shouting and running about.
*Yèchā*, hungry ghosts,
all sorts of vile birds and beasts,
hungry and desperate, looking in all directions,
peering through windows.
Such are the numerous calamities,
immeasurable fears.
This decayed old house
belongs to one person.
The person went out nearby,
not long ago.
Afterwards, in the house,
suddenly a fire started,
on all four sides at once,
Beams, rafters, and pillars
burst and crack with loud noises,
collapsing and falling,
the walls crumbling down.
All the ghosts and spirits
raised their voices and cried out.
Eagles, vultures, and other birds,
*jiūpántú* and others,
*zhōuzhāng*＝*zhāngzhāng* terrified and panicked,
unable to escape.
Vile beasts and venomous insects
hid and scurried into holes.
*Píshěshé* ghosts
also lived within,
but due to their meager blessings and virtues,
they were pressed by the fire,
and harmed each other,
drinking blood and devouring flesh.
Jackals and the like
had already died earlier,
and all the great vile beasts
competed to eat and devour them,
foul smoke billowing everywhere,
filling all four sides.
Centipedes, millipedes,
and types of venomous snakes
were burned by the fire,
struggling to crawl out of their holes,
and *jiūpántú* ghosts
seized them and ate them.
Again, all the hungry ghosts
had flames burning on their heads,
suffering from hunger, thirst, and heat,
running about in confusion.
Such was the house,
exceedingly terrifying,
with poisonous harms and fire disasters,
countless calamities.
At this time, the householder
stood outside the gate,
and heard someone say:
"Your children
first came into this house for fun,
and being young and ignorant,
they enjoy themselves and are attached to it."
Having heard this, the elder
was startled and entered the burning house,
trying to rescue them,
lest they be burned.
He warned his children,
telling them of the various calamities,
vile ghosts, venomous insects,
the spreading fire,
the succession of sufferings,
continuing without end.
Venomous snakes, salamanders,
and all the *yèchā*,
*jiūpántú* ghosts,
jackals, foxes, dogs,
eagles, vultures, owls,
and all sorts of centipedes,
driven by hunger, thirst, and vexation,
are exceedingly terrifying.
This is a place of suffering and difficulty,
not to mention the great fire.
The children were ignorant,
and though they heard their father's instructions,
they still enjoyed themselves,
and did not stop playing.
At this time, the elder
thought to himself:
"These children are only
increasing my sorrow and vexation.
Now this house
has nothing enjoyable,
yet these children
are immersed in play,
and do not heed my teachings,
and will be harmed by the fire."
Then he pondered
and devised various expedient means,
and told his children:
"I have all sorts of
precious and playful things,
wonderful jeweled carts,
sheep carts, deer carts,
and great ox carts,
now outside the gate.
You all come out,
and I will create these carts for you,
so you can play as you please,
and have fun."
Hearing about these
various carts, the children
immediately rushed and raced,
running out
to an open space,
away from all suffering and difficulty.
The elder saw his children
emerge from the burning house
and stay at the crossroads.
He sat on a lion throne
and celebrated, saying:
"I am happy now!
These children,
their birth and rearing were very difficult,
they were foolish and ignorant,
and entered a perilous house.
There were many poisonous insects,
and terrifying Chīmèi,
and a great, fierce fire,
rising on all four sides.
But these children
were greedy for pleasure and play.
I have already saved them,
causing them to escape the difficulty.
Therefore, everyone,
I am happy now."
At that time, the children,
knowing that their father was sitting peacefully,
all went to where their father was,
and said to their father:
"We wish you would grant us
the three kinds of jeweled carriages,
as you promised before:
'When the children come out,
I will give them three carriages,
according to their desires.'
Now is the right time,
we only ask that you give them to us."
The elder was very wealthy,
with many treasures in his storehouses,
gold, silver, lapis lazuli,
carriage ornaments, agate –
with many precious things,
he made many great carriages.
He adorned and decorated them,
with railings all around,
and bells hanging on all four sides,
with golden ropes crisscrossing.
Pearl nets
were spread out above,
and golden flower tassels
hung down everywhere,
with various colorful decorations
surrounding them,
and soft fine floss
used as cushions.
The finest silk,
worth a thousand million,
pure white and clean,
was used to cover them.
There were large white oxen,
fat, strong, and powerful,
with beautiful bodies,
to pull the jeweled carriages.
Many attendants
were there to serve and protect them.
With these wonderful carriages,
he equally bestowed them on his children.
At that time, the children,
rejoiced and leaped for joy,
riding in these jeweled carriages,
traveling in all directions,
playing happily,
free and unhindered.
He told Shèlìfú:
"I am also like this,
the most honored among the saints,
the father of the world.
All sentient beings
are all my children,
deeply attached to worldly pleasures,
without wisdom.
The Three Realms are without peace,
like a burning house,
full of suffering,
truly terrifying.
There is always the worry of birth, old age, sickness, and death,
such fires
blaze without ceasing.
The Tathāgata has already left
the burning house of the Three Realms,
dwelling quietly in seclusion,
peacefully residing in the forest wilderness.
Now these Three Realms,
are all mine,
and the sentient beings within them,
are all my children.
But now this place,
has many misfortunes and difficulties,
and I alone
can provide rescue and protection.
Although I teach and instruct them,
they do not believe and accept it,
because they are deeply attached
to the defilements of desire.
With this expedient means,
I preach the Three Vehicles,
causing all sentient beings
to know the suffering of the Three Realms,
opening up and expounding
the path to transcendence.
If these children
are resolute in their minds,
possessing the three kinds of knowledge,
and the six supernatural powers,
some will attain Pratyekabuddhahood,
and others will become irreversible Bodhisattvas.
You, Shèlìfú!
For the sake of sentient beings,
I use this parable,
to preach the One Buddha Vehicle.
If you can
believe and accept these words,
all of you will
attain Buddhahood.
This vehicle is subtle,
pure, and foremost,
in all the worlds,
it is unsurpassed,
and pleasing to the Buddha.
All sentient beings
should praise,
make offerings, and prostrate to it.
Immeasurable billions
of powers, liberations,
samādhi, wisdom,
and the Buddha's other dharmas,
are obtained through this vehicle.
Causing these children
to constantly play, day and night for kalpas,
together with all the Bodhisattvas,
and the Śrāvaka assembly,
riding this jeweled vehicle,
directly to the Bodhimaṇḍa.
Because of this cause and condition,
seeking earnestly in the ten directions,
there is no other vehicle,
except for the Buddha's expedient means."
He told Shèlìfú:
"You all
are all my children,
and I am the father.
You have been burned by suffering for kalpas,
and I have rescued you all,
causing you to leave the Three Realms.
Although I said before:
'You will attain extinction,'
it is only the exhaustion of birth and death,
