and in reality, it is not extinction;
what you should do now,
is only the wisdom of the Buddha.
If there are Bodhisattvas
in this assembly,
who can listen wholeheartedly
to the true dharma of the Buddhas,
the World-Honored Ones, the Buddhas,
although using expedient means,
the sentient beings they transform,
are all Bodhisattvas.
If people are of small wisdom,
and deeply attached to love and desire,
for the sake of these,
I preach the truth of suffering.
The sentient beings rejoice,
obtaining what they have never had before,
the Buddha's preaching of the truth of suffering,
is true and without difference.
If there are sentient beings,
who do not know the origin of suffering,
and are deeply attached to the cause of suffering,
unable to relinquish it even for a moment,
for the sake of these,
I expediently preach the path.
The cause of all suffering,
is rooted in greed and desire,
if greed and desire are extinguished,
there is nothing to rely on,
the extinguishing of all suffering,
is called the third truth.
For the sake of the truth of extinction,
cultivating the path,
and leaving all the bonds of suffering,
is called obtaining liberation.
From what do these people
obtain liberation?
Only by leaving falsity,
is it called liberation;"
In reality, one has not yet attained
complete liberation.
The Buddha says that such a person
has not truly attained extinction.
Because this person has not attained
the unsurpassed Way,
I do not wish
to cause them to reach extinction.
I am the Dharma King,
free and at ease in the Dharma,
bringing peace to sentient beings,
therefore I appear in the world.
You, Shèlìfú!
This Dharma seal of mine,
I speak for the benefit
wherever you travel, do not recklessly spread it.
If there are those who hear it,
rejoice and receive it with reverence,
know that such a person
will never regress.
If there are those who believe and accept
this scripture,
this person has already
seen past Buddhas,
respectfully made offerings,
and also heard this Dharma.
If a person is able
to believe what you say,
then they have seen me,
and also seen you,
and the community of monks,
along with all the Bodhisattvas.
This *Saddharma Puṇḍarīka Sūtra*
is spoken for those of profound wisdom;
those of shallow understanding, upon hearing it,
will be confused and not understand.
All *śrāvakas*
and *pratyekabuddhas*
in this scripture,
their strength is insufficient.
You, Shèlìfú!
Even you, with regard to this scripture,
have entered through faith;
how much more so the other *śrāvakas*.
The other *śrāvakas*,
believe in the Buddha's words,
and follow this scripture,
it is not their own intellectual capacity.
Moreover, Shèlìfú!
Those who are arrogant and lazy,
who cling to the view of self,
do not speak this scripture to them.
Common people with shallow understanding,
deeply attached to the five desires,
upon hearing it, cannot understand,
do not speak it to them either.
If a person does not believe
and slanders this scripture,
then they sever all
Buddha seeds in the world.
Or even frown
and harbor doubts,
you should listen and hear
the karmic retribution of this person.
Whether the Buddha is in the world
or after his extinction,
those who slander
such scriptures as this,
seeing those who read, recite,
write and uphold the scriptures,
lightly regard them with hatred and jealousy,
and harbor resentment.
The karmic retribution of this person,
you should listen again now.
When that person's life ends,
they enter the Avīci hell,
for a full *kalpa*;
when the *kalpa* ends, they are born again.
In this way, revolving
for countless *kalpas*,
emerging from hell,
they will fall into the animal realm.
As dogs and jackals,
their forms will be emaciated,
dark, scabby, and leprous,
harassed by people.
Moreover, they will be
despised and loathed by people,
constantly suffering from hunger and thirst,
their bones and flesh withered,
living in torment,
dying under tiles and stones.
Because they severed the Buddha seed,
they receive this karmic retribution.
If they become camels,
or are born among donkeys,
their bodies constantly bearing heavy loads,
subjected to beatings with sticks,
thinking only of water and grass,
knowing nothing else.
Because they slandered this scripture,
they obtain such karmic consequences.
Some become jackals,
entering villages,
their bodies scabby and leprous,
also without one eye.
Beaten and pelted
by children,
enduring all kinds of suffering,
sometimes even to death.
Having died in this way,
they further receive the body of a python.
Its form is long and large,
five hundred *yojanas*,
deaf, foolish, and without feet,
writhing on its belly,
eaten and bitten
by various small insects,
suffering day and night,
without rest.
Because they slandered this scripture,
they obtain such karmic consequences.
If they are able to become human,
their faculties are dull and dim,
short, ugly, crippled,
blind, deaf, hunchbacked.
Whatever they say,
people do not believe or accept,
their breath is constantly foul,
possessed by demons and goblins.
Poor and lowly,
used by others,
often sick and emaciated,
without refuge or support.
Although they are close to people,
people do not care about them,
whatever they obtain,
they quickly forget and lose.
If they practice medicine,
following prescriptions to cure illnesses,
they instead increase others' ailments,
or even cause death.
If they themselves are sick,
no one heals or treats them,
even if they take good medicine,
their condition worsens.
If others rebel,
plunder, rob, and steal,
such crimes as these,
calamites are laid upon them.
Such a sinful person
will never see the Buddha,
the King of all Sages,
speaking the Dharma and teaching.
Such a sinful person
is constantly born in difficult places,
mad, deaf, their mind confused,
never hearing the Dharma.
For countless *kalpas*,
like the sands of the Gaṅgā River,
they are always born deaf and mute,
their faculties incomplete.
Constantly dwelling in hell,
as if strolling in a garden,
remaining in evil paths,
as if in their own home,
camels, donkeys, pigs, and dogs,
are where they go.
Because they slandered this scripture,
they obtain such karmic consequences.
If they are able to become human,
deaf, blind, mute,
poor, and with all kinds of decline,
they adorn themselves with these.
Bloated with edema, withered with consumption,
scabby, leprous, with ulcers and sores,
such illnesses as these,
they use as clothing.
Their bodies constantly stink,
filthy and unclean,
deeply attached to the view of self,
increasing anger and hatred,
lust is rampant,
not discriminating between humans and animals.
Because they slandered this scripture,
they obtain such karmic consequences."
He told Shèlìfú:
"If one were to speak of the sins of those who slander this scripture,
one could not exhaust them in countless *kalpas*.
Because of this cause and condition,
I therefore tell you:
'Do not speak this scripture among the unintelligent.'
If there are those with sharp roots,
clear intelligence and wisdom,
much learning and strong memory,
who seek the Buddha Way,
such a person as this,
then you may speak it to them.
If someone has seen
hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
planted all kinds of good roots,
and has a deep and firm mind,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
If someone is diligent,
constantly cultivates a mind of loving-kindness,
and does not spare their own life,
they are fit to hear it.
If someone is respectful,
has no divided mind,
is detached from common fools,
and dwells alone in the mountains and marshes,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
Furthermore, Shèlìfú!
If you see someone
abandoning evil teachers,
and befriending good companions,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
If you see a Buddha-child
upholding the precepts purely,
like a clean and bright pearl,
seeking the Great Vehicle Sutra,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
If someone is without anger,
honest, upright, gentle, and yielding,
constantly has compassion for all,
and reveres all Buddhas,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
Furthermore, if a Buddha-child
in a great assembly,
with a pure mind,
using all kinds of causes and conditions,
similes, metaphors, and eloquent words,
preaches the Dharma without obstruction,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
If there is a Bhiksu
seeking the wisdom of all-knowing,
seeking the Dharma in all directions,
joining palms and receiving it on the crown of their head,
only delighting in receiving and upholding
the Great Vehicle scriptures,
even to the point of not receiving
a single verse of other scriptures,
such a person
is fit to hear it.
If a person sincerely
seeks the relics of the Buddha,
and seeks this scripture in the same way,
and after obtaining it, receives it on the crown of their head,
and that person no longer
aspires to other scriptures,
nor has ever thought of
externalist texts,
such a person
is fit to hear it."
The Buddha told Shèlìfú:
"I say that these characteristics
of those who seek the Buddha Way
cannot be exhausted even in countless kalpas."
Such people
are able to believe and understand,
you should preach to them
the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Sutra.
At that time, Huìmìng Xūpútí,
Móhē Jiāzhānyán,
Móhē Jiāshè,
Móhē Mùjiānlián,
having heard from the Buddha this unprecedented Dharma,
that the World Honored One bestowed on Shèlìfú the prediction of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi,
gave rise to a rare and wonderful mind, rejoicing and leaping for joy,
immediately arose from their seats, adjusted their robes,
bared their right shoulders, knelt on their right knees,
single-mindedly joined their palms,
bowed respectfully,
gazed up at the Venerable Countenance,
and said to the Buddha:
"We are leaders of the Sangha,
our years are passing and we are becoming decrepit,
thinking that we have already attained Nirvāṇa, and are incapable of anything,
no longer advancing to seek Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
World Honored One, in the past, when you preached the Dharma for a long time,
we were present in the assembly,
our bodies were weary and lax,
only contemplating emptiness, signlessness, and non-action,
regarding the Bodhisattva Dharma—spiritual powers as play, purifying the Buddha-lands, perfecting sentient beings—our minds did not delight in it.
Why is this?
World Honored One, you caused us to emerge from the Triple Realm and attain the proof of Nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, now that we are old and decrepit,
regarding the Buddha's teaching, the transformation of Bodhisattvas, and Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi,
we do not give rise to a single thought of delight or joy.
Now we, in the presence of the Buddha,
having heard the prediction of Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi for Śrāvakas,
our minds are greatly joyful,
attaining what we had never attained before.
Not expecting that today, we would suddenly hear this rare and wonderful Dharma,
we deeply rejoice and congratulate ourselves, obtaining great benefits,
immeasurable treasures, obtained without seeking them.
"World Honored One!
Now we delight in speaking a parable to illuminate this meaning.
It is like a person who, when young and immature,
abandons their father and flees, dwelling in another country for a long time,
perhaps ten, twenty, or even fifty years.
When they have grown up, they are also poor and destitute,
running around in all directions seeking food and clothing.
Gradually wandering, they encounter and head towards their home country."
Their father had been seeking his son for a long time, but could not find him,
and stopped in one city.
His family was very wealthy, with limitless treasures—
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, coral, amber, crystal pearls, and so on.
All of his storehouses were completely full;
he had many servants, ministers, officials, and common people;
elephants, horses, carriages, and countless cattle and sheep—
his income and profits extended to other countries,
and there were also very many merchants and traders.
At that time, the poor son
wandered through the villages, passing through countries and cities,
and eventually arrived at the city where his father was staying.
The parents thought of their son,
having been separated from him for over fifty years,
but had never told anyone about this matter,
only pondering to themselves, with hearts full of regret and remorse,
thinking that they were old and decrepit,
with much wealth,
gold, silver, treasures, and overflowing storehouses;
and no children,
if they suddenly died,
the wealth would be scattered and lost,
with no one to entrust it to.
Therefore, they diligently and constantly remembered their son,
and again had this thought:
'If I were to obtain a son, entrust the wealth to him,
I would be relaxed and happy, without any worries.'
World Honored One!
At that time, the poor son
while working as a hired laborer, gradually encountered his father's house,
and stood at the side of the gate. From afar, he saw his father
sitting on a lion throne, with a jeweled pedestal supporting his feet,
Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and householders all respectfully surrounding him,
adorning his body with a pearl necklace worth millions;
officials, common people, and servants, holding white whisks in their hands, attended him on the left and right.
He was covered by a jeweled canopy,
with various flower banners hanging down,
fragrant water sprinkled on the ground,
and various famous flowers scattered about,
precious objects were arranged in rows, being brought in and out, taken and given,
there were such various kinds of adornments,
his awesome virtue was especially honored.
The poor son, seeing his father having great power and influence,
immediately felt fear and terror,
regretting coming to this place.
He secretly had this thought:
'This is perhaps a king,
or someone like a king,
not a place where I can obtain things by hired labor.
It would be better to go to a poor village, where I can exert my strength and find a place,
and obtain food and clothing easily.
If I stay here for a long time,
I might be coerced and forced to work.'
Having had this thought,
he quickly ran away.
At that time, the wealthy elder
on the lion throne, saw his son and recognized him,
his heart greatly rejoiced,
and he immediately had this thought:
'My wealth and treasures now have someone to be entrusted to.
I have constantly thought of this son,
having no way to see him,
and now he has suddenly come by himself,
greatly satisfying my wish.
Although I am old, I am still greedy and protective.'
He immediately sent someone nearby to urgently chase after him and bring him back.
At that time, the messenger quickly ran to seize him.
The poor son was astonished and terrified, crying out and complaining loudly:
'I have not committed any offense, why are you seizing me?'
The messenger held him more urgently, forcefully dragging him back.
At that time, the poor son, thinking
that he was innocent, but was being imprisoned and seized,
thought that he would certainly die;
he became even more terrified, fainted and collapsed on the ground.
The father saw him from afar,
and said to the messenger:
'There is no need for this person,
do not forcefully bring him here.
Sprinkle cold water on his face, let him regain consciousness,
do not speak to him again.'"
What is the reason for this?
The father knew that his son's aspirations and intentions were base and inferior,
and he knew that his own wealth and status would be difficult for his son to accept.
He carefully acknowledged that this was his son
and used skillful means, not telling others that this was his son.
He sent a messenger to tell him:
『I am now setting you free, to go wherever you please.』
The poor son was overjoyed, feeling something he had never felt before.
He rose from the ground and went to poor villages to seek food and clothing.
At that time, the elder
wanted to entice and guide his son
and devised a skillful plan.
He secretly sent two men who looked haggard and lacked imposing presence:
『Go to him and gently tell the poor son:
"There is work here, and we will pay you double."
If the poor son agrees, bring him here to work.
If he asks, "What kind of work?"
then tell him: "We will hire you to remove waste.
We two will also work with you."』
The two messengers then sought out the poor son.
Having found him, they explained the matter in detail.
At that time, the poor son first took his wages and then immediately began removing waste.
His father saw his son and felt pity and bewilderment.
Another day, he remotely saw his son through a window.
He was thin and haggard, covered in waste and dust, dirty and unclean.
He immediately took off his necklace, fine soft clothes, and ornaments,
and put on coarse, worn, and greasy clothes,
covered himself in dust, and held a waste-removing tool in his right hand,
appearing somewhat fearful. He said to the workers:
『Work diligently, do not be lazy.』
Through skillful means, he was able to get close to his son.
Later, he further said:
『Hey, man!
Always work here, do not go elsewhere again.
I will increase your wages.
Whatever you need, such as pots, pans, rice, noodles, salt, and vinegar,
do not hesitate to ask.
There are also old and worn-out servants who can provide what you need.
Make yourself comfortable.
I am like your father, do not worry anymore.
What is the reason for this?
I am old, and you are young and strong.
When you work, you are never deceitful, lazy, angry, or resentful.
I have not seen any of these bad qualities in you, unlike the other workers.
From now on, I will treat you like my own son.』
Immediately, the elder gave him a new name, calling him "Son."
At that time, the poor son,
though pleased by this encounter,
still considered himself a hired, lowly worker.
Because of this, he was always made to remove waste for twenty years.
After that period,
they trusted each other, and there were no restrictions on his coming and going,
but he still lived in his original place.
"Bhagavan,
at that time, the elder became ill
and knew that he would die soon.
He said to the poor son:
『I now have much gold, silver, and precious jewels, and the storehouses are overflowing.
You know the quantity of each, what should be taken and given.
I feel this way, so you should understand my intention.
What is the reason for this?
Now, what I have is no different from what you have.
You should be more diligent and not let anything be lost.』
At that time, the poor son
immediately received the instructions
and took charge of all the possessions,
the gold, silver, precious jewels, and all the storehouses,
but he had no desire to take even a single meal's worth.
However, he still lived in his original place,
and his inferior mentality had not yet been discarded.
After some more time,
the father knew that his son's mind had gradually become open and at ease, and that he had developed great aspirations, despising his former self.
When he was about to die, he summoned his son
and gathered his relatives,
the king, ministers, *chà lì*, householders,
and everyone was assembled.
He then declared:
『Everyone should know!
This is my son,
whom I fathered.
He left me and ran away from a certain city.
He has been wandering and suffering for over fifty years.
His original name was so-and-so.
My name is so-and-so.
In the past, I was in that city,
worrying and searching for him.
Suddenly, I encountered and found him here.
This is indeed my son,
and I am indeed his father.
Now, all my possessions
belong to my son.
He knows all that has been given out and taken in.』
Bhagavan!
At that time, the poor son heard his father's words
and was overjoyed, feeling something he had never felt before.
He thought to himself:
『I originally had no intention to seek anything,
but now this treasure has come to me naturally.』
Bhagavan!
The great wealthy elder is like the *Rúlái*,
and we are all like the Buddha's sons.
The *Rúlái* always says that we are his sons.
Bhagavan!
Because of the three sufferings,
we experience various torments in the cycle of birth and death.
We are confused, ignorant, and attached to the small laws.
Today, the Bhagavan is causing us to reflect,
to clear away the waste of the frivolous debates of all dharmas.
Among them, we diligently exert ourselves, attaining the price of one day of Nirvana.
Having attained this, we are overjoyed and consider ourselves satisfied,
and then we say to ourselves:
『Because we are diligent and exert ourselves in the Buddha's Dharma,
we have gained much.』
But the Bhagavan
already knew that our minds were attached to base desires and delighted in the small laws.
He then allowed us to be, not explaining to us:
『You should have a share in the *Rúlái*'s knowledge and vision, the treasure trove.』
The Bhagavan uses skillful means to speak of the *Rúlái*'s wisdom.
We follow the Buddha and obtain the price of one day of Nirvana,
thinking it is a great gain;
we have no aspiration for this great vehicle.
We also use the *Rúlái*'s wisdom to explain and expound to the Bodhisattvas,
but we ourselves have no aspiration for this.
What is the reason for this?
The Buddha knows that our minds delight in the small laws.
With skillful means, he speaks according to our level;
but we do not know that we are truly the Buddha's sons.
Now we know
that the Bhagavan is not
stingy with the Buddha's wisdom.
What is the reason for this?
We have been truly the Buddha's sons from the past,
but we only delight in the small laws.
If we had a mind that delighted in the great,
the Buddha would have spoken the great vehicle Dharma for us.
In this sutra, only the One Vehicle is spoken of,
but in the past, in front of the Bodhisattvas, he criticized the *Śrāvakās* who delight in the small laws.
But the Buddha truly used the Great Vehicle to teach and transform them.
Therefore, we say that we originally had no intention to seek anything.
Now the great treasure of the Dharma King has come to us naturally,
and all that a Buddha's son should obtain has already been obtained."
At that time, *Móhē Jiāshè*
wanted to restate this meaning
and spoke in verse, saying:
We today,
hearing the Buddha's voice and teaching,
rejoice and leap for joy,
gaining what we have never gained before.
The Buddha says that *Śrāvakās*
will attain Buddhahood.
The supreme treasure trove
is obtained without seeking.
It is like a child,
young and ignorant,
abandoning his father and running away,
traveling far to other lands,
wandering through various countries,
for over fifty years.
His father worries and thinks of him,
searching for him in all directions.
Having grown weary of searching,
he stops in a city,
building a house,
and indulging himself in the five desires.
His family is extremely wealthy,
with much gold and silver,
*chē qú*, *mǎ năo*,
pearls, and *liúlí*;
elephants, horses, cattle, and sheep,
palanquins and carriages;
fields, servants,
and many people.
His income from buying and selling
extends to other countries.
Merchants and traders
are everywhere.
Hundreds of millions of people
surround him with respect and reverence.
He is always loved
and respected by the king,
and all the ministers and powerful clans
revere him together.
Because of these reasons,
there are many who come and go.
He is so wealthy
and powerful.
As he grows old,
he worries more and more about his son, thinking of him day and night.
The time of death is approaching.
The foolish son abandoned me, for more than fifty years,
What will become of the stored goods
in the treasury?
At that time, the poor son
sought clothing and food,
from village to village,
from country to country.
Sometimes he obtained something,
sometimes he obtained nothing,
hungry and emaciated,
his body covered with sores and scabies.
Gradually passing through,
he arrived at the city where his father lived,
hired as a laborer and moving from place to place,
he eventually reached his father's house.
At that time, the elder,
inside his gate, spread out a great jeweled tent,
seated on a lion throne,
surrounded by his family,
with many people attending him.
Some were calculating
gold, silver, and jewels,
managing the incoming and outgoing property,
and recording the documents and notes.
The poor son saw his father
wealthy, noble, and dignified,
and thought he was a king.
"If he is a king or the like,
I am frightened and surprised myself.
Why have I come here?"
He reflected to himself,
"If I stay here long,
I might be forced
to work against my will."
Having thought this,
he ran away,
inquiring about poor neighborhoods,
wanting to find work as a laborer.
The elder, at that time,
on the lion throne,
saw his son from afar,
and silently recognized him.
He immediately ordered a messenger
to seize him and bring him back.
The poor son cried out in alarm,
confused and collapsing to the ground:
"This man is seizing me,
surely I will be killed.
What use is clothing and food
if I am brought to this?"
The elder knew his son
was foolish and narrow-minded,
not believing his words,
not believing he was his father.
He then used an expedient,
and sent other people,
with defective eyes and dwarfish,
without imposing dignity:
"You can tell him,
that we will hire him,
to remove all the filth,
and pay him double."
The poor son heard this,
and joyfully followed them,
to remove the filth,
and clean all the rooms.
The elder, from the window,
often saw his son,
thinking his son was foolish and inferior,
content with lowly tasks.
Thereupon the elder,
wearing tattered and dirty clothes,
holding a dung-cleaning tool,
went to where his son was,
conveniently getting close,
and told him to work diligently:
"I will increase your wages,
and provide oil for your feet,
ample food and drink,
and thick, warm mats."
He spoke such harsh words:
"You must work diligently."
Then with gentle words:
"Like my own son."
The elder was wise,
gradually allowing him to enter and leave,
for twenty years,
managing the affairs of the household.
Showing him the gold, silver,
pearls, and crystal;
making him aware of all the incoming and outgoing goods.
He made him know everything.
Still he lived outside the gate,
dwelling in a grass hut,
thinking of his poverty:
"I have none of these things."
The father knew his son's mind,
had gradually broadened,
and wanted to give him the property.
He then gathered his relatives,
the king and great ministers,
the kṣatriyas and householders.
Before this great assembly,
he declared, "This is my son,
who abandoned me and went elsewhere,
for fifty years.
Since seeing my son return,
it has been twenty years.
Long ago, in a certain city,
I lost this son,
and searched everywhere,
finally coming to this place.
All that I have,
the houses and people,
I give entirely to him,
to use as he pleases."
The son remembered his past poverty,
his intentions were base and inferior,
but now at his father's place,
he had obtained great treasures,
along with houses,
and all property.
He was greatly delighted,
and had never experienced such a thing.
The Buddha is also like this,
knowing that we delight in the small,
he never said,
"You will become Buddhas."
But he said that we
obtained all the outflows,
accomplished the Small Vehicle,
and were *Śrāvakā* disciples.
The Buddha commanded us
to speak of the Supreme Path,
those who cultivate this
will attain Buddhahood.
I accept the Buddha's teaching,
for the sake of great *bodhisattvas*,
with various causes and conditions,
various parables,
and many words,
I speak of the unsurpassed path.
All you sons of the Buddha,
hearing the Dharma from me,
day and night contemplating,
diligently cultivating.
At that time, all the Buddhas,
immediately bestowed their predictions:
"In the future,
you shall become Buddhas."
All the Buddhas,
the Dharma of the secret treasury,
only for the *bodhisattvas*, expound the true reality,
but not for us,
speak of this true essence.
Like that poor son,
getting close to his father,
although he knew of all the possessions,
his mind did not aspire to take them.
Although we speak of
the Buddha Dharma treasury,
we ourselves have no aspirations,
and it is just like that.
We attained inner extinction,
considered ourselves satisfied,
only understanding this matter,
with nothing further.
If we were to hear of
pure Buddha lands,
and teaching sentient beings,
we would have no joy or delight.
Why is this?
All dharmas,
are completely empty and still,
without arising or ceasing,
without large or small,
without outflow or activity.
Thinking like this,
we do not generate joy or delight.
For a long time,
in the Buddha's wisdom,
we had no greed or attachment,
no further aspirations;
and regarding the Dharma itself,
considered it the ultimate.
For a long time,
cultivating the empty Dharma,
we attained liberation from the Three Realms,
and the suffering and affliction,
Dwelling in the final body,
possessing Nirvāṇa with remainder.
What the Buddha taught,
obtaining the Dao is not empty;
thus it is considered already obtained,
repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Although we are,
all Buddha's sons,
speaking the Bodhisattva Dharma,
in order to seek the Buddha Way;
yet regarding this Dharma,
we have no perpetual desire for joy.
The guide, seeing that we would abandon it,
because of observing our minds,
initially did not encourage advancement,
speaking of its real benefits.
Like a rich elder,
knowing his sons' inferior aspirations,
with skillful means,
gently subdues their minds,
and only then entrusts
all his wealth to them.
The Buddha is also like this,
manifesting rare and wonderful things,
knowing those who delight in the small,
with skillful means,
taming and subduing their minds,
then teaches great wisdom.
We today,
have obtained what we never had before,
not what we initially hoped for,
but now we obtain it ourselves,
like that poor son,
who obtains limitless treasures.
World Honored One, we now,
have attained the Dao and achieved the fruit,
regarding the unconditioned Dharma,
obtained the pure eye.
We, for a long night,
have upheld the Buddha's pure precepts,
and only today,
obtained their fruit and reward,
within the Dharma King's Dharma,
cultivated pure conduct for a long time,
and now obtained the unconditioned,
unsurpassed great fruit.
We now,
are truly Śrāvakas,
using the Buddha Way's voice,
to cause all to hear.
We now,
are true Arhats,
in all the worlds,
of gods, humans, demons, and Brahmās,
universally among them,
worthy of receiving offerings.
World Honored One's great kindness,
with rare and wonderful things,
compassionately teaching and transforming,
benefiting us,
for limitless hundreds of millions of kalpas,
who can repay?
Supplying with hands and feet,
bowing with the head at the top [of the body],
all offerings,
cannot repay.
If with the crown of the head bearing,
carrying on both shoulders,
for Ganges-river-sand kalpas,
wholeheartedly reverent;
and also with delicious foods,
limitless precious garments,
and all kinds of bedding,
various medicinal soups,
sandalwood from *Niútóu*,
and all precious treasures,
to erect towers and temples,
and spread precious garments on the ground.
Such things as these,
using them to make offerings,
for Ganges-river-sand kalpas,
also cannot repay.
The Buddhas are rare,
limitless and boundless,
inconceivable,
with great spiritual power,
unconditioned and uncreated,
kings of all Dharmas.
Able to, for the inferior,
endure such matters,
grasping-at-appearances ordinary people,
according to what is suitable, speak for them.
The Buddhas, regarding the Dharma,
attain the most freedom,
knowing all sentient beings, various desires and joys,
and their aspirations and strengths.
According to what they are capable of,
with limitless metaphors,
they speak the Dharma for them.
According to all sentient beings, past-life good roots,
and knowing those who are mature and those who are not mature,
with all kinds of considerations,
having discerned and known,
regarding the One Vehicle Path,
according to what is suitable, speak of the Three.
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* Scroll Three
Tripiṭaka Master from the *Qiūcí* Kingdom of the Later *Qín*,
Jūmóluóshí, by imperial order, translated.
At that time, the World Honored One told Mahākāśyapa and the great disciples:
"Excellent, excellent! Kāśyapa,
you have excellently spoken of the Tathāgata's true merits and virtues.
Truly as you have said,
the Tathāgata also has limitless, boundless asaṃkhya merits and virtues;
even if you were to speak of them for limitless hundreds of millions of kalpas, you could not exhaust them.
Kāśyapa! You should know
that the Tathāgata is the King of all Dharmas;
whatever he says is not false.
Regarding all Dharmas,
with wisdom and skillful means, he expounds them;
what he speaks,
all arrives at the ground of all-knowing wisdom.
The Tathāgata observes and knows where all Dharmas ultimately lead,
and also knows what all sentient beings deeply think and do,
penetrating without obstruction;
and regarding all Dharmas, he thoroughly understands and clarifies them,
showing all sentient beings all wisdom.
Kāśyapa!

For example, in the three-thousand great-thousand world, the mountains, rivers, streams, valleys, and land produce herbs, trees, thickets, and forests, and all medicinal plants, in many kinds, with names and colors each different.
Dense clouds spread out, covering the three-thousand great-thousand world,
simultaneously pouring down equally, and their moisture universally saturates. Herbs, trees, thickets, and forests,
with small roots, small stems, small branches, and small leaves,
medium roots, medium stems, medium branches, and medium leaves,
large roots, large stems, large branches, and large leaves,
all trees, large and small,
according to upper, middle, and lower, each receive what they need.
The rain from one cloud,
according to its species nature,
enables it to grow and flourish,
with flowers blooming and fruits ripening.
Although born from the same earth and moistened by the same rain,
all the grasses and trees,
each have their differences.
Kāśyapa! You should know
that the Tathāgata is also like this,
appearing in the world like a great cloud rising,
with a great voice, universally throughout the world of gods, humans, and asuras,
like that great cloud covering the three-thousand great-thousand lands.
Within the great assembly, he proclaims these words:

'I am the Tathāgata, worthy of offerings, perfectly enlightened, complete in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, understander of the world, unsurpassed worthy, tamer of men, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World Honored One,
causing those who are not yet liberated to be liberated,
causing those who do not yet understand to understand,
causing those who are not yet peaceful to be peaceful,
causing those who have not yet attained Nirvāṇa to attain Nirvāṇa,
in this life and the next, knowing them as they truly are.
I am the one who knows all,
the one who sees all,
the one who knows the Path,
the one who opens the Path,
the one who speaks the Path,
you gods, humans, and asura assemblies,
should all come here,
for the sake of listening to the Dharma.'
At that time, countless millions of kinds of sentient beings
come to the Buddha's place and listen to the Dharma.
The Tathāgata at that time, observing these sentient beings' sharp or dull faculties, diligence or laziness,
according to their capabilities, speaks the Dharma for them,
in various limitless ways,
causing them all to be joyful and quickly gain good benefits.
These sentient beings, having heard this Dharma,
are peaceful in this life and are born in good places in the future,
receiving joy through the Path, and also able to hear the Dharma.
Having heard the Dharma, they are free from all obstacles,
and within all Dharmas,
according to their ability, gradually enter the Path.
Like that great cloud, raining on all herbs, trees, thickets, and forests, and all medicinal plants,
according to their species nature,
fully receiving moisture, each grows and flourishes.
The Tathāgata speaks the Dharma, with one mark, one taste —
what is called: the mark of liberation, the mark of detachment, the mark of extinction,
ultimately reaching all-knowing wisdom.
Those sentient beings who hear the Tathāgata's Dharma,
if they uphold it, read it, recite it, and practice as it says,
the merits and virtues they obtain, they do not realize themselves.
Why is this?
Only the Tathāgata knows these sentient beings' species' appearance and substance nature,
what they contemplate,
what they think about,
what they cultivate,
how they contemplate,
how they think about,
how they cultivate,
with what Dharma they contemplate,
with what Dharma they think about,
with what Dharma they cultivate,
with what Dharma they obtain what Dharma.
Living beings dwell in various kinds of lands,
only the *Rúlái* truly sees them, clearly and without obstruction.
Like those grasses, trees, thickets, forests, and various medicinal herbs,
which do not themselves know their superior, intermediate, and inferior natures.
*Rúlái* knows that it is a Dharma of one appearance and one taste—
that is: the appearance of liberation, the appearance of detachment, the appearance of extinction—
ultimate *Nièpán*, the appearance of constant quiescence and extinction, ultimately returning to emptiness.
Having known this, the Buddha observes the desires of sentient beings and protects them,
therefore, he does not immediately speak of all-knowing wisdom.
"You, *Jiāshè*! Are very rare,
able to know that *Rúlái* preaches the Dharma according to what is suitable, able to believe and receive it.
Why is that? It is difficult to understand and know that all Buddhas, the World Honored Ones, preach the Dharma according to what is suitable."
At that time, the World Honored One, desiring to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
Breaking through existence, the Dharma King,
appears in the world,
according to the desires of sentient beings,
preaching the Dharma in various ways.
*Rúlái* is venerable,
with profound and far-reaching wisdom,
having long been silent about this essential teaching,
not striving to speak it quickly.
If those with wisdom hear it,
they will be able to believe and understand;
those without wisdom will doubt and regret,
and thus lose it forever.
Therefore, *Jiāshè*!
I preach according to my strength,
using various causes and conditions,
to enable them to attain right view.
*Jiāshè* should know!
It is like a great cloud,
rising in the world,
covering everything;
a cloud of wisdom containing moisture,
with lightning flashing brilliantly,
thunder rumbling afar,
causing all to rejoice.
The sunlight is obscured,
the ground is cool and refreshing,
thick and dense, hanging low,
as if it can be grasped.
The rain falls equally everywhere,
descending in all four directions,
flowing and pouring immeasurably,
filling all the land.
Mountains, rivers, dangerous valleys,
and secluded places,
grasses, trees, medicinal herbs,
large and small trees,
hundreds of grains and seedlings,
sugarcane and grapes,
nourished by the rain,
all are abundant and sufficient,
the dry land is universally moistened,
and medicinal plants grow luxuriantly together.
The water that the cloud emits
is of one taste,
but grasses, trees, and thickets,
receive moisture according to their capacity.
All the trees,
superior, intermediate, and inferior,
according to their size,
each obtain growth,
roots, stems, branches, leaves,
flowers, fruits, light, and color,
all reached by a single rain,
all become fresh and lustrous.
According to their physical forms,
natures, sizes,
the moisture received is the same,
but each grows luxuriantly.
The Buddha is also like this,
appearing in the world,
like a great cloud,
universally covering everything.
Having appeared in the world,
for all sentient beings,
he analyzes and explains
the reality of all Dharmas.
The Great Sage, the World Honored One,
among all devas and humans,
in all assemblies,
declares these words:
'I am *Rúlái*,
the Honored One of Two Feet,
appearing in the world,
like a great cloud,
fully moistening everything.
Causing withered sentient beings,
all to be liberated from suffering,
attaining peace and happiness—
the happiness of the world,
and the happiness of *Nièpán*.
All devas and humans,
listen attentively with one mind,
all should come here,
to see the unsurpassed Honored One.'
I am the World Honored One,
none can compare,
bringing peace to sentient beings,
therefore I appear in the world.
For the great assembly I speak,
the sweet dew of pure Dharma,
that Dharma is of one taste,
liberation and *Nièpán*.
With one wonderful sound,
I expound this meaning,
always creating the cause
for the Great Vehicle.
I observe everything,
universally and equally,
without any difference,
or feelings of love and hatred.
I have no greed or attachment,
nor any limitations or obstacles,
I constantly and equally
preach the Dharma to all.
As for one person,
so too for many,
I constantly preach the Dharma,
and have never done anything else.
Whether going, coming, sitting, or standing,
I never tire,
satisfying the world,
like rain universally moistening.
Noble and base, high and low,
those who uphold the precepts and those who break them,
those who are complete in dignified conduct,
and those who are not,
those with right view and those with wrong view,
those with sharp faculties and those with dull faculties,
equally raining the rain of Dharma,
without weariness or fatigue.
All sentient beings,
who hear my Dharma,
receive it according to their capacity,
and dwell in various lands.
Some are in the realms of humans and devas,
*Zhuǎnlún Shèngwáng*,
*Shì*, *Fàn*, and various kings,
these are small medicinal herbs.
Knowing the unconditioned Dharma,
able to attain *Nièpán*,
arising with the six superknowledges,
and attaining the three insights,
dwelling alone in the mountains and forests,
constantly practicing *chán* meditation,
attaining the realization of *Yuánjué*,
these are intermediate medicinal herbs.
Seeking the place of the World Honored One,
thinking, "I shall become a Buddha,"
practicing diligent *dìng*,
these are superior medicinal herbs.
Furthermore, those sons of the Buddha,
who are focused on the Buddha Path,
constantly practicing loving-kindness and compassion,
knowing themselves that they will become Buddhas,
certain and without doubt,
these are called small trees.
Dwelling in superknowledges,
turning the irreversible wheel,
liberating countless hundreds
of millions of sentient beings,
such *Púsà*s,
are called large trees.
The Buddha preaches equally,
like rain of one taste;
according to the nature of sentient beings,
what is received is different,
like those grasses and trees,
whose inherent qualities are diverse.
The Buddha uses this analogy,
to skillfully reveal and explain,
with various words and phrases,
preaching the One Dharma,
in the Buddha's wisdom,
like a single drop in the ocean.
I rain the rain of Dharma,
filling the world,
the Dharma of one taste,
practicing according to one's capacity.
Like those thickets,
medicinal herbs, and various trees,
according to their size,
gradually increasing and becoming beautiful.
The Dharma of all Buddhas,
is always of one taste,
causing all in the world,
to universally become complete,
gradually cultivating,
all attain the fruit of the Path.
The *Shēngwén* and *Yuánjué*,
residing in mountains and forests,
dwelling in their last body,
hearing the Dharma and attaining the fruit,
are called medicinal herbs,
each attaining growth.
If there are *Púsà*,
whose wisdom is firm and solid,
who understand the Three Realms,
and seek the highest vehicle,
they are called small trees,
and attain growth.
Furthermore, there are those who dwell in *chán*,
and obtain supernatural powers,
hearing that all dharmas are empty,
their hearts greatly rejoice,
emitting countless lights,
liberating all sentient beings,
they are called large trees,
and attain growth.
Thus, *Jiāyè*!
The Dharma spoken by the Buddha,
is like a great cloud,
with a single flavor of rain,
moistening the human flowers,
each attaining fruition.
*Jiāyè* should know!
By various causes and conditions,
and various metaphors,
I reveal the Buddha path,
this is my expedient means,
and so do all Buddhas.
Now, for you all,
I speak the most real truth:
'All the *Shēngwén* assembly,
are not extinguished.
The path you walk,
is the *Púsà* path,
gradually cultivate and learn,
all shall become Buddhas.'
At that time, after the World Honored One spoke this verse,
he addressed the great assembly, proclaiming these words:
"This disciple of mine, *Móhē Jiāyè*,
in the future, will offer to three million *yì* Buddhas, World Honored Ones,
making offerings, revering, respecting, and praising,
widely proclaiming the immeasurable great Dharma of all Buddhas.
In his last body, he will become a Buddha,
named *Guāngmíng Rúlái*, *Yìnggòng*, *Zhèngbiànzhī*, *Míngxíngzú*, *Shànshì*, *Shìjiānjiě*, *Wúshàngshì*, *Tiáoyùzhàngfū*, *Tiānrénshī*, *Fó*, *Shìzūn*.
His country will be named *Guāngdé*,
his *jié* will be named *Dàzhuāngyán*.
The Buddha's life will be twelve small *jié*,
the Proper Dharma will abide in the world for twenty small *jié*,
the Semblance Dharma will also abide for twenty small *jié*.
His land will be adorned,
without any filth or evil,
tiles, gravel, or thorns,
excrement or impurity.
That land will be level and just,
without any high or low places,
pits, bumps, or mounds.
*Liúlí* will be the ground,
rows of precious trees,
golden ropes will mark the paths,
scattered with precious flowers, all around pure and clean.
In that country, the *Púsà* will be countless thousands of *yì*,
the *Shēngwén* assembly will also be countless,
without any demonic affairs,
though there be demons and their people,
they will all protect the Buddha Dharma."
At that time, the World Honored One, desiring to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Announcing to all *Bǐqiū*:
'With my Buddha eye,
I see this *Jiāyè*,
in a future world,
passing countless *jié*,
shall become a Buddha.
And in the coming age,
offering and attending,
three million *yì*,
Buddhas, World Honored Ones.
For the wisdom of the Buddha,
purely cultivating Brahma conduct.
Having offered to the highest,
the two-legged honored one,
cultivating all,
unsurpassed wisdom.
In his last body,
he shall become a Buddha.
His land will be pure,
*liúlí* will be the ground,
many precious trees,
in rows on the sides of the paths,
golden ropes marking the paths,
those who see them rejoice.
Constantly emitting good incense,
scattering famous flowers,
various wonderful things,
to adorn it.
The ground will be level and just,
without hills or pits.
The *Púsà* assembly,
cannot be counted,
their hearts are gentle and compliant,
attaining great supernatural powers,
upholding the Buddhas,
the Great Vehicle scriptures.
The *Shēngwén* assembly,
without outflows in their last body,
sons of the Dharma King,
also cannot be counted,
even with the heavenly eye,
one cannot know the number.
That Buddha's lifespan will be,
twelve small *jié*;
the Proper Dharma abiding in the world,
twenty small *jié*;
the Semblance Dharma will also abide,
*Guāngmíng* World Honored One,
such are these affairs.'
At that time, *Dàmùqiánlián*,
*Xūpútí*, *Móhē Jiāzhānyán*, and others,
were all filled with trepidation,
with one mind, joining their palms,
gazing at the honored countenance,
not turning their eyes away for a moment,
and together spoke
this verse:
Greatly Heroic World Honored One,
Dharma King of the *Shì* clan,
out of compassion for us,
bestowing the Buddha's voice.
If you know our deep hearts,
and foresee us receiving predictions,
it is like sprinkling with sweet dew,
removing heat and gaining coolness.
Like coming from a famine-stricken country,
suddenly encountering a great king's feast,
the heart still harbors doubt and fear,
not daring to eat immediately;
if one receives the king's instruction,
then one dares to eat.
We are also like this,
always mindful of the faults of the Small Vehicle,
not knowing how,
to obtain the Buddha's unsurpassed wisdom.
Though we hear the Buddha's voice,
saying that we shall become Buddhas,
our hearts still harbor worry and fear,
like not daring to eat immediately;
if we receive the Buddha's prediction,
then we will be joyful and at peace.
Greatly Heroic World Honored One,
constantly wishing to bring peace to the world,
may you grant us predictions,
like the hungry needing instruction to eat.
At that time, the World Honored One
knew what the great disciples were thinking in their hearts,
and told the *Bǐqiū*:
"This *Xūpútí*, in the future, will offer to three million *yì* *nàyóutā* Buddhas,
making offerings, revering, respecting, and praising,
constantly cultivating Brahma conduct, perfecting the *Púsà* path.
In his last body, he will become a Buddha,
named *Míngxiàng Rúlái*, *Yìnggòng*, *Zhèngbiànzhī*, *Míngxíngzú*, *Shànshì*, *Shìjiānjiě*, *Wúshàngshì*, *Tiáoyùzhàngfū*, *Tiānrénshī*, *Fó*, *Shìzūn*.
His *jié* will be named *Yǒubǎo*.
His country will be named *Bǎoshēng*.
That land will be level and just,
*pōlí* will be the ground,
adorned with precious trees,
without any hills, pits, sand, gravel, thorns, or the filth of excrement,
precious flowers covering the ground, all around pure and clean.
The people of that land will all dwell in precious terraces and exquisite pavilions.
The *Shēngwén* disciples will be immeasurable and boundless,
beyond what can be known by calculation or metaphor.
The *Púsà* assembly will be countless thousands of *yì* *nàyóutā*.
The Buddha's life will be twelve small *jié*,
the Proper Dharma will abide in the world for twenty small *jié*,
the Semblance Dharma will also abide for twenty small *jié*.
That Buddha will constantly dwell in the void,
speaking the Dharma for the assembly,
liberating immeasurable *Púsà* and *Shēngwén* assemblies."
At that time, the World Honored One, desiring to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Monks,
I now tell you all,
that you should all be of one mind,
and listen to what I say:
My great disciple,
Shū Pútí,
will attain Buddhahood,
with the name Míngxiàng.
He will make offerings to countless
millions of billions of Buddhas,
following the path of the Buddhas,
gradually perfecting the Great Path.
In his final life, he will obtain
the thirty-two marks,
perfect and beautiful,
like a precious mountain.
His Buddha-land
will be the most beautifully adorned.
All beings who see it
will without exception love and rejoice.
The Buddha within it
will liberate immeasurable beings.
Within his Buddha-dharma,
there will be many Bodhisattvas,
all possessing sharp faculties,
turning the irreversible wheel.
That land will constantly be
adorned with Bodhisattvas.
The assembly of Śrāvakas
will be beyond counting,
all having attained the three insights,
possessing the six super-knowledges,
abiding in the eight liberations,
and having great power and virtue.
His Dharma-teaching
will manifest in limitless
spiritual powers and transformations,
inconceivable.
Gods and people,
in numbers like the Ganges sands,
will all join their palms together,
listening to and receiving the Buddha's words.
His Buddha's lifespan
will be twelve small kalpas,
the Proper Dharma will abide in the world
for twenty small kalpas,
and the Semblance Dharma will also abide
for twenty small kalpas.
At that time, the World-Honored One further addressed the assembly of monks:
"I now tell you,
that the great Jiāzhān Yán, in a future age,
will use various offerings to make offerings and attend to eight billion Buddhas, revering and honoring them.
After the Buddhas have passed away,
he will each time raise stupas and temples, a thousand yojanas high,
five hundred yojanas in breadth and width,
all made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *chēqú*, *mǎnǎo*, pearls, rose quartz, and the seven treasures,
with various flowers, necklaces, perfumed creams, powdered incense, burning incense, silk canopies, banners, and flags,
to make offerings to the stupas and temples.
After this has passed,
he will again make offerings to twenty billion Buddhas,
and so on.
Having made offerings to all these Buddhas,
perfecting the Bodhisattva path, he will attain Buddhahood,

with the name *Yánfú Nàtí Jīngguāng Rúlái*, Worthy of Offerings, Universally Aware, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding the World, Unexcelled One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
His land will be level and just,
with crystal as its ground, adorned with jeweled trees,
with ropes of gold delineating the sides of the roads,
covered with wondrous flowers, all around pure and clean,
those who see it will rejoice.
There will be no four evil paths—hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and *Āxiūluó*—
but many gods, humans, and assemblies of Śrāvakas,
and Bodhisattvas, immeasurable millions of billions, adorning his country.
The Buddha's lifespan will be twelve small kalpas,
the Proper Dharma will abide in the world for twenty small kalpas,
and the Semblance Dharma will also abide for twenty small kalpas."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
Monks,
all listen with one mind,
to what I say,
which is true and without difference.
This Jiāzhān Yán,
will use various
wondrous and excellent offerings,
to make offerings to all the Buddhas.
After the Buddhas have passed away,
he will raise seven-jeweled stupas,
and also use flowers and incense,
to make offerings to the relics.
In his final body,
he will obtain Buddha-wisdom,
and attain Equal and Proper Enlightenment.
His country will be pure and clean,
delivering immeasurable
millions of billions of beings,
all being by the ten directions
offered to.
The Buddha's light
will have no one who can surpass it.
That Buddha will be named
*Yánfú Jīngguāng*.
Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas,
cutting off all existence,
immeasurable and countless, will adorn his country.
At that time, the World-Honored One further addressed the great assembly:
"I now tell you,
that the great Mùjiānlián
will use various offerings to make offerings to eight thousand Buddhas,
revering and honoring them.
After the Buddhas have passed away,
he will each time raise stupas and temples, a thousand yojanas high,
five hundred yojanas in breadth and width,
all made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *chēqú*, *mǎnǎo*, pearls, rose quartz, and the seven treasures,
with various flowers, necklaces, perfumed creams, powdered incense, burning incense, silk canopies, banners, and flags,
to use in making offerings.
After this has passed,
he will again make offerings to two million billion Buddhas,
and so on.
He will attain Buddhahood,
with the name *Duōmóluó Bápá Zhāntánxiāng Rúlái*,
Worthy of Offerings, Universally Aware, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding the World, Unexcelled One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
The kalpa will be named Delight-Filled,
the country will be named Mind-Pleasing.
His land will be level and just,
with crystal as its ground, adorned with jeweled trees,
scattered with true pearl flowers, all around pure and clean,
those who see it will rejoice.
There will be many gods, humans, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas, their number immeasurable.
The Buddha's lifespan will be twenty-four small kalpas,
the Proper Dharma will abide in the world for forty small kalpas,
and the Semblance Dharma will also abide for forty small kalpas."
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
This disciple of mine,
the great Mùjiānlián,
having relinquished this body,
will see eight thousand,
two million billion,
Buddhas, World-Honored Ones.
For the sake of the Buddha-path,
he will make offerings and revere,
at the places of all the Buddhas,
constantly cultivating pure conduct,
for immeasurable kalpas,
upholding the Buddha-dharma.
After the Buddhas have passed away,
he will raise seven-jeweled stupas,
with long pillars and golden *chà*,
with flowers, incense, music,
and with these make offerings
to the Buddhas' stupas and temples.
Gradually perfecting
the Bodhisattva path,
in the Mind-Pleasing country,
he will attain Buddhahood.
His name will be *Duōmóluó*,
of *Zhāntán* incense.
The Buddha's lifespan
will be twenty-four kalpas,
constantly for gods and humans,
expounding the Buddha-path.
The Śrāvakas will be immeasurable,
like the Ganges sands,
with the three insights and six super-knowledges,
having great power and virtue.
The Bodhisattvas will be countless,
with firm resolve and vigorous progress,
regarding the Buddha's wisdom,
all irreversibly advancing.
After the Buddha has passed into extinction,
the Proper Dharma will abide,
for forty small kalpas,
and the Semblance Dharma will also be so.
All my disciples,
possessing complete power and virtue,
five hundred in number,
will all receive predictions
that in future lives,
they will all attain Buddhahood.
I and you all, due to
past life causes and conditions,
I will now speak of them,
you should listen well.
The Buddha told the monks:
"In the past, in immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable *asaṃkhya* kalpas,
at that time there was a Buddha,

named *Dàtōng Zhìshèng Rúlái*, Worthy of Offerings, Universally Aware, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding the World, Unexcelled One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
His country was named Good Achievement,
the kalpa was named Great Appearance.
Monks!
The time since that Buddha's Parinirvana is exceedingly long and distant.
Suppose someone were to grind all the soil in the three-thousand-great-thousand world system into ink.
Passing over a thousand buddha-fields to the east, they drop a speck,
as small as a mote of dust.
Then, passing over another thousand buddha-fields,
they drop another speck.
They continue in this way until all the soil-ink is used up.
What do you think?
Could a mathematician,
or a mathematician's disciple,
reach the limit of these buddha-fields and know their number?"
"No, World Honored One!"
"Monks! If all the buddha-fields traversed by that person,
both those with and without dots,
were ground into dust,
with each dust mote representing one kalpa,
the time since that Buddha's Parinirvana would still surpass that number by
immeasurable, boundless, hundreds of thousands of millions of *asaṃkhya* kalpas.
With the power of a *Tathāgata*'s knowledge and vision,
I observe that long ago as if it were today."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke the following verse:
"I recall the past,
immeasurable and boundless kalpas ago,
there was a Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings,
named *Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝).
As if a person, with strength, grinds
the soil of a three-thousand-great-thousand world system,
using all of that soil
entirely as ink.
Passing over a thousand buddha-fields,
they drop one speck of dust,
and continue dropping specks in this manner,
using up all of that dust-ink.
All of those buddha-fields,
both those with dots and those without,
are again ground into dust,
and each dust mote becomes one kalpa.
This number of dust motes,
and the kalpas surpass even that.
Since that Buddha's Parinirvana,
such immeasurable kalpas have passed.
The *Tathāgata*'s unobstructed wisdom
knows that Buddha's Parinirvana,
as well as his *śrāvakas* and *bodhisattvas*,
as if seeing their Parinirvana today.
Monks, you should know!
The Buddha's wisdom is pure and subtle,
without outflows and without obstruction,
comprehending immeasurable kalpas."
The Buddha told the monks,
"*Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝) Buddha
lived for five hundred forty million *nayuta* kalpas.
That Buddha originally sat in the *bodhimaṇḍa*,
having defeated the armies of Mara,
about to attain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
but the Buddha-dharmas did not manifest before him.
For one small kalpa, even up to ten small kalpas,
he sat in the lotus position, his body and mind unmoving,
but the Buddha-dharmas still did not manifest before him.
At that time, the *Trayastriṃśa* heavens
had previously prepared a lion throne for that Buddha beneath the Bodhi tree, one *yojana* high.
The Buddha, upon this seat,
was about to attain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
As soon as he sat upon that seat,
the Brahma kings rained down heavenly flowers,
covering a hundred *yojanas*.
Fragrant breezes came at times, blowing away the withered flowers,
and replacing them with new ones.
This continued without ceasing for ten small kalpas, offering to the Buddha,
and they continued to rain down these flowers until his Parinirvana.
The Four Heavenly Kings
constantly beat the heavenly drums to make offerings to the Buddha.
The other devas made heavenly music,
for ten small kalpas,
and until his Parinirvana,
it was likewise.
Monks!
*Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝) Buddha, after ten small kalpas,
finally had the Buddhadharmas manifest before him and attained *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Before that Buddha left home,
he had sixteen sons,
the first of whom was named *Zhìjī* (智積).
Each of the sons had various rare and precious playthings.
Upon hearing that their father had attained *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
they all abandoned their treasures and went to the Buddha's location.
Their mothers wept and followed them."
Their grandfather, a *cakravartin* king,
along with one hundred ministers and hundreds of thousands of millions of people,
all surrounded and followed them to the *bodhimaṇḍa*.
They all wished to draw near to the *Tathāgata* *Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝),
to offer, revere, respect, and praise him.
Having arrived, they bowed their heads to his feet, circumambulated the Buddha,
single-mindedly joined their palms, and gazed up at the World Honored One,
reciting the following gatha:
'World Honored One of great might and virtue,
for the sake of liberating sentient beings,
through immeasurable millions of kalpas,
you have finally attained Buddhahood,
all vows have been fulfilled,
auspicious, good, and unsurpassed.
World Honored One, how rare,
sitting for ten small kalpas,
your body, hands, and feet
are still and unmoving.
Your mind is always serene,
never scattered,
ultimately forever extinguished,
abiding in the Dharma without outflows.
Now seeing the World Honored One,
peacefully attaining Buddhahood,
we have obtained great benefit,
and celebrate with great joy.
Sentient beings constantly suffer,
blind and without a guide,
not knowing the path to the cessation of suffering,
not knowing to seek liberation.
Throughout the long night, evil destinies increase,
and the multitude of devas diminish,
going from darkness into darkness,
never hearing the Buddha's name.
Now the Buddha has attained the supreme,
peaceful, and outflow-free path,
we and the devas
have obtained the greatest benefit,
therefore we bow our heads
and take refuge in the Unsurpassed Honored One.'"
At that time, the sixteen princes, having praised the Buddha with verses,
urged the World Honored One to turn the Dharma wheel,
all saying,
"May the World Honored One preach the Dharma, bringing peace, compassion, and benefit to devas and humans."
They spoke again in verse:
"Hero of the world, unequaled,
adorned with hundreds of blessings,
having attained unsurpassed wisdom,
we hope you will speak for the sake of the world.
Liberating us
and all classes of sentient beings,
please differentiate and reveal
so we may attain this wisdom.
If we attain Buddhahood,
sentient beings will be the same.
The World Honored One knows the thoughts
and paths of practice
in the depths of sentient beings' minds, also knowing their wisdom,
desires, merit,
and karmic actions from past lives.
Having fully known all this, World Honored One,
please turn the unsurpassed wheel."
The Buddha told the monks,
"When *Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝) Buddha
attained *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
five hundred million buddha-fields in each of the ten directions shook in six ways.
In the dark places between those countries,
where the sun and moon could not shine,
all became brightly illuminated. The beings within could see each other,
and all wondered,
'How did beings suddenly appear here?
Furthermore, the borders of these lands, the palaces of the devas,
even the Brahma palaces, are shaking in six ways;
a great light shines everywhere, filling the worlds,
surpassing the light of the devas.'
At that time, in the five hundred million buddha-fields in the east,
the Brahma palaces shone with light, many times brighter than usual.
The Brahma kings all thought,
'The light of our palaces is unprecedented.
What is the cause of this phenomenon?'
At that time, the Brahma kings
went to each other and discussed this matter together.
Among them was a Great Brahma King
named *Jiù Yīqiè* (救一切),
who spoke the following verse for the Brahma assembly:
'The light of our palaces
is unprecedented,
what is the cause of this,
we should all seek it together.
Is a greatly virtuous deva born,
or has a Buddha appeared in the world,
that this great light
shines everywhere in the ten directions?'"
At that time, the Brahma kings from the five hundred million buddha-fields,
together with their palaces,
each filled their garments with heavenly flowers,
and together went westward to investigate this phenomenon.
They saw the *Tathāgata* *Dàtōng Zhìshèng* (大通智勝) in the *bodhimaṇḍa*,
sitting on a lion throne beneath the Bodhi tree,
surrounded by devas, *nāgas*, *gandharvas*, *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, humans, and non-humans, all reverently surrounding him,
and they saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel."
Immediately, all the Brahma kings prostrated themselves before the Buddha,
circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times,
and then scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha—
the flowers they scattered were like Mount Xūmí;
and also used them to make offerings to the Buddha's Bodhi tree—
the Bodhi tree was ten *yóuxún* high.
After offering the flowers,
each presented their palaces to that Buddha,
and said:
'We only ask for your compassion, to benefit us.
We hope you will accept the palaces we offer.'
Then the Brahma kings,
in front of the Buddha, with one mind and voice, spoke in verse:
'The World-Honored One is exceedingly rare,
difficult to encounter,
possessing immeasurable merits,
able to protect all.
The great teacher of gods and humans,
has compassion for the world,
all sentient beings in the ten directions,
universally receive benefit.
The lands from which we have come, five hundred million *yì* countries,
abandoning the joy of deep meditation,
for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha.
Our blessings from past lives,
make our palaces extremely adorned,
now we offer them to the World-Honored One,
we only hope you will accept them with compassion.'
At that time, the Brahma kings,
having praised the Buddha in verse,
each said:
'We only hope the World-Honored One will turn the Dharma wheel,
delivering sentient beings and opening the path to *Nièpán*.'
Then the Brahma kings,
with one mind and voice, spoke in verse:
'World Hero, honored among two-legged beings,
we only hope you will expound the Dharma,
with great compassion and power,
to deliver suffering sentient beings.'
At that time, the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Thus Come One,
silently agreed.
"Furthermore, monks! The Great Brahma Kings from five hundred million *yì* lands in the southeast
each saw their palaces
shining with light, as never before.
Rejoicing and leaping for joy, with rare thoughts arising,
they immediately approached each other and discussed this matter.
At that time, among them
was a Great Brahma King,
named Dàbēi (大悲),
who spoke to the Brahma assembly
in verse:
'What is the cause and condition
that this sign appears?
The light of our palaces
has never been seen before.
Is it because a greatly virtuous god is born?
Or is it because a Buddha has appeared in the world?
Having never seen this sign,
we should seek it with one mind.
Passing through millions of *yì* lands,
following the light to investigate together,
it is mostly likely that a Buddha has appeared in the world,
to deliver suffering sentient beings.'
At that time, the five hundred million *yì* Brahma Kings,
together with their palaces,
each filled their sleeves with heavenly flowers,
and together went to the northwest to seek out this sign.
They saw the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Thus Come One, in the *Dàochǎng*
under the Bodhi tree, seated on a lion throne,
with gods, dragon kings, *gāntàpó*, *jǐnnuóluó*, *móhóuluóqié*, humans and non-humans, respectfully surrounding him,
and also saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel.
At that time, the Brahma Kings
prostrated themselves before the Buddha, circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times,
and then scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha—
the flowers they scattered were like Mount Xūmí,
and also used them to make offerings to the Buddha's Bodhi tree.
After offering the flowers,
each presented their palaces to that Buddha,
and said:
'We only ask for your compassion, to benefit us.
We hope you will accept the palaces we offer.'
At that time, the Brahma Kings,
in front of the Buddha, with one mind and voice,
spoke in verse:
'Holy Lord, King among the gods,
with the voice of a *jiālíngpínqié*,
compassionate to sentient beings,
we now respectfully bow to you.
The World-Honored One is exceedingly rare,
appearing only after a long time,
for one hundred and eighty *jié*,
passing in vain without a Buddha.
The three evil paths are full,
the assemblies of gods diminish,
now the Buddha appears in the world,
to be eyes for sentient beings.
The refuge of the world,
protecting all,
as a father to sentient beings,
compassionate and beneficial.
We are fortunate from past blessings,
to now encounter the World-Honored One.'
At that time, the Brahma Kings, having praised the Buddha in verse,
each said:
'We only hope the World-Honored One will have compassion for all,
turn the Dharma wheel,
and deliver sentient beings.'
Then the Brahma Kings,
with one mind and voice, spoke in verse:
'Great Sage, turn the Dharma wheel,
reveal the characteristics of all *dharmas*,
deliver suffering sentient beings,
and bring them great joy.
Sentient beings who hear this Dharma,
attain the Way, or are born in the heavens,
the evil paths diminish,
and those who are patient and good increase.'
"At that time, the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Thus Come One
silently agreed.
"Furthermore, monks!
The Great Brahma Kings from five hundred million *yì* lands in the south,
each saw their palaces
shining with light, as never before.
Rejoicing and leaping for joy, with rare thoughts arising,
they immediately approached each other and discussed this matter:
'What is the cause and condition that our palaces have this light?'
At that time, among them
was a Great Brahma King,
named Miàofǎ (妙法),
who spoke to the Brahma assembly
in verse:
'The light of our palaces is very brilliant and majestic.
This is not without cause,
this sign should be sought.
Passing through hundreds of thousands of *jié*,
we have never seen this sign before.
Is it because a greatly virtuous god is born?
Or is it because a Buddha has appeared in the world?'
At that time, the five hundred million *yì* Brahma Kings,
together with their palaces,
each filled their sleeves with heavenly flowers,
and together went to the north to seek out this sign.
They saw the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Thus Come One, in the *Dàochǎng*
under the Bodhi tree, seated on a lion throne,
with gods, dragon kings, *gāntàpó*, *jǐnnuóluó*, *móhóuluóqié*, humans and non-humans, respectfully surrounding him,
and also saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel. Then the Brahma Kings
prostrated themselves before the Buddha, circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times,
and then scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha—
the flowers they scattered were like Mount Xūmí,
and also used them to make offerings to the Buddha's Bodhi tree.
After offering the flowers,
each presented their palaces to that Buddha,
and said:
'We only ask for your compassion, to benefit us.
We hope you will accept the palaces we offer.'
At that time, the Brahma Kings,
in front of the Buddha, with one mind and voice,
spoke in verse:
'The World-Honored One is very difficult to see,
one who destroys all afflictions,
after passing one hundred and thirty *jié*,
we now finally see him.
To all hungry and thirsty sentient beings,
you bring fulfillment with the rain of Dharma,
one whom we have never seen before,
of immeasurable wisdom,
like an *udumbara* flower,
we encounter you today.
Our palaces,
are adorned because of your light,
World-Honored One, with great compassion,
we only hope you will accept them.'
"At that time, the Brahma Kings, having praised the Buddha in verse,
each said:
'We only hope the World-Honored One will turn the Dharma wheel,
so that all beings in the world, gods, *mó*, *fàn*, *shāmén*, *bāluómén*,
may obtain peace and deliverance.'
Then the Brahma Kings,
with one mind and voice,
spoke in verse:
"We only wish that the World Honored One will turn the unsurpassed Dharma wheel,
strike the great Dharma drum,
and blow the great Dharma conch,
universally raining down the great Dharma rain,
delivering immeasurable sentient beings.
We all return and request,
+ENDVERSE You should expound the profound and far-reaching sound."
At that time, the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victorious Buddha
silently granted it.
The same was true from the southwest direction to even the downward direction.
At that time, the Great Brahma Kings of five million billion lands in the upward direction
all saw their own palaces
shining with light and majesty, which they had never seen before.
Rejoicing and leaping, they gave rise to rare thoughts,
and immediately visited each other, discussing this matter together:
"What is the cause and condition that our palaces have such light?"
At that time, among that assembly, there was a Great Brahma Heaven King,
named Shī Qì,
who spoke a verse for all the Brahma multitudes,
"Now, what is the cause and condition
that our palaces
shine with majestic and virtuous light,
adorned in a way never seen before?
Such a wonderful sign,
never heard or seen in the past,
is it the birth of a greatly virtuous deva?
Or the appearance of a Buddha in the world?"
At that time, the five million billion Brahma Heaven Kings,
together with their palaces,
each filled their sleeves with various celestial flowers,
and together went downwards to seek this sign.
They saw the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victorious Tathāgata, residing in the place of enlightenment
under the Bodhi tree, sitting on a lion throne,
surrounded by devas, dragon kings, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, etc., with reverence,
and saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel.
At that time, the Brahma Heaven Kings
bowed their heads and paid homage to the Buddha, circling him hundreds of thousands of times,
and then scattered celestial flowers upon the Buddha—
the scattered flowers were like Mount Xūmí,
and they also made offerings to the Buddha's Bodhi tree.
After offering the flowers,
they each offered their palaces to that Buddha,
and said these words:
"We only hope that you will see our plight and benefit us.
We offer these palaces, may you accept them."
At that time, the Brahma Heaven Kings,
in front of the Buddha, with one mind and voice,
recited a verse in praise:
"Excellent is seeing all the Buddhas,
the Holy Ones who save the world,
who can from the three realms' prison, diligently extract all sentient beings.
Universally wise, Honored One of devas and humans,
have compassion for the masses of beings,
able to open the gate of sweet dew,
extensively delivering all.
In the past, for countless kalpas,
passing by in vain without a Buddha,
when the World Honored One had not yet appeared,
the ten directions were always dark and obscure,
the three evil paths increased,
the asuras also flourished,
the multitudes of devas gradually decreased,
many died and fell into evil paths.
Not hearing the Dharma from the Buddha,
they constantly practiced unwholesome deeds,
color, strength, and wisdom,
all of these diminished.
Because of the causes and conditions of sinful deeds,
they lost joy and the thought of joy,
dwelling in the Dharma of wrong views,
not recognizing good conduct,
not being transformed by the Buddha,
they constantly fell into evil paths.
The Buddha is the eye of the world,
appearing only after a long time,
having compassion for all sentient beings,
therefore manifesting in the world.
Transcending and attaining right enlightenment,
we are extremely happy and rejoice,
and all the other multitudes,
joyfully exclaim, something never before experienced.
Our palaces,
adorned by your light,
now we offer them to the World Honored One,
we only hope you will accept them with compassion.
May we, with this merit,
universally extend it to all,
we and all sentient beings,
may all together attain the Buddha path."
At that time, the five million billion Brahma Heaven Kings, having praised the Buddha with verses,
each said to the Buddha:
"We only wish that the World Honored One
will turn the Dharma wheel,
bringing much peace and security,
and delivering many."
At that time, the Brahma Heaven Kings
spoke a verse:
"May the World Honored One turn the Dharma wheel,
strike the drum of sweet dew Dharma,
deliver sentient beings from suffering,
and reveal the path of Nirvāṇa.
We only wish you will accept our request,
and with great and subtle sounds,
compassionately expound
the Dharma practiced for immeasurable kalpas."
At that time, the Great Penetrating Wisdom Victorious Tathāgata,
accepting the request of the Brahma Heaven Kings of the ten directions and the sixteen princes,
immediately turned the twelve-spoked Dharma wheel in three turns—
which neither śrāmaṇas nor Brahmins,
nor devas, māras, Brahmas, nor the rest of the world can turn—
namely, this is suffering,
this is the accumulation of suffering,
this is the extinction of suffering,
this is the path to the extinction of suffering;
and extensively expounded the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination—
ignorance conditions action,
action conditions consciousness,
consciousness conditions name and form,
name and form condition the six entrances,
the six entrances condition contact,
contact conditions feeling,
feeling conditions craving,
craving conditions grasping,
grasping conditions becoming,
becoming conditions birth,
birth conditions old age, death, sorrow, grief, suffering, and distress.
With the extinction of ignorance, action is extinguished,
with the extinction of action, consciousness is extinguished,
with the extinction of consciousness, name and form are extinguished,
with the extinction of name and form, the six entrances are extinguished,
with the extinction of the six entrances, contact is extinguished,
with the extinction of contact, feeling is extinguished,
with the extinction of feeling, craving is extinguished,
with the extinction of craving, grasping is extinguished,
with the extinction of grasping, becoming is extinguished,
with the extinction of becoming, birth is extinguished,
with the extinction of birth, old age, death, sorrow, grief, suffering, and distress are extinguished.
When the Buddha spoke this Dharma in the assembly of devas and humans,
six hundred million nayutas of people,
because of not accepting any Dharma,
were liberated from the afflictions of their minds,
and all attained profound and wonderful samādhi,
the three kinds of knowledge, the six supernatural powers,
and possessed the eight liberations.
When the Dharma was spoken a second, third, and fourth time,
countless billions of gaṅgā sands of nayutas of sentient beings
also, because of not accepting any Dharma,
were liberated from the afflictions of their minds.
From this point onwards,
the Śrāvaka assembly
was immeasurable, boundless, and uncountable.
At that time, the sixteen princes—
all having left home as boys and becoming śrāmaṇeras,
with their faculties keen and their wisdom clear,
having already made offerings to hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
purely cultivating Brahma conduct,
seeking anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi—
together said to the Buddha:
