"World Honored One!
These immeasurable millions of great virtuous śrāvakas
have all already accomplished their goals.
World Honored One,
you should also speak the Dharma of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi for us,
and after we hear it, we will all cultivate and learn it together.
World Honored One!
Our aspiration is to know and see as the Tathāgata does,
and the thoughts in our deep minds, the Buddha knows himself."
At that time, eighty billion people among the multitude led by the Holy King who turns the wheel,
seeing the sixteen princes leave home,
also sought to leave home. The King immediately granted permission.
"At that time, that Buddha, accepting the request of the śrāmaṇeras,
after twenty thousand kalpas,
then in the midst of the four assemblies
spoke this Great Vehicle Sūtra,
named the 'Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower,' which teaches the bodhisattva Dharma,
protected and念ed by the Buddha.
After speaking this Sūtra,
the sixteen śrāmaṇeras,
for the sake of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
all together received, upheld, recited, and thoroughly understood it.
When this Sūtra was spoken,
the sixteen bodhisattva śrāmaṇeras all believed and accepted it;
among the śrāvaka assembly, there were also those who believed and understood;
the remaining sentient beings, in the millions of billions, all gave rise to doubts.
The Buddha spoke this Sūtra,
for eight thousand kalpas without ever resting.
After speaking this Sūtra, he immediately entered a quiet chamber,
dwelling in samādhi for eighty-four thousand kalpas.
At this time, the sixteen bodhisattva śrāmaṇeras,
knowing that the Buddha had entered the chamber and was quietly in samādhi, each ascended the Dharma seat and, also for eighty-four thousand kalpas,
extensively spoke and distinguished the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Sūtra for the four assemblies.
Each of them delivered six hundred million nayutas of gaṅgā sands of sentient beings, showing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them,
causing them to generate the mind of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"After the Da tōng zhì shèng Fó
had passed eighty-four thousand *kalpas*,
he arose from *samādhi*,
went to the Dharma seat, sat down peacefully,
and announced to the assembly:
'These sixteen *śrāmaṇera* Bodhisattvas
are extremely rare.
Their roots are sharp,
their wisdom is clear,
and they have already made offerings to countless millions of billions of Buddhas. In the presence of all those Buddhas, they constantly cultivated pure conduct,
received and upheld the wisdom of the Buddha,
opened and showed it to living beings, causing them to enter it.
All of you should frequently approach and make offerings to them.
Why is that?
If *śrāvakas*, *pratyekabuddhas*, and all Bodhisattvas
can believe in the Sutra Dharma spoken by these sixteen Bodhisattvas
and uphold it without destroying it,
then these people will all attain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the wisdom of the *Tathāgata*.' "
The Buddha told the *bhikṣus*:
"These sixteen Bodhisattvas constantly delight in speaking this wonderful *Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Dharma*.
Each Bodhisattva has transformed six million *nayutas* of *koṭis* of *gaṅgā* sands of living beings.
In every lifetime, they are together with the Bodhisattvas,
hear the Dharma from them, and all believe and understand it.
Due to this cause and condition,
they have encountered four million *koṭis* of Buddhas, World Honored Ones, and it is still not exhausted today.
*Bhikṣus*!
I now tell you:
'Those disciples of that Buddha, the sixteen *śrāmaṇeras*,
have now all attained *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In the ten directions of lands,
they are now speaking the Dharma,
with limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of Bodhisattvas and *śrāvakas* as their retinue.
Two of those *śrāmaṇeras* have become Buddhas in the east,
one named Āchù, in the Land of Joy,
the second named Sūmí Dǐng;
Two Buddhas in the southeast,
one named Shīzi Yīn,
the second named Shīzi Xiàng;
Two Buddhas in the south,
one named Xūkōng Zhù,
the second named Cháng Miè;
Two Buddhas in the southwest,
one named Dì Xiàng,
the second named Fàn Xiàng;
Two Buddhas in the west,
one named Āmítuó,
the second named Dù Yíqiè Shìjiān Kǔnǎo;
Two Buddhas in the northwest,
one named Duōmóluó Bápó Zhāntánxiāng Shéntōng,
the second named Sūmí Xiàng;
Two Buddhas in the north,
one named Yún Zìzài,
the second named Yún Zìzài Wáng;
The Buddha in the northeast
is named Huài Yíqiè Shìjiān Bùwèi;
The sixteenth, I, Śākyamuni Buddha,
have attained *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the *Saha* world.' "
*Bhikṣus*!
When we were *śrāmaṇeras*,
each of us taught and transformed limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of *gaṅgā* sands of living beings,
who heard the Dharma from us, for *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Of these living beings,
those who are now abiding in the ground of *śrāvakas*,
I constantly teach for *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
These people
should gradually enter the Buddha path through this Dharma.
Why is that?
The wisdom of the *Tathāgata* is difficult to believe and difficult to understand.
Those limitless *gaṅgā* sands of living beings who were transformed at that time
are you *bhikṣus*, and the *śrāvaka* disciples in the future world after my extinction.
After my extinction,
there will also be disciples who do not hear this sutra,
do not know or perceive the practices of the Bodhisattvas,
and generate the thought of extinction in the merit they have attained,
and will enter *nirvāṇa*.
I will become a Buddha in another land,
with a different name.
Although these people generate the thought of extinction and enter *nirvāṇa*,
they will seek the wisdom of the Buddha in that land,
hear this sutra,
and only through the Buddha vehicle will they attain extinction,
without any other vehicle,
except for the *Tathāgatas'* expedient teachings.
*Bhikṣus*!
If the *Tathāgata* knows that the time of *nirvāṇa* has arrived,
and the assembly is pure, their faith and understanding are firm,
they have thoroughly understood the Dharma of emptiness, and have deeply entered *dhyāna*,
then he gathers all the Bodhisattvas and the assembly of *śrāvakas* to speak this sutra for them.
In the world, there is no two vehicles by which one can attain extinction,
only the one Buddha vehicle can attain extinction.
*Bhikṣus*, you should know!
The *Tathāgata* is skilled in means, deeply understanding the nature of living beings,
knowing that their will and delight is in the small Dharma, and they are deeply attached to the five desires,
and for the sake of these people, he speaks of *nirvāṇa*.
If these people hear it, then they will believe and accept it.
It is like a dangerous and difficult road of five hundred *yojanas*, desolate and without people, a place of fear.
If there is a large crowd
who want to cross this road to a place of treasures.
There is a guide
who is intelligent and perceptive, and knows well the appearance of the road's dangers and blockages,
and leads the people, wanting to cross this difficulty.
The people he is leading
become weary and retreat midway, and say to the guide:
'We are exhausted and also afraid,
and cannot go forward anymore;
the road ahead is still far,
and now we want to retreat.'
The guide has many expedient means
and thinks to himself:
'These people are pitiable,
how can they abandon the great treasures and want to retreat?'
Having thought this,
with the power of expedient means,
he transforms a city in the dangerous road after three hundred *yojanas*,
and tells the crowd:
'You should not be afraid, and must not retreat.
Now this great city
can be stopped in at will.
If you enter this city, you will quickly obtain peace.
If you can go forward to the treasure place, you can also leave.'
At that time, the exhausted crowd
were greatly delighted and exclaimed that it was unprecedented:
'Now we are spared this evil road and quickly obtain peace.'
Thereupon, the crowd
entered the transformed city,
generating the thought that they had already crossed,
generating the thought of peace.
At that time, the guide,
knowing that this crowd had already stopped and rested, and were no longer weary,
then extinguished the transformed city,
and told the crowd:
'You can go now, the treasure place is near.
The great city earlier was transformed by me to give you a place to rest.'
" *Bhikṣus*!
The *Tathāgata* is also like this,
now acting as a great guide for you,
knowing that the evil paths of birth, death, afflictions, are dangerous, difficult, long, and far, and should be left and crossed over.
If living beings only hear of the one Buddha vehicle,
then they will not want to see the Buddha, will not want to approach him,
and will think:
'The Buddha path is long and far, and only after enduring diligent hardship
can it be accomplished.'
The Buddha knows that their minds are timid and inferior,
and with the power of expedient means, in order to provide rest in the middle of the path, he speaks of two *nirvāṇas*.
If living beings abide in the two grounds,
then the *Tathāgata* at that time will speak for them:
'What you have done is not yet completed,
the ground you abide in is near the Buddha's wisdom,
you should observe and consider that
the *nirvāṇa* you have obtained
is not real.
It is only the power of the *Tathāgata's* expedient means,
speaking of three by distinguishing them from the one Buddha vehicle.'
It is like that guide, for the sake of providing rest, transforming a great city.
Having already known that they had rested,
he told them: 'The treasure place is near,
this city is not real,
it was transformed by me.' "
At that time, the World Honored One, wanting to restate this meaning,
spoke these verses:
The Da tōng zhì shèng Buddha,
sat in the *bodhimaṇḍa* for ten *kalpas*.
The Buddhadharma did not appear before him,
and he could not attain the Buddha path.
All the *devas*, *nāga* kings,
*asura* hosts, and others,
constantly rained down heavenly flowers
to make offerings to that Buddha.
All the *devas* struck heavenly drums
and played all kinds of music.
Fragrant winds blew away the withered flowers,
and rained down new and beautiful ones again.
After ten small *kalpas* had passed,
he then attained the Buddha path.
All the *devas* and people of the world
were all filled with joy.
The sixteen sons of that Buddha,
all with their retinues,
surrounded by millions of *koṭis*,
together went to the Buddha's place,
prostrated themselves at the Buddha's feet,
and requested the turning of the Dharma wheel:
'May the rain of the Dharma of the holy lion
fill us and all beings.'
The World Honored One is very difficult to encounter,
appearing once after a long time,
to awaken the multitudes of beings,
shaking all things.
In the eastern worlds,
five hundred million *koṭis* of lands,
the light of the Brahma palaces shone brightly,
something that had never happened before.
All the *Brahmās* saw this sign,
and immediately came to the Buddha's place,
scattered flowers to make offerings,
and presented their palaces,
requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel,
praising him in verses.
The Buddha knew the time had not yet arrived,
and silently sat after being requested.
From the three directions and four intermediate directions,
above and below as well,
flowers were scattered, offered to the palace,
requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel:
'World Honored One is very difficult to encounter,
may you, with great compassion,
widely open the gate of sweet dew,
and turn the unsurpassed Dharma wheel.'
The World Honored One of boundless wisdom,
accepted the request of those people,
and proclaimed various Dharmas:
'The Four Noble Truths and Twelve Nidānas,
from ignorance to old age and death,
all arise from the condition of birth.
Such are the numerous faults,
you all should be aware of.'
When this Dharma was proclaimed and expounded,
six hundred million yì *gāi*,
attained the end of all suffering,
and all became Arhats.
During the second Dharma talk,
thousands of millions of *héng hé shā* beings,
being unattached to all dharmas,
also attained Arhatship.
From then on, those who attained the Dao,
their number was immeasurable,
and could not be counted even in billions of *jié*,
there was no end to it.
At that time, sixteen princes,
renounced their homes and became *shā mí*,
all together requested that Buddha,
to expound the Great Vehicle Dharma:
'We and our followers,
shall all attain Buddhahood,
wishing to be like the World Honored One, with eyes of wisdom that are the purest.'
The Buddha knew the thoughts of the youths,
and what they had practiced in past lives,
and with countless causes and conditions,
and various analogies,
spoke of the Six *bō luó mì*,
and matters of supernatural powers.
Differentiating the real and true Dharma,
the path walked by Bodhisattvas,
he spoke of the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
as many *héng hé shā* *gè*.
After that Buddha had spoken the scripture,
he entered meditative concentration in a quiet room,
sitting single-mindedly in one place,
for eighty-four thousand *jié*.
Those *shā mí* and others,
knowing that the Buddha had not yet emerged from *chán*,
spoke to countless millions of beings,
about the unsurpassed wisdom of the Buddha.
Each sitting on a Dharma seat,
expounded this Great Vehicle scripture,
after the Buddha entered stillness and silence,
they proclaimed and assisted in spreading the Dharma.
Each and every *shā mí* and others, the beings they converted,
numbered six hundred million yì, as numerous as *héng hé shā*.
After that Buddha entered *miè dù*,
these who heard the Dharma,
in all Buddha lands,
were always born together with their teacher.
These sixteen *shā mí*,
completely practiced the Buddha way,
and now in the ten directions,
each has attained perfect enlightenment.
Those who heard the Dharma at that time,
are each in various Buddhas' places,
those who remained in the *shēng wén* vehicle,
are gradually taught the Buddha way.
I was among the sixteen,
and once spoke this for you,
therefore with expedient means,
I lead you toward the Buddha's wisdom.
With this original cause and condition,
I now speak the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
allowing you to enter the Buddha way,
do not harbor fear or dread.
It is like a dangerous and evil road,
remote and filled with poisonous beasts,
and without water or grass,
a place dreaded by people.
Countless millions of beings,
wished to cross this dangerous road,
the road was extremely vast and far,
spanning five hundred *yóu xún*.
At that time, there was a guide,
with strong knowledge and wisdom,
clear mind and firm resolve,
who rescued the multitude from difficulties in the dangerous place.
The multitude were all weary,
and said to the guide:
'We are now utterly exhausted,
and wish to turn back here.'
The guide thought to himself:
'These people are truly pitiable,
how can they want to turn back,
and lose the great treasures?'
Immediately thinking of an expedient,
he decided to employ supernatural powers,
and transformed a great city,
adorning it with houses and dwellings,
surrounded by gardens and groves,
canals, streams, and bathing ponds,
with layered gates and high pavilions,
filled with men and women.
After making this transformation,
he comforted the multitude and said, 'Do not fear:
You may enter this city,
each can follow what you enjoy.'
The people, having entered the city,
were all greatly delighted,
all felt a sense of peace and security,
thinking they had already been delivered.
The guide, knowing they had rested,
gathered the multitude and said:
'You should continue forward,
this is but a transformation city.
Seeing you weary and exhausted,
wanting to turn back midway,
therefore with the power of expedient means,
I temporarily transformed this city.
You should diligently advance,
and together reach the place of treasures.'
I am also like this,
a guide for all.
Seeing all those who seek the Dao,
becoming lax and abandoning it midway,
unable to cross the cycle of birth and death,
and the dangerous roads of afflictions.
Therefore, with the power of expedient means,
I speak of *niè pán* for rest.
Saying, 'You have extinguished suffering,
and all that needs to be done is complete.'
Having known they have reached *niè pán*,
and all attained Arhatship,
then I gather the great assembly,
to speak the real and true Dharma.
The Buddhas, with the power of expedient means,
differentiate and speak of the Three Vehicles,
but there is only one Buddha Vehicle,
speaking of two only for the place of rest.
Now I speak the truth for you,
what you have attained is not *miè*,
for the all-encompassing wisdom of the Buddha,
you should generate great diligence.
You will attain the all-encompassing wisdom,
the ten powers and other Buddha Dharmas,
possessing the thirty-two marks,
that is the real and true *miè*.
The guides of all Buddhas,
speak of *niè pán* for rest,
having known this rest,
they lead them into the Buddha's wisdom.
*Miào Fǎ Lián Huā Jīng*
*Miào Fǎ Lián Huā Jīng*, Volume Four
Tripiṭaka Master *Jiū Mó Luó Shí* of the *Qiū Cí* Kingdom of the Later *Qín*,
under Imperial Decree, respectfully translates.
At that time, *Fù Lóu Ná Mí Duō Luó Ní Zǐ*,
having heard from the Buddha about the skillful means of expedient Dharma talks,
and also heard of the predictions of *Ā nòu duō luó sān miǎo sān pú tí* given to the great disciples,
and also heard of the events of past lives and causes,
and also heard that all Buddhas have great, self-existent, supernatural powers,
attained what he had never attained before, his mind pure and joyful.
Immediately rising from his seat, he went before the Buddha, bowed his head to the ground,
and stepped back to stand on one side,
gazing at the revered countenance, his eyes not leaving for even a moment,
and thought to himself:
"The World Honored One is most wondrous,
what he does is rare!
Following the various natures of the world,
with expedient wisdom and insight, he speaks the Dharma,
extracting beings from their attachments in all places.
Our words cannot express the Buddha's merit and virtue,
only the Buddha, the World Honored One,
can know our deep heart and original vows."
At that time, the Buddha told all the *bǐ qiū*:
"Do you see this *Fù Lóu Ná Mí Duō Luó Ní Zǐ*?
I often commend him as the foremost among speakers of the Dharma,
and often praise his various merits and virtues,
diligently upholding and assisting in proclaiming my Dharma,
able to instruct, guide, benefit, and gladden the four assemblies,
fully explaining the Buddha's true Dharma,
and greatly benefiting those who practice the holy life together.
Apart from the *Rú Lái*, no one can exhaust his eloquence and skill in debate.
Do not think that *Fù Lóu Ná* is only able to uphold and assist in proclaiming my Dharma,
but also in the past, in the presence of ninety billion Buddhas,
he upheld and assisted in proclaiming the Buddhas' true Dharma,
and was also the foremost among the speakers of the Dharma in their presence."
Furthermore, he was clear and thoroughly understood the emptiness taught by all the Buddhas,
attained the Four Unimpeded Knowledges,
and was always able to preach the Dharma scrupulously and purely,
without any doubts,
fully possessing the supernatural powers of a Bodhisattva.
Throughout his lifespan, he constantly cultivated pure conduct.
The people of that Buddha's world
all considered him to be truly a Śrāvaka;
however, Fúlóunà, with these skillful means,
benefited immeasurable hundreds of thousands of living beings,
and also transformed immeasurable asaṃkhya people,
causing them to establish Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For the sake of purifying the Buddha lands,
he constantly performed Buddha-deeds, teaching and transforming living beings.
"Monks!
Fúlóunà was also the foremost among the Dharma-preachers of the Seven Buddhas,
and now he is also the foremost among the Dharma-preachers in my assembly.
Among the future Buddhas in this Bhadrakalpa, he will also be the foremost among the Dharma-preachers,
and he will always protect and assist in proclaiming the Buddha-dharma.
In the future, he will also protect and assist in proclaiming the Dharma of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas,
teach and benefit immeasurable living beings,
and cause them to establish Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For the sake of purifying the Buddha lands,
he will constantly diligently teach and transform living beings,
gradually perfecting the Bodhisattva Path.
After passing through immeasurable asaṃkhya kalpas,
he will attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi in this land,
and will be named Fǎmíng Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara-puruṣadamyasarathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ, Buddha, Bhagavat.
That Buddha will use three thousand great thousand worlds, equal to the sands of the Ganges, as one Buddha land,
with the seven treasures as its ground.
The ground will be as level as the palm of a hand,
without mountains, hills, streams, or valleys.
Towers and pavilions of the seven treasures will fill it completely,
and the palaces of the devas will be close to the empty space,
with humans and devas interacting and seeing each other.
There will be no evil paths, and no women either.
All living beings will be born by transformation,
without any lust or desire.
They will attain great supernatural powers,
their bodies emitting light, freely flying about,
their minds steadfast, diligent, and wise,
all universally golden in color, adorned with the thirty-two marks.
The living beings in that land will always have two kinds of food:
first, the food of Dharma-joy,
second, the food of Dhyāna-bliss.
There will be immeasurable asaṃkhya millions of koṭis of nayutas of Bodhisattva assemblies,
having attained great supernatural powers and the Four Unimpeded Knowledges,
skillful in teaching and transforming all kinds of living beings.
The assembly of Śrāvakas will be so numerous that it cannot be known by calculation or reckoning.
All will have fully attained the Six Superknowledges, the Three Clarities, and the Eight Liberations.
That Buddha land
will be adorned and accomplished with such immeasurable meritorious virtues.
The kalpa will be named Bǎomíng,
and the land will be named Shànjìng.
That Buddha's lifespan
will be immeasurable asaṃkhya kalpas,
and the Dharma will abide for a very long time.
After the Buddha's Parinirvāṇa,
seven-treasure stupas will be erected, filling the entire land."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"Monks, listen carefully!
The path practiced by the Buddha-sons,
through skillful learning of expedient means,
is inconceivable.
Knowing that beings delight in small Dharmas,
and fear great wisdom,
therefore, the Bodhisattvas,
act as Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas,
with countless expedient means,
transforming all kinds of living beings.
They claim to be Śrāvakas,
far removed from the Buddha Path,
liberating immeasurable multitudes,
all of whom will attain accomplishment.
Though having small desires and laziness,
gradually, they will be caused to become Buddhas.
Inwardly, they conceal the Bodhisattva conduct,
outwardly, they appear as Śrāvakas,
with few desires and weary of birth and death,
truly purifying their own Buddha lands.
They show beings that they have the three poisons,
and also manifest the appearance of wrong views.
My disciples are like this,
skillfully liberating living beings.
If I were to fully describe
the various manifestations and transformations,
those beings who hear of this,
would then harbor doubts in their minds.
Now, this Fúlóunà,
in the past, with thousands of millions of Buddhas, diligently cultivated the path he practiced,
proclaiming and protecting the Dharmas of all the Buddhas.
For the sake of seeking unsurpassed wisdom,
and among all the Buddhas,
he appeared as the foremost of disciples,
greatly learned and wise.
What he says is fearless,
able to cause joy to others.
He has never been weary or tired,
and with this, he assists in the Buddhas' deeds.
He has already crossed over with great supernatural powers,
possessing the Four Unimpeded Knowledges,
knowing the sharpness and dullness of all faculties,
he constantly speaks of the pure Dharma.
Expounding and spreading such meaning,
he teaches thousands of millions of beings,
causing them to abide in the Great Vehicle Dharma,
and thus purifying his own Buddha land.
In the future, he will also make offerings to
immeasurable and countless Buddhas,
protecting and assisting in proclaiming the correct Dharma,
and also purifying his own Buddha land.
Constantly with all kinds of expedient means,
he preaches the Dharma without fear,
liberating uncountably many beings,
accomplishing all wisdom.
He makes offerings to all the Tathāgatas,
protecting and upholding the Dharma-treasure store,
and afterwards he will attain Buddhahood,
with the name Fǎmíng.
His land will be named Shànjìng,
composed of the seven treasures,
and the kalpa will be named Bǎomíng.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas will be very numerous,
their number immeasurable millions,
all having crossed over with great supernatural powers,
their majestic virtue and strength fully possessed,
filling his land.
The Śrāvakas will also be countless,
with the Three Clarities and Eight Liberations,
having attained the Four Unimpeded Knowledges,
and these will be his Saṃgha.
All the beings in that land,
have already severed lust and desire,
purely born by transformation,
adorned with bodies possessing the marks.
Their food is Dharma-joy and Dhyāna-bliss,
having no thought of any other food.
There are no women,
and no evil paths either.
The monk Fúlóunà,
his meritorious virtues are all complete and fulfilled,
and he will attain such a pure land,
with a very numerous assembly of sages and worthies.
Such immeasurable matters,
I now only speak of briefly."
At that time, the one thousand two hundred Arhats, those whose minds were at ease, thought to themselves:
"We are joyful, having obtained what we have never had before.
If the World-Honored One would each grant us a prediction, as with the other great disciples,
would that not be wonderful!"
The Buddha, knowing what these beings were thinking in their hearts,
said to Móhē Jiāshè:
"These one thousand two hundred Arhats,
I will now, in their presence, grant them the prediction of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi in order.
Among this assembly,
my great disciple, the monk Jiāochénrú,
will make offerings to sixty-two thousand koṭis of Buddhas,
and then attain Buddhahood,
with the name Pǔmíng Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara-puruṣadamyasarathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ, Buddha, Bhagavat.
Those five hundred Arhats:
Yōulóupínluó Jiāshè, Gāyé Jiāshè, Nàtí Jiāshè,
Jiālú Tuóyí, Yōutuóyí, Ānóulóutuó, Líbōduō, Jiébīnnà,
Bójūluó, Zhōutuó, Shāqié Tuó, and so on,
will all attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and all have the same name,
called Pǔmíng."
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"The monk Jiāochénrú,
will see immeasurable Buddhas,
and after passing through asaṃkhya kalpas,
will then accomplish perfect enlightenment.
He will constantly emit great light,
fully possessing all supernatural powers,
his name will be heard throughout the ten directions,
respected by all,
he will constantly speak of the unsurpassed path,
therefore, he is named Pǔmíng.
His land will be pure and clean,
the Bodhisattvas all courageous and fierce,
all ascending to wonderful pavilions,
traveling to all the lands of the ten directions,
with unsurpassed offerings,
they will present them to all the Buddhas.
Having made these offerings,
their hearts will be filled with great joy,
and in an instant, they will return to their original land,
possessing such supernatural power.
The Buddha's lifespan will be sixty thousand kalpas,
the Proper Dharma will abide for twice that long,
the Semblance Dharma will again be twice that long,
and when the Dharma disappears, the devas and humans will be sorrowful.
Those five hundred monks,
in order, will all become Buddhas,
with the same name Pǔmíng,
granting predictions in succession."
After my extinction,
a certain person, Mǒu Jiǎ, will become a Buddha,
and the world he transforms
will be like mine today.
The adornment and purity of his land,
as well as his various supernatural powers,
his assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas,
his True Dharma and Semblance Dharma,
and the length of his lifespan in kalpas,
will all be as described above.
Jiāshè, you already know
about the five hundred masters of self-mastery;
the remaining śrāvakas
will also be like this.
For those not present at this assembly,
you should proclaim this."
At that time, the five hundred Arhats,
having received their predictions before the Buddha,
were filled with joy and elation.
They immediately rose from their seats, went before the Buddha,
bowed their heads to the ground at his feet,
repented, and blamed themselves:
"World Honored One! We constantly held this thought,
thinking we had already attained ultimate extinction,
but now we know we were like ignorant people.
Why is this?
We should have attained the Tathāgata's wisdom,
but instead, we were content with our small wisdom.
World Honored One! It is like a person who goes to the house of a close friend and falls asleep drunk.
At that time, the friend has official business to attend to,
so he ties a priceless jewel inside the sleeping man's clothes and departs.
The man, drunk and asleep, is completely unaware.
When he wakes up, he travels to another country.
For the sake of clothing and food,
he toils and struggles, facing great hardship.
If he obtains even a little, he considers it enough.
Later, the friend meets him again
and says:
'Alas, sir!
Why do you toil so for clothing and food?
I wanted to give you ease and comfort, allowing you to indulge your five desires.
On such and such a date,
I tied a priceless jewel inside your clothes.
It is still there now,
but you do not know it.
You toil and worry, seeking to support yourself,
which is very foolish.
You can now trade this jewel for whatever you need,
and always have your wishes fulfilled, lacking nothing.'
The Buddha is also like this.
When you were a bodhisattva, you taught and transformed us,
causing us to aspire to the mind of all-knowing wisdom.
But we soon forgot and were unaware.
Having attained the path of Arhatship,
we considered ourselves extinguished,
our livelihood difficult,
satisfied with little.
But the vow of all-knowing wisdom remains, not lost.
Now the World Honored One awakens us,
saying:
'Monks!
What you have attained is not ultimate extinction.
For a long time, I caused you to plant roots of goodness for Buddhahood.
Through expedient means, I showed you the appearance of nirvāṇa,
but you thought
you had truly attained extinction.'
World Honored One!
Now I know
that we are truly bodhisattvas,
and will receive the prediction of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Because of this cause and condition, we are greatly joyful and have gained what we never had before."
At that time, Āruò Jiāochénrú and the others,
wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
We have heard the supreme, peaceful prophecy,
and are filled with joy as never before,
bowing to the Buddha of immeasurable wisdom.
Now before the World Honored One,
we repent all our faults and errors.
From the immeasurable Buddha jewel,
we obtained a small portion of nirvāṇa,
and like ignorant fools,
were content with ourselves.
It is like a poor man
who goes to the house of a close friend.
His friend's house is very wealthy,
and has prepared all kinds of delicacies.
He ties a priceless jewel
inside the poor man's clothes,
silently gives it and leaves.
The poor man sleeps unaware.
When the man wakes up,
he travels to another country,
seeking clothing and food to sustain himself.
His livelihood is very difficult,
and he is content with little,
no longer desiring anything better.
He is unaware that inside his clothes
there is a priceless jewel.
The friend who gave the jewel
later sees this poor man,
and after sternly rebuking him,
shows him the jewel tied to his clothes.
The poor man sees this jewel,
and his heart is filled with great joy.
He becomes rich with all kinds of wealth,
and indulges in the five desires.
We are also like this.
The World Honored One, throughout the long night,
always compassionately taught and transformed us,
causing us to plant the supreme aspiration.
Because of our ignorance,
we were unaware and did not know.
We obtained a small portion of nirvāṇa,
were content and did not seek anything more.
Now the Buddha awakens us,
saying that it is not true extinction.
Obtaining the Buddha's supreme wisdom,
that is then true extinction.
Now we hear from the Buddha
about the matter of the prediction's adornment,
and the successive predictions that follow.
Our bodies and minds are filled with joy.
At that time, Ānán and Luóhóuluó thought to themselves:
"We often think to ourselves:
'Wouldn't it be wonderful if we were to receive a prediction?' "
They immediately rose from their seats,
went before the Buddha, bowed their heads to the ground at his feet,
and together said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
We should also have a share in this.
Only the Tathāgata is our refuge.
Moreover, we are known and recognized by all the worlds of gods, humans, and asuras—
Ānán is always an attendant, protecting and upholding the Dharma treasury;
Luóhóuluó is the Buddha's son—
If the Buddha sees fit to grant us the prediction of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
our wishes will be fulfilled, and the expectations of the assembly will be satisfied."
At that time, two thousand disciples, śrāvakas who were still learning and those beyond learning,
all rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, went before the Buddha,
single-mindedly joined their palms, gazed up at the World Honored One,
as Ānán and Luóhóuluó wished,
and stood to one side.
At that time, the Buddha told Ānán:
"In the future, you will become a Buddha,

named Shānhǎi Huì Zìzài Tōng Wáng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Complete in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding of the World, Supreme Guide, Trainer of People, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World Honored One.
You will make offerings to sixty-two billion Buddhas, protect and uphold the Dharma treasury,
and then attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
You will teach and transform twenty koṭis of nayutas of trillions of gaṅgā sands of bodhisattvas,
causing them to attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Your country will be named Constantly Standing Victorious Banner;
its land will be pure, with lapis lazuli as its ground.
The kalpa will be named Wonderfully Resounding Everywhere.
The lifespan of that Buddha
will be immeasurable trillions of asaṃkhya kalpas.
If someone were to calculate and count throughout trillions of immeasurable asaṃkhya kalpas, they could not know its extent.
The True Dharma will abide in the world twice as long as his lifespan, and the Semblance Dharma will abide twice as long as the True Dharma.
Ānán!
This Buddha, Shānhǎi Huì Zìzài Tōng Wáng,
will be praised and extolled for his merits and virtues
by the countless trillions of gaṅgā sands of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, in the ten directions."
At that time, the World Honored One,
wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Now in the Saṃgha, I say,
that Ānán, the upholder of the Dharma,
will make offerings to all Buddhas,
and then achieve Perfect Enlightenment,
and will be named Shānhǎi Huì
Zìzài Tōng Wáng Buddha.
His country will be pure,
named Constantly Standing Victorious Banner.
He will teach and transform bodhisattvas,
their number like the sands of the Gaṅgā.
That Buddha will have great majestic virtue,
his name renowned throughout the ten directions.
His lifespan will be immeasurable,
because of his compassion for sentient beings.
The True Dharma will be twice his lifespan,
and the Semblance Dharma will be twice that again.
Like the sands of the Gaṅgā,
countless sentient beings,
in this Buddha's Dharma,
will plant the cause and condition for the Buddha path.
At that time, eight thousand newly aspiring bodhisattvas in the assembly
all thought to themselves:
"We have not even heard of great bodhisattvas receiving such a prediction.
What is the cause and condition
that these śrāvakas receive such a pronouncement?"
At that time, the World Honored One
knew what was in the minds of all the Bodhisattvas,
and told them, saying:
"Good men!
I and Ānánda 等 (děng),
at Kōngwáng Fó (空王佛) Buddha's place,
at the same time aroused the mind of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Ānánda (阿難) always loved to hear much,
I always diligently persevered,
therefore I have already attained Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and Ānánda (阿難) protects and upholds my Dharma,
also protects the Dharma treasury of future Buddhas,
teaches and perfects all the Bodhisattva assemblies,
his original vow was thus,
therefore he obtained this prediction."
Ānánda (阿難) in front of the Buddha,
personally heard the prediction and the adornment of the land,
his wishes were fulfilled,
his heart greatly rejoiced, gaining what he had never had before.
Immediately he recalled the past immeasurable millions of billions of Buddhas' Dharma treasuries,
penetrating and unobstructed, like what he heard today,
and also recognized his original vow.
At that time, Ānánda (阿難)
spoke in verse, saying:
"The World Honored One is extremely rare,
causing me to remember the past,
the immeasurable Buddhas' Dharmas,
like what I hear today.
I now have no more doubts,
dwelling in the Buddha path,
skillfully being a attendant,
protecting and upholding all the Buddhas' Dharmas."
At that time, the Buddha told Luóhóuluó (羅睺羅):
"In the future, you will become a Buddha,

named Dǎo Qī Bǎo Huá Rúlái (蹈七寶華如來), Worthy of Offerings, Fully Aware, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World Honored One.
You will make offerings to Buddhas and Tathāgatas as numerous as the dust particles in ten world systems,
and will always be the eldest son of the Buddhas,
just as you are now.
This Dǎo Qī Bǎo Huá Fó (蹈七寶華佛) Buddha's land will be adorned,
the duration of his life and kalpas,
the disciples he will transform,
the True Dharma, the Semblance Dharma,
will also be no different from Shānhǎi Huì Zìzài Tōng Wáng Rúlái (山海慧自在通王如來),
and you will also be the eldest son of this Buddha.
After this, you will attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, the World Honored One,
wanting to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"When I was a prince,
Luóhóuluó (羅睺羅) was my eldest son,
Now that I have attained Buddhahood,
he receives the Dharma and becomes my Dharma son.
In the future world,
he will see immeasurable billions of Buddhas,
and will always be their eldest son,
single-mindedly seeking the Buddha path.
Luóhóuluó's (羅睺羅) secret practices,
only I can know,
Now he appears as my eldest son,
to show all sentient beings.
Immeasurable billions of tens of millions,
his merits are countless,
He dwells in the Buddha Dharma,
seeking the unsurpassed path."
At that time, the World Honored One
saw two thousand people in the states of learning and no-learning, their minds gentle, still and pure, single-mindedly contemplating the Buddha.
The Buddha told Ānánda (阿難):
"Do you see these two thousand people in the states of learning and no-learning?"
"Yes, I see them."
"Ānánda (阿難)!
These people,
will make offerings to Buddhas and Tathāgatas as numerous as the dust particles in fifty world systems,
revering and respecting them,
protecting and upholding the Dharma treasury.
Eventually, at the same time, in the ten directions, they will each attain Buddhahood,
all with the same name,
named Bǎoxiàng Rúlái (寶相如來), Worthy of Offerings, Fully Aware,
Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understanding the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha,
World Honored One.
Their life span will be one kalpa.
Their land will be adorned, the Śrāvakas, Bodhisattvas, True Dharma,
and Semblance Dharma, will all be equal."
At that time, the World Honored One, wanting to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"These two thousand Śrāvakas,
now dwell before me,
I will give them all predictions,
that in the future they will become Buddhas.
The Buddhas they will make offerings to,
are as numerous as the dust particles described above,
They will protect and uphold their Dharma treasury,
and later they will attain Perfect Enlightenment.
Each in the ten directions,
all with the same name,
simultaneously sitting at the Bodhi-maṇḍa,
to realize unsurpassed wisdom,
all named Bǎoxiàng (寶相).
Their lands and disciples,
the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma,
will all be equal without difference.
All with their spiritual powers,
will liberate sentient beings in the ten directions,
Their names will be universally known,
and gradually they will enter Nirvāṇa."
At that time, the two thousand people in the states of learning and no-learning,
hearing the Buddha's prediction,
rejoiced and leapt for joy,
and spoke in verse, saying:
"The World Honored One's lamp of wisdom shines brightly,
We hear the sound of the prediction,
Our hearts are filled with joy,
as if sprinkled with sweet dew."
At that time, the World Honored One, because of the Boddhisattva Yàowáng (藥王),
told the eighty thousand great beings:
"Yàowáng (藥王)!
Do you see in this great assembly,
the immeasurable devas, dragon kings, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
and bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, those seeking to become Śrāvakas,
those seeking to become Pratyekabuddhas, those seeking the Buddha path,
such beings as these,
all before the Buddha,
hearing one verse or one line of the wonderful *Lotus Sūtra*,
even for a moment rejoicing with them,
I will give them all a prediction,
that they will attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi."
The Buddha told Yàowáng (藥王):
"Also, after the Tathāgata enters Parinirvāṇa,
if someone hears the wonderful *Lotus Sūtra*,
even one verse or one line,
for a moment rejoicing with them,
I will also give them the prediction of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, if someone
receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, or copies the wonderful *Lotus Sūtra*,
even one verse,
regards this scripture roll with reverence as if it were the Buddha,
and makes various offerings—flowers, incense, garlands,
powdered incense, scented paste, burning incense, silken canopies, banners, clothing, music,
even putting their palms together respectfully.
Yàowáng (藥王)!
You should know that these people
have already made offerings to hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
have fulfilled great vows in the presence of all the Buddhas,
and out of compassion for sentient beings,
have been born in this human world.
Yàowáng (藥王)!
If someone asks: 'What kind of beings will become Buddhas in the future?'
You should show them: 'These people will certainly become Buddhas in the future.'
Why is this?
If good men or good women,
with regard to the *Lotus Sūtra*, even one line, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, or copy it,
and make various offerings to the scripture roll—flowers, incense, garlands, powdered incense, scented paste, burning incense, silken canopies, banners, clothing, music,
and put their palms together respectfully;
then these people should be revered and honored by all the world,
and should be offered the same offerings as one would offer to a Tathāgata.
Know that this person is a great Bodhisattva,
who has attained Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and out of compassion for sentient beings,
has vowed to be born here,
to widely expound and differentiate the wonderful *Lotus Sūtra*.
How much more so those who can fully receive, uphold, and make various offerings?
Yàowáng (藥王)!
You should know that these people,
abandoning their own pure karmic reward,
after my Parinirvāṇa,
out of compassion for sentient beings,
are born in an evil world,
to widely expound this scripture.
If there are good men or good women,
after my Parinirvāṇa,
who can secretly speak the *Lotus Sūtra* for even one person,
even one line;
know that these people are messengers of the Tathāgata,
sent by the Tathāgata, doing the Tathāgata's work.
How much more so those who widely speak for others in a great assembly?
Yàowáng (藥王)!
If there are evil people, with unkind hearts,
who for one kalpa constantly revile the Buddha in the Buddha's presence,
their offense is still light;
if someone with one evil word,
criticizes those who, whether lay or monastic, read and recite the *Lotus Sūtra*,
their offense is extremely heavy."
Yàowáng!
If there are those who read and recite the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
you should know that these people adorn themselves with the adornments of the Buddha,
and thus become those borne by the Tathāgata on his shoulders.
Wherever they go,
you should face them and bow,
with one mind joining your palms,
respectfully making offerings,
honoring and praising them with flowers, incense, necklaces,
powdered incense, fragrant oils, burning incense, silk canopies, banners, clothing, delicacies, and making all kinds of music,
the highest offerings among people, and make offerings to them,
you should hold heavenly treasures and scatter them upon them,
heavenly treasures should be offered to them.
Why is this?
Because these people joyfully expound the Dharma,
and hearing it even for a moment,
one immediately attains ultimate *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí*.」
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
If you wish to abide in the Buddha-path,
and attain natural wisdom,
you should always diligently make offerings to
those who receive and uphold the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*.
If there are those who wish to quickly obtain
all kinds of wisdom,
they should receive and uphold this *jīng*,
and also make offerings to those who uphold it.
If there are those who can receive and uphold
the wonderful *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
you should know that they are messengers of the Buddha,
compassionate towards all sentient beings.
If there are those who can receive and uphold
the wonderful *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
they abandon their pure lands,
and are born here out of compassion for beings.
You should know that such people
are free to be born wherever they wish,
and are able to widely expound the unsurpassed Dharma
in this evil world.
You should use heavenly flowers and incense,
as well as heavenly treasure clothing,
and heavenly collections of precious treasures,
to make offerings to those who expound the Dharma.
In the evil world after my extinction,
those who can uphold this *jīng*,
should join their palms and bow in reverence,
as if making offerings to the World-Honored One.
Offer the finest delicacies and the most delicious flavors,
as well as all kinds of clothing,
to make offerings to these children of the Buddha,
hoping to hear them for even a moment.
If one can in a later age
receive and uphold this *jīng*,
I send them into the world,
to perform the deeds of the Tathāgata.
If for one *jié*,
one constantly harbors unkind thoughts,
making faces and cursing the Buddha,
one incurs immeasurable grave offenses.
If there are those who read, recite, and uphold
this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
and for a moment add evil words,
their offense is even greater than that.
If someone seeks the Buddha-path,
and for one *jié*,
joins their palms before me,
and praises me with countless verses,
because of praising the Buddha in this way,
they attain immeasurable merits,
but praising those who uphold the *jīng*,
their blessings are even greater than that.
For eighty billion *jié*,
with the most wonderful sights and sounds,
as well as fragrances, tastes, and textures,
make offerings to those who uphold the *jīng*.
Having made such offerings,
if one obtains even a moment of hearing,
then one should rejoice,
"I have now obtained great benefit."
Yàowáng, I now tell you,
among all the *jīng*s I have spoken,
in this *jīng*,
the *Fǎ Huá* is the most supreme.
At that time, the Buddha further addressed the *púsà mó诃sà* Yàowáng:
"The *jīngdiǎn*s that I have spoken are countless, tens of millions, billions;
those already spoken, those now spoken, and those to be spoken, but among them, this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* is the most difficult to believe and understand.
Yàowáng!
This *jīng* is the secret treasury of all the Buddhas,
it should not be distributed and rashly given to others;
it is guarded by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
and from ancient times until now, it has never been openly spoken.
And this *jīng*, even when the Tathāgata is present, still attracts much resentment and jealousy,
how much more so after my extinction?
Yàowáng!
You should know that after the Tathāgata's extinction,
those who can write, uphold, read, recite, make offerings, and speak it for others,
the Tathāgata will cover them with his robe,
and they will also be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of other directions who are now present.
These people have great power of faith,
as well as power of aspiration and the power of all good roots.
You should know that these people dwell together with the Tathāgata,
and the Tathāgata will pat their heads.
Yàowáng!
In every place, whether speaking, reading, reciting, or writing,
wherever the *jīng* scroll is kept, one should erect a seven-treasure pagoda,
making it extremely tall, broad, and adorned,
without needing to further enshrine *shèlì*.
Why is this?
Because within it is already the complete body of the Tathāgata.
This pagoda should be offered with all kinds of flowers, incense, necklaces, silk canopies,
banners, music, and songs, paying homage respectfully,
honoring and praising it.
If someone is able to see this pagoda and bow in reverence and make offerings,
you should know that these people are all close to *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí*.
Yàowáng!
Many people, whether at home
or having left home, practice the *púsà* path, but if they are unable to see, hear, read, recite, write, uphold,
or make offerings to this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*, you should know that these people have not practiced the *púsà* path well;
if there are those who can hear this *jīngdiǎn*, then they are able to practice the *púsà* path well.
If there are sentient beings who seek the Buddha-path, and see or hear this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
and after hearing it, believe, understand, receive, and uphold it, you should know that these people are close to *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí*.
Yàowáng!
For example, if someone is thirsty and needs water,
and digs in the highlands seeking it,
and still sees dry earth, they know the water is still far away;
but continuing their efforts without stopping,
they gradually see damp earth,
and then gradually reach mud,
their mind is certain,
and they know the water must be near.
The *púsà* is also like this;
if they have not heard, understood,
or been able to cultivate and practice this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
you should know that these people are still far from *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí*;
if they are able to hear, understand, contemplate, and cultivate it,
they will certainly know that they are close to *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí*.
Why is this?
All *púsà*s' *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎo Sānpútí* belongs to this *jīng*--
this *jīng* opens the gate of expedient means and reveals the true aspect.
This *Fǎ Huá Jīng* treasury is deep, firm, secluded, and far-reaching, and no one can reach it,
but now the Buddha teaches and transforms those accomplished *púsà*s and opens it for them.
Yàowáng!
If there are *púsà*s who hear this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*
and are startled, doubtful, and fearful,
you should know that they are newly aspiring *púsà*s;
if *shēngwén*s hear this *jīng*
and are startled, doubtful, and fearful,
you should know that they are those with increased arrogance.
Yàowáng!
If there are good men and good women,
after the Tathāgata's extinction,
who wish to expound this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* for the four assemblies,
how should they expound it?
These good men and good women should enter the Tathāgata's room,
wear the Tathāgata's robe, and sit on the Tathāgata's seat,
and then they should widely expound this *jīng* for the four assemblies.
The Tathāgata's room
is the great compassionate mind towards all sentient beings;
the Tathāgata's robe is the gentle and patient mind;
the Tathāgata's seat is the emptiness of all *fǎ*.
Abiding in this,
then with an unremitting mind,
widely expound this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* for the *púsà*s and the four assemblies.
"Yàowáng!
In other lands, I send transformation people to gather an assembly to listen to the Dharma,
and I also send transformation *bǐqiū*s, *bǐqiūní*s, *yōupósè*s, and *yōupóyí*s to listen to their expounding of the Dharma;
these transformation people, hearing the Dharma, believe and accept it, complying and not opposing.
If the Dharma expounder is in a secluded place,
I then widely send *tiān*, *lóng*, ghosts, gods, *qiántuópó*, *āxiūluó*, etc., to listen to their expounding of the Dharma.
Although I am in another land,
I often cause the Dharma expounder to see my body.
If they forget phrases or clauses in this *jīng*, I will speak them again for them,
causing them to be complete."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
If you wish to abandon all laziness,
you should listen to this *jīng*;
this *jīng* is difficult to hear,
and it is also difficult for those who believe and accept it.
Like a person thirsty for water,
digging in the highlands,
and still seeing dry earth,
they know they are still far from water;
gradually seeing damp earth and mud,
they definitely know they are near water.
Yàowáng, you should know!
Such people as these,
not hearing the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
are very far from the Buddha's wisdom;
if they hear this profound *jīng*,
they will definitely understand the *shēngwén* Dharma.
This is the king of all *jīng*s,
and after hearing it, earnestly contemplate it,
you should know that these people
are close to the Buddha's wisdom.
If a person speaks this sūtra,
they should enter the Tathāgata's chamber,
wear the Tathāgata's robe,
and sit on the Tathāgata's seat,
being fearless in the assembly,
widely explaining and distinguishing.
Great compassion is the chamber,
gentleness and forbearance the robe,
the emptiness of all dharmas the seat;
abiding in this is speaking the Dharma.
If, when speaking this sūtra,
someone curses with evil words,
adds knives, staves, tiles, and stones,
one should for the sake of remembering the Buddha endure.
In my millions of billions of lands,
I manifest a pure, firm body,
for countless billions of kalpas,
speaking the Dharma for sentient beings.
If, after my parinirvāṇa,
there is one who can speak this sūtra,
I will send manifested four assemblies,
*bǐqiū*, *bǐqiūní*,
and pure believing men and women,
to make offerings to the Dharma master,
to guide all sentient beings,
gathering them to listen to the Dharma.
If a person wishes to add evil,
knives, staves, tiles, and stones,
then I will send manifested people,
to act as protectors for them.
If the person speaking the Dharma,
is alone in an empty, quiet place,
solitary with no human sound,
reciting this scripture,
at that time I will manifest
a pure, bright body.
If they forget phrases and sentences,
I will speak them to make them clear and fluent.
If a person possesses these virtues,
or speaks for the four assemblies,
or recites the scripture in an empty place,
all will be able to see my body.
If a person is in an empty, quiet place,
I will send *tiānlóngwáng*,
*yèchā*, ghost spirits, and others,
to act as an assembly listening to the Dharma.
This person delights in speaking the Dharma,
distinguishing without hindrance,
because the Buddhas protect and remember them,
they are able to make the great assembly rejoice.
If one is close to the Dharma master,
one quickly attains the Bodhisattva path,
following this teacher's learning,
one is able to see Ganges-sand Buddhas.
At that time, in front of the Buddha was a seven-jeweled pagoda,
five hundred *yóuxún* high,
and two hundred and fifty *yóuxún* wide and broad,
emerging from the earth and abiding in the air,
adorned with all kinds of jewels.
Five thousand railings,
ten million niches,
countless banners and streamers were used as adornments,
draping jeweled necklaces and hanging billions of jeweled bells above it.
From all four sides emerged the fragrance of *duōmóluóbá zhāntán*, pervading the world.
The banners and canopies were made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *chēqú*, agate, pearl, rose quartz, and the seven jewels,
reaching as high as the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings.
The *sānshísāntiān* rained *tiānmàntuóluóhuā*,
making offerings to the jeweled pagoda.
The remaining devas, *lóng*, *yèchā*,
*qiántápó*, *āxiūluó*, *jiālóuluó*, *jǐnnàluó*, *móhóuluóqié*, human and non-human beings,
in the millions and billions,
with all kinds of flowers, incense, necklaces, banners, canopies, and music,
made offerings to the jeweled pagoda,
respectfully, reverently, and praisingly.
At that time, from within the jeweled pagoda, a great voice emerged, exclaiming:
"Excellent, excellent! Śākyamuni, World-Honored One!
Able to use equal great wisdom
to teach the Bodhisattva Dharma,
the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*, protected by the Buddhas,
for the great assembly."
"Thus it is, thus it is! Śākyamuni, World-Honored One!
What you have spoken is all true."
At that time, the four assemblies,
seeing the great jeweled pagoda abiding in the air,
and also hearing the sound emerging from within the pagoda,
all obtained Dharma joy,
marveling at what had never been before,
rose from their seats,
respectfully joining their palms,
and stood aside.
At that time, there was a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Dàlèshuō,
knowing the doubts in the minds of all the worlds' devas, humans, *āxiūluó*, and others,
and said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! Due to what cause and condition does this jeweled pagoda emerge from the earth,
and also emit this sound from within it?"
At that time, the Buddha told the Dàlèshuō Bodhisattva:
"Within this jeweled pagoda is the whole body of a Tathāgata,
from the infinitely many millions of billions of *āsēngqí* worlds to the east in the past,
in a country named Bǎojìng,
there was a Buddha named Duōbǎo.
When that Buddha was practicing the Bodhisattva path,
he made a great vow:
'If, after I become a Buddha and enter parinirvāṇa,
in any of the ten directions' lands there is a place where the *Fǎhuá Jīng* is spoken,
my stupa and temple,
for the sake of listening to this sūtra,
will emerge before it,
to act as proof,
and praise, saying, "Excellent!"'
"After that Buddha attained enlightenment,
when approaching parinirvāṇa,
he told all the *bǐqiū* in the assembly of devas and humans:
'After my parinirvāṇa,
if there are those who wish to make offerings to my whole body,
they should erect a great pagoda.'
That Buddha, with the power of his supernatural vow,
in the worlds of the ten directions,
in every place,
if there is one who speaks the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
that jeweled pagoda will emerge before it,
his whole body being within the pagoda,
praising, saying: 'Excellent, excellent!'
"Dàlèshuō!
Now Duōbǎo Tathāgata's pagoda,
because it heard the *Fǎhuá Jīng* being spoken,
emerged from the earth, praising, saying:
'Excellent, excellent!' "
At that time, the Dàlèshuō Bodhisattva,
due to the Tathāgata's spiritual power,
said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
We wish to see this Buddha's body."
The Buddha told the Dàlèshuō Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
"This Duōbǎo Buddha
has a profound and weighty vow:
'If my jeweled pagoda,
for the sake of listening to the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
emerges before all the Buddhas,
if there are those who wish to show my body to the four assemblies,
the division-body Buddhas of that Buddha—
speaking the Dharma in the worlds of the ten directions,
must all return and gather in one place,
then my body will appear.'
"Dàlèshuō!
My division-body Buddhas—
speaking the Dharma in the worlds of the ten directions,
should now gather."
Dàlèshuō said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
We also wish to see the World-Honored One's division-body Buddhas,
to bow and make offerings."
At that time, the Buddha emitted a white hair-mark light,
and immediately saw the Buddhas in the lands to the east, as many as five million billion *nàyōutā* Ganges sands,
those lands were all made of crystal as the ground,
adorned with jeweled trees and jeweled robes,
countless millions of billions of Bodhisattvas filling them,
spreading jeweled canopies everywhere,
with jeweled nets covering them.
The Buddhas of those lands, with great, wondrous sounds, spoke all the Dharmas,
and saw countless millions of billions of Bodhisattvas, filling all the lands,
speaking the Dharma for the assemblies.
To the south, north, west, the four intermediate directions, above, and below,
wherever the light of the white hair-mark shone,
it was also like this.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions each told the Bodhisattvas of their assemblies:
"Good men! I should now go to the Sahā world,
to Śākyamuni Buddha's place,
and make offerings to Duōbǎo Tathāgata's jeweled pagoda."
At that time, the Sahā world immediately transformed into purity,
with crystal as the ground,
adorned with jeweled trees,
with golden ropes marking the eight paths,
without any settlements, villages, towns, cities, great seas, rivers, mountains, forests, or thickets.
Burning great, jeweled incense,
*màntuóluóhuā* were spread everywhere on the ground,
with jeweled nets and canopies covering them,
hanging all kinds of jeweled bells.
Only this assembly was left,
all the devas and humans were moved to other lands.
At that time, all the Buddhas each brought a great Bodhisattva as an attendant,
to the Sahā world,
each arriving at the foot of a jeweled tree.
Each jeweled tree was five hundred *yóuxún* high,
its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits adorned in an orderly manner,
under each jeweled tree was a lion's seat, five *yóuxún* high,
also adorned with great jewels.
At that time, all the Buddhas, each on this seat,
sat in the lotus position.
In this way, they gradually filled the three-thousand-great-thousand world,
and the division-bodies on Śākyamuni Buddha's one side were still not completely there.
At that time, Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛,
desiring to accommodate the various Buddhas who were his emanations,
in each of the eight directions, transformed two million myriad nayuta countries,
making them all pure,
without hells, hungry ghosts, animals, or asuras,
and moving the gods and humans to other lands.
The lands that were transformed
also used lapis lazuli as their ground, adorned with jeweled trees,
the trees being five hundred *yóuxùn 由旬* in height,
their branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits decorated in order,
and under each tree was a jeweled lion throne,
five *yóuxùn 由旬* in height,
decorated with various jewels.
There were also no great seas or rivers,
nor Mount Mùzhēnlintuóshān 目真隣陀山,
Mount Móhē Mùzhēnlintuóshān 摩訶目真隣陀山, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, Mount Xūmíshān 須彌山, or other mountain kings,
all becoming one Buddha land.
The jeweled ground was level and even,
and jeweled-interwoven canopies covered it entirely;
banners and canopies were hung,
great jeweled incense was burned,
and the jeweled flowers of the gods covered the ground.
Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛, for the sake of the Buddhas who were to come and sit,
again transformed two million myriad nayuta countries in each of the eight directions,
making them all pure,
without hells, hungry ghosts, animals, or asuras,
and moving the gods and humans to other lands.
The lands that were transformed
also used lapis lazuli as their ground,
adorned with jeweled trees,
the trees being five hundred *yóuxùn 由旬* in height, their branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits adorned in order,
and under each tree was a jeweled lion throne,
five *yóuxùn 由旬* in height,
also decorated with great jewels.
There were also no great seas or rivers,
nor Mount Mùzhēnlintuóshān 目真隣陀山, Mount Móhē Mùzhēnlintuóshān 摩訶目真隣陀山, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, Mount Xūmíshān 須彌山, or other mountain kings,
all becoming one Buddha land. The jeweled ground was level and even,
and jeweled-interwoven canopies covered it entirely;
banners and canopies were hung,
great jeweled incense was burned,
and the jeweled flowers of the gods covered the ground.
At that time, the Buddhas who were emanations of Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛 in the eastern direction,
from hundreds of thousands of myriads of millions of *Hénghéshā 恆河沙*-like lands,
each expounding the Dharma,
came and gathered here;
in this order, the Buddhas of the ten directions all came and gathered,
sitting in the eight directions.
At that time, in each direction, four hundred myriad millions of nayuta lands were filled with Buddhas, *Rúlái 如來*.
At this time, the Buddhas were each under a jeweled tree, sitting on a lion throne,
each sending attendants to inquire after Shìjiāmóunífó’s 釋迦牟尼佛 well-being,
each carrying a handful of jeweled flowers, and saying:
"Good man!
Go to Mount Qíshéjuéshān 耆闍崛山, to the place of Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛,
and say to him as I say:
'Are you free from illness and trouble, and are your strength and happiness secure,
and are the bodhisattvas and *shēngwén 聲聞* assembly all peaceful and safe?'
Scatter these jeweled flowers to offer to the Buddha, and say these words:
'That certain Buddha desires to open this jeweled pagoda.'"
The Buddhas sent their messengers, and so it was.
At that time, Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛,
seeing that all the Buddhas who were his emanations had come and gathered,
each sitting on a lion throne,
and hearing that all the Buddhas together desired to open the jeweled pagoda,
immediately arose from his seat
and stood in the empty sky.
All the four assemblies stood up, put their palms together,
and single-mindedly gazed at the Buddha.
Thereupon, Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛 used his right finger to open the door of the seven-jeweled pagoda,
emitting a great sound,
like unlocking a bolt and opening the gate of a great city.
Immediately, all the assembly
saw Duōbǎo Rúlái 多寶如來 inside the jeweled pagoda, sitting on a lion throne,
his entire body intact,
as if in meditation.
They also heard him say:
"Excellent, excellent! Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛!
Quickly speak this *Fǎhuá Jīng 法華經*;
I have come here to listen to this sutra."
At that time, the four assemblies,
seeing a Buddha who had passed into extinction countless millions of myriads of *jié 劫* ago speaking such words,
marveled that such a thing had never happened before,
and with clusters of heavenly jeweled flowers,
scattered them on Duōbǎo Fó 多寶佛 and Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛.
At that time, Duōbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
divided his half of the seat in the jeweled pagoda with Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛, and said:
"Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛! Please take this seat."
Immediately, Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛 entered the pagoda,
sat on the half-seat,
and sat in the lotus position.
At that time, the great assembly
saw the two *Rúlái 如來* in the seven-jeweled pagoda on the lion throne, sitting in the lotus position,
and each thought:
"The Buddha's seat is high and far away;
we only wish that the *Rúlái 如來* would use his supernatural power
to cause us all to be in the empty sky."
Immediately, Shìjiāmóunífó 釋迦牟尼佛, with his supernatural power,
took all the great assembly into the empty sky,
and with a great voice proclaimed to the four assemblies:
"Who can widely speak this wonderful *Fǎhuá Jīng 法華經* in this Sahā world?
Now is the right time.
The *Rúlái 如來* will soon enter *nièpán 涅槃*;
the Buddha wishes to entrust this wonderful *Fǎhuá Jīng 法華經* to someone."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
The holy lord, the World Honored One,
though long since passed into extinction,
in the jeweled pagoda,
still comes for the sake of the Dharma.
How can you people
not diligently act for the sake of the Dharma?
This Buddha passed into extinction
countless *jié 劫* ago,
and everywhere listens to the Dharma,
because it is difficult to encounter.
That Buddha's original vow is that,
after my extinction,
wherever he goes,
he will always listen to the Dharma.
And my emanations,
countless Buddhas,
like the sands of the *Héng Hé 恆河*,
come desiring to listen to the Dharma,
and to see the extinction of Duōbǎo Rúlái 多寶如來.
Each gives up their wonderful lands,
and disciples,
gods, humans, dragons, and spirits,
and all offerings,
to make the Dharma long endure;
therefore, they come to this place.
For the sake of seating the Buddhas,
with supernatural power,
I move countless beings,
making the countries pure.
The Buddhas each
like pure ponds,
adorned with lotuses.
Under those jeweled trees
the Buddhas sit upon them,
their light adorning them,
like in the darkness of night,
a great torch is lit.
From their bodies emanates a wonderful fragrance,
pervading the ten directions,
and the beings who are熏蒙
are overjoyed beyond themselves.
It is like a great wind
blowing on small branches.
With this expedient means,
I make the Dharma long endure.
I tell the great assembly:
'After my extinction,
who can protect and uphold, read and recite this sutra?
Now, before the Buddha,
speak your vows yourselves.'
That Duōbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
though long since passed into extinction,
with his great vow,
roars like a lion.
Duōbǎo Rúlái 多寶如來,
and my body,
and the Buddhas that I have emanated,
you should know this intent.
All you sons of the Buddha,
who can protect the Dharma?
You should make a great vow,
to cause it to long endure.
Those who can protect
this sutra and Dharma,
will be making offerings
to me and Duōbǎo 多寶.
This Duōbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
dwells in the jeweled pagoda,
constantly traveling in the ten directions.
For the sake of this sutra,
he also makes offerings
to all the Buddhas who come as emanations,
adorning and illuminating
all the worlds.
If you speak this sutra,
you will be seeing me,
Duōbǎo Rúlái 多寶如來,
and all the emanated Buddhas.
All you good men!
Carefully consider this;
this is a difficult thing,
you should make a great vow.
The other sutras,
as numerous as the sands of the *Héng Hé 恆河*,
though you speak of these,
it would not be difficult enough.
If you take Mount Xūmí 須彌,
and throw it to another direction,
to countless Buddha lands,
that would also not be difficult enough.
If with a toe,
you move a great thousand worlds,
and throw it far away to another country,
that would also not be difficult enough.
If one establishes oneself on the summit,
and for the multitude expounds
limitless other sūtras,
that would not be difficult.
If, after the Buddha's extinction,
in an evil age,
one can speak this sūtra,
that would be difficult.
Suppose someone
grasps the empty sky
and travels with it,
that would not be difficult.
After my extinction,
if one personally writes and upholds,
or causes others to write,
that would be difficult.
If one takes the great earth,
places it on one's toenail,
and ascends to the Brahmā heaven,
that would not be difficult.
After the Buddha's extinction,
in an evil age,
to briefly read this sūtra,
that would be difficult.
Suppose a kalpa is burning,
and one carries dry grass
into it without being burned,
that would not be difficult.
After my extinction,
if one upholds this sūtra
and speaks it for even one person,
that would be difficult.
If one upholds the eighty-four thousand collections of teachings,
the twelve divisions of sūtras,
and expounds them for others,
causing all who listen
to attain the six superknowledges,
even if one could do so,
that would not be difficult.
After my extinction,
to listen and receive this sūtra,
and inquire into its meaning and purpose,
that would be difficult.
If someone speaks the Dharma,
causing millions upon millions,
countless, immeasurable, numerous as the sands of the Ganges River,
living beings
to attain arhatship,
even with such benefit,
that would not be difficult.
After my extinction,
if one can reverently uphold
such a sūtra as this,
that would be difficult.
For the sake of the Buddha path,
in countless lands,
from the beginning until now,
I have extensively spoken various sūtras,
and among them,
this sūtra is the foremost.
If one can uphold it,
it is to uphold the Buddha's body.
Good men!
After my extinction,
who can receive, uphold,
and recite this sūtra?
Now, before the Buddha,
make a vow yourself.
This sūtra is difficult to uphold;
if one temporarily upholds it,
I will be delighted,
and so will all the Buddhas.
Such a person
is praised by all the Buddhas.
This is courageous,
this is diligent,
this is called upholding precepts,
practicing dhūta;
one will quickly attain
unsurpassed Buddhahood.
To be able to read and uphold this sūtra in the future age,
is to be a true Buddha-child,
dwelling in a pure and virtuous land.
After the Buddha's extinction,
to be able to understand its meaning,
is to be the eye of all gods and humans,
in the world.
In a fearful world,
to be able to speak it for even a moment,
all gods and humans
should make offerings.'
At that time, the Buddha told the bodhisattvas and the fourfold assembly of gods and humans:
"In the past, during immeasurable kalpas,
I sought the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* without懈惓.
For many kalpas, I constantly acted as king,
making a vow to seek unsurpassed *Pútí*,
with a mind that did not退轉.
Desiring to fulfill the six *bōluómì*,
I diligently practiced giving,
with a mind without悋惜,
elephants, horses, the seven treasures, countries, cities, wives, children, servants, attendants,
heads, eyes, marrow, brains,
bodies, flesh, hands, feet,
not sparing my life.
At that time, people's lifespans were immeasurable;
for the sake of the Dharma,
I relinquished my position as king,
entrusting the government to the crown prince,
and beating the drum, I proclaimed
in all directions, seeking the Dharma:
'Who can explain the Great Vehicle for me?
I will provide for their needs and serve them for life.'"
At that time, a hermit came and said to the king:
"I have the Great Vehicle,
named *Miào Fǎ Huá Jīng*.
If you do not disobey me,
I will expound it for you."
The king heard the hermit's words,
and was overjoyed,
and immediately followed the hermit,
providing for his needs——
gathering fruit, drawing water, collecting firewood, preparing food,
even using his body as a bed and seat——
his body and mind without惓,
serving him at that time. After a thousand years,
for the sake of the Dharma,
I diligently served him,
ensuring that he lacked nothing."
Then the World-Honored One, desiring to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"I recall the past kalpas,
for the sake of seeking the Great Dharma,
though acting as a king in the world,
I did not crave the pleasures of the five desires.
Striking the bell, I announced in all directions,
'Who has the Great Dharma?
If they explain it for me,
I will serve them as a slave.'
At that time, the hermit *Āsí*
came and spoke to the great king:
'I have a subtle and wondrous Dharma,
rare in the world.
If you can practice it,
I will explain it for you.'
The king heard the hermit's words,
and great joy arose in his heart,
and immediately followed the hermit,
providing for his needs,
gathering firewood and fruits,
respectfully giving them at the appropriate time,
with his heart focused on the wondrous Dharma,
his body and mind without懈惓.
Universally for all living beings,
he diligently sought the Great Dharma,
not for his own sake,
nor for the pleasures of the five desires.
Therefore, as a great king,
he diligently sought and obtained this Dharma,
thereby attaining Buddhahood,
and now I explain it for you."
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"The king at that time was my very self;
the hermit at that time is the present *Típó Dáduō*.
Because of *Típó Dáduō*'s good knowledge,
I was able to perfect the six *bōluómì*,
loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity,
the thirty-two marks,
the eighty minor characteristics,
the color of refined gold,
the ten powers,
the four fearlessnesses,
the four means of attraction,
the eighteen unshared divine powers,
attained perfect enlightenment, and extensively liberated living beings,
all because of *Típó Dáduō*'s good knowledge."
He told the four assemblies:
"*Típó Dáduō*, after passing through countless kalpas in the future,
will attain Buddhahood,

named *Tiānwáng Rúlái*, worthy of offerings, perfectly and completely enlightened, perfect in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, understanding the world, unsurpassed, taming hero, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
His world will be named *Tiāndào*.
At that time, *Tiānwáng* Buddha will dwell in the world for twenty middle kalpas,
extensively speaking the wondrous Dharma for living beings,
living beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River will attain the fruit of arhatship,
countless living beings will awaken the mind of a *pratyekabuddha*,
living beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River will awaken the unsurpassed *bodhi*-mind,
attaining 無生忍,
reaching non-retrogression.
After *Tiānwáng* Buddha enters *nirvāṇa*,
the Right Dharma will abide in the world for twenty middle kalpas.
A seven-jeweled pagoda will be erected for his whole-body relics,
sixty *yóuxún* high,
and forty *yóuxún* in breadth and width,
and all the gods and people will offer miscellaneous flowers, powdered incense, burning incense, perfumed incense, clothing, necklaces, banners, canopies, music, and songs,
bowing and making offerings to the wondrous seven-jeweled pagoda.
Countless living beings will attain the fruit of arhatship,
countless living beings will awaken to being a *pratyekabuddha*,
inconceivable living beings will awaken the *bodhi*-mind,
reaching non-retrogression."
The Buddha told the assembled *bǐqiū* (比丘):
"In a future age, if there are good men and good women
who hear the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng Típó Dáduō Pǐn* (妙法蓮華經提婆達多品) [Chapter on Devadatta in the *Lotus Sūtra*],
and with pure hearts believe and revere it without any doubt,
they will not fall into the hells, or among the hungry ghosts, or into the animal realm,
but will be born before the Buddhas in the ten directions.
In whatever place they are born, they will always hear this *sūtra*.
If they are born among humans or gods,
they will receive supreme and wonderful happiness.
If they are in the presence of a Buddha,
they will be born from a lotus flower."
At that time, a *púsà* (菩薩) named *Zhìjī* (智積), who had come from the place of the *Duōbǎo Shìzūn* (多寶世尊) Buddha,
said to *Duōbǎo* Buddha:
"I wish to return to my native land."
*Shìjiāmóuní Fó* (釋迦牟尼佛) told *Zhìjī*:
"Good man, wait a moment.
There is a *púsà* here named *Wénshūshīlì* (文殊師利). You can meet with him
and discuss the wonderful *dharma* before
you return to your native land."
At that time, *Wénshūshīlì*,
sitting on a thousand-petaled lotus flower as large as a cartwheel—
the *púsà* who came with him were also sitting on jeweled lotus flowers—
sprang forth naturally from the dragon palace of *Suōjiélúo* (娑竭羅) in the great ocean,
and remained in empty space.
He went to *Língjiū Shān* (靈鷲山)
and descended from the lotus flower
to the place of the Buddha,
and reverently bowed his head to the feet of the two World Honored Ones.
Having completed his reverence,
he went to *Zhìjī*'s place,
exchanged greetings with him,
and sat to one side.
*Zhìjī Púsà* asked *Wénshūshīlì*:
"How many beings did you transform
when you went to the dragon palace?"
*Wénshūshīlì* said:
"Their number is limitless,
uncountable,
beyond what can be spoken by the mouth
and beyond what can be measured by the mind.
Wait a moment,
and you will have proof yourself."
Before he finished speaking,
countless *púsà*, sitting on jeweled lotus flowers,
sprang forth from the ocean
and went to *Língjiū Shān*,
remaining in empty space.
All these *púsà* were transformed and liberated by *Wénshūshīlì*,
and possessed the conduct of a *púsà*.
They all discussed the Six *Pāramitās*.
Those who had originally been *shēngwén* (聲聞)
and practiced the conduct of *shēngwén* in empty space
were now all cultivating the meaning of the Great Vehicle emptiness.
*Wénshūshīlì* said to *Zhìjī*:
