"My teaching and transformation in the ocean
is like this."
At that time, *Zhìjī Púsà* praised him in verse, saying:
"Great wisdom, virtue, courage, and strength,
Transforming and liberating limitless beings,
Now this great assembly,
And I, have all seen it.
Expounding the meaning of true reality,
Revealing and explaining the One Vehicle *dharma*,
Widely guiding all sentient beings,
Enabling them to quickly attain *bōtí* (菩提)."
*Wénshūshīlì* said:
"In the ocean,
I only ever expound the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*."
*Zhìjī* asked *Wénshūshīlì*:
"This *sūtra* is very profound and subtle,
a treasure among *sūtras*,
rare in the world.
Are there any beings
who diligently and vigorously cultivate this *sūtra*
and quickly attain Buddhahood?"
*Wénshūshīlì* said:
"There is the daughter of the *Suōjiélúo* Dragon King,
who is only eight years old.
She is sharp-witted and intelligent,
and knows well the roots and actions of beings.
She has attained *tuóluóní* (陀羅尼)
and can uphold all the profound and secret treasures spoken by the Buddhas.
She has deeply entered into *chán* (禪) meditation,
clearly understands all *dharmas*,
generated the *bōtí* mind in an instant,
attained non-retrogression,
and possesses unobstructed eloquence.
She cherishes sentient beings
like her own children.
Her merits and virtues are complete.
Her mind thinks and her mouth speaks
subtly and broadly.
She is compassionate, kind, and yielding,
with a harmonious and elegant will,
and is capable of attaining *bōtí*."
*Zhìjī Púsà* said:
"I have seen *Shìjiā Rúlái* (釋迦如來)
practicing difficult practices for countless *jié* (劫),
accumulating merit and virtue,
seeking the path to *bōtí* without ever resting.
Observing the three thousand great thousand worlds,
there is not even a space the size of a mustard seed that is not a place where a *púsà* has given up their life
for the sake of sentient beings,
and only then was able to attain the path to *bōtí*.
I do not believe that this woman can become a fully enlightened Buddha in an instant."
Before he finished speaking,
the Dragon King's daughter suddenly appeared before them,
bowed her head in reverence,
and stood to one side,
praising in verse:
"Deeply understanding the aspects of sin and fortune,
Illuminating the ten directions,
Subtle and pure *dharma* body,
Possessing the thirty-two marks,
Using the eighty minor marks
To adorn the *dharma* body.
Revered and admired by gods and humans,
Respected by dragons and spirits,
All kinds of sentient beings,
None do not venerate and follow.
Hearing of the attainment of *bōtí*,
Only the Buddha can certify it.
I unfold the Great Vehicle teachings,
To liberate suffering sentient beings."
At that time, *Shèlìfú* (舍利弗) said to the Dragon Girl:
"You say that you will attain unsurpassed enlightenment soon,
but this is hard to believe.
Why is that?
A woman's body is impure
and not a vessel for the *dharma*.
How can you attain unsurpassed *bōtí*?
The Buddha path is distant and vast,
requiring countless *jié* of diligent and arduous practice,
fully cultivating all the *pāramitās*,
and only then can it be attained.
Moreover, a woman's body still has five obstacles:
first, she cannot become a *Fàntiān Wáng* (梵天王),
second, *Dìshì* (帝釋),
third, a demon king,
fourth, a wheel-turning sage king,
fifth, the body of a Buddha.
How can a woman's body quickly attain Buddhahood?"
At that time, the Dragon Girl had a precious pearl
worth three thousand great thousand worlds,
which she held up and offered to the Buddha.
The Buddha immediately accepted it.
The Dragon Girl said to *Zhìjī Púsà* and the Venerable *Shèlìfú*:
"Was my offering of the precious pearl
and the World Honored One's acceptance
swift or not?"
They answered, "Very swift."
The Dragon Girl said, "With your spiritual power,
observe my attainment of Buddhahood,
which will be even swifter than this."
At that time, the entire assembly
saw the Dragon Girl suddenly transform into a man,
possessing the conduct of a *púsà*.
He immediately went to the stainless world in the south,
sat on a jeweled lotus flower,
and attained complete and perfect enlightenment,
with the thirty-two marks
and eighty minor marks,
universally expounding the wonderful *dharma* for all sentient beings in the ten directions.
At that time, in the *Suōpó* (娑婆) world,
the *púsà*, *shēngwén*, the eight classes of gods and dragons, humans and non-humans,
all remotely saw the Dragon Girl attain Buddhahood,
universally teaching the *dharma* to the assembly of humans and gods,
and their hearts were greatly joyful,
and they all remotely paid their respects.
Countless sentient beings
heard the *dharma* and understood,
attaining non-retrogression;
countless sentient beings
received predictions of their path.
The stainless world
shook in six ways;
in the *Suōpó* world, three thousand sentient beings dwelt in the stage of non-retrogression,
and three thousand sentient beings generated the *bōtí* mind and received predictions of their path.
*Zhìjī Púsà* and *Shèlìfú*,
and the entire assembly,
silently believed and accepted it.
At that time, the *Yàowáng Púsà Mó訶sà* (藥王菩薩摩訶薩) and the *Dàlèshuō Púsà Mó訶sà* (大樂說菩薩摩訶薩),
together with a retinue of twenty thousand *púsà*,
all made this vow before the Buddha:
"May the World Honored One not be concerned.
After the Buddha's *nièpán* (涅槃),
we will uphold, read, recite, and speak this *sūtra*.
In the evil age to come,
sentient beings' roots of goodness will gradually diminish,
and they will mostly increase in arrogance,
greedily seeking offerings,
increasing their roots of unwholesomeness,
and distancing themselves from liberation.
Although they are difficult to teach and transform,
we will cultivate great forbearance,
recite this sūtra,
uphold, speak, write it,
and make all kinds of offerings,
not sparing our lives."
At that time, five hundred Arhats in the assembly who had received prophecies
said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! We also make a vow ourselves
to widely preach this sūtra in other lands."
Furthermore, eight thousand people, both learners and non-learners, who had received prophecies,
arose from their seats,
joined their palms, and made this vow to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! We will also widely preach this sūtra in other lands.
Why is this?
It is because in this *Suōpó* [娑婆] world,
people are mostly wicked and evil,
harboring increased arrogance,
with shallow merit, full of anger, turbidity, flattery, and deceit,
and their hearts are not genuine."
At that time, the Buddha's aunt, *Móhē Bōshébōtí* [摩訶波闍波提] *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼],
together with six thousand *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼], both learners and non-learners,
arose from their seats,
single-mindedly joined their palms,
gazed up at the venerable countenance,
without their eyes leaving for a moment.
At that time, the World-Honored One told *Qiáotánmí* [憍曇彌]:
"Why do you look at the *Rúlái* [如來] with a worried expression?
Is it perhaps that you think I will not mention your name
and give you the prediction of *Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí* [阿耨多羅三藐三菩提]?
*Qiáotánmí* [憍曇彌]! I have already given a general prediction to all *shēngwén* [聲聞].
Now, if you wish to know your prediction,
in the future,
you will be a great Dharma master in the Dharma of sixty-eight thousand *yì* [億] Buddhas,
and together with six thousand *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼], both learners and non-learners, you will be Dharma masters.
In this way, you will gradually perfect the *púsà* [菩薩] path,
and you will become a Buddha,
named *Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn Rúlái* [一切眾生喜見如來], *Yìnggòng* [應供], *Zhèngbiànzhī* [正遍知], *Míngxíngzú* [明行足],
*Shànshì* [善逝], *Shìjiānjiě* [世間解], *Wúshàngshì* [無上士], *Tiáoyù Zhàngfū* [調御丈夫], *Tiānrénshī* [天人師], *Fó* [佛], *Shìzūn* [世尊].
*Qiáotánmí* [憍曇彌]! This *Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn Fó* [一切眾生喜見佛] and the six thousand *púsà* [菩薩]
will successively receive predictions of *Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí* [阿耨多羅三藐三菩提]."
At that time, *Luóhóuluó* [羅睺羅]'s mother, *Yéshūtuóluó* [耶輸陀羅] *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼], thought to herself:
"In giving predictions, the World-Honored One has not mentioned my name."
The Buddha told *Yéshūtuóluó* [耶輸陀羅]:
"In the future, you will cultivate the *púsà* [菩薩] conduct in the Dharma of hundreds of thousands of *yì* [億] Buddhas,
and you will be a great Dharma master,
gradually perfecting the Buddha path.
In a good land, you will become a Buddha,
named *Jùzú Qiānwàn Guāngxiàng Rúlái* [具足千萬光相如來], *Yìnggòng* [應供],
*Zhèngbiànzhī* [正遍知], *Míngxíngzú* [明行足], *Shànshì* [善逝],
*Shìjiānjiě* [世間解], *Wúshàngshì* [無上士], *Tiáoyù Zhàngfū* [調御丈夫], *Tiānrénshī* [天人師], *Fó* [佛], *Shìzūn* [世尊].
The Buddha's lifespan will be immeasurable *Āsēngqí* [阿僧祇] *jié* [劫]."
At that time, *Móhē Bōshébōtí* [摩訶波闍波提] *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼] and *Yéshūtuóluó* [耶輸陀羅] *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼],
together with their retinue, were all greatly delighted
and obtained what they had never had before.
Immediately before the Buddha, they spoke these verses:
"World-Honored One, the guide and teacher,
bringing peace and security to gods and humans,
we have heard the prediction,
and our hearts are peaceful and fulfilled."
After the *Bǐqiūní* [比丘尼] spoke these verses,
they said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! We can also widely propagate this sūtra in other lands."
At that time, the World-Honored One looked at the eight hundred thousand *yì* [億] *Nàyōutā* [那由他] *púsà móhēsà* [菩薩摩訶薩].
These *púsà* [菩薩]—all were *Āwéiyuèzhì* [阿惟越致],
turning the wheel of non-regression Dharma,
having obtained all the *tuóluóní* [陀羅尼]—
immediately arose from their seats,
went to the Buddha,
joined their palms single-mindedly,
and thought to themselves:
"If the World-Honored One instructs us to uphold and preach this sūtra,
we will follow the Buddha's teachings
and widely propagate this Dharma."
They further thought:
"The Buddha is now silent
and does not give instructions.
What should we do?"
At that time, the *púsà* [菩薩], respecting and complying with the Buddha's intention
and also wishing to fulfill their original vows,
then roared like lions before the Buddha and made a vow, saying:
"World-Honored One!
After the *Rúlái* [如來]'s extinction,
we will travel back and forth in the ten directions of the world,
enabling sentient beings to write this sūtra, uphold, recite,
explain its meaning,
practice according to the Dharma,
and remember it correctly.
All of this is due to the Buddha's power.
We only hope that the World-Honored One
will remotely see, protect, and guard us in other lands."
Immediately, all the *púsà* [菩薩] together voiced and spoke these verses:
"Please do not be concerned.
After the Buddha's extinction,
in the fearful and evil world,
we will widely preach it.
There will be ignorant people
who will curse and revile us with evil mouths,
and even use knives and clubs.
We will endure all of this.
In the evil world, there will be *bǐqiū* [比丘]
with distorted wisdom and deceitful hearts,
claiming to have attained what they have not,
full of arrogance.
Some will dwell in the *ālányě* [阿練若],
wearing patched robes in secluded places,
claiming to practice the true path,
and belittling those in the human world.
Greedy for profit and offerings,
they will preach the Dharma to laypeople,
seeking to be respected by the world,
like *Luóhàn* [羅漢] with the six superknowledges.
These people harbor evil intentions,
constantly thinking about worldly matters,
falsely claiming to be in the *ālányě* [阿練若],
eager to point out our faults, and will say such things:
'These *bǐqiū* [比丘] and others,
for the sake of greed and offerings,
preach externalist doctrines;
they have created this sūtra themselves
to deceive the people of the world.
Seeking fame and reputation, they analyze and discuss this sūtra.'
Constantly in large gatherings,
wanting to slander us,
to kings, ministers,
*Bāluómén* [婆羅門], laypeople,
and other *bǐqiū* [比丘],
they will slander and speak of our evil,
claiming that we are heretics
who preach externalist doctrines.
Because we respect the Buddha,
we will endure all these evils.
Being belittled by these words,
'You are all Buddhas,'
such contemptuous words,
we will endure them all.
In the defiled *jié* [劫] and evil world,
there will be many terrors.
Evil spirits will enter their bodies,
cursing and reviling us.
Because we respect and believe in the Buddha,
we will wear the armor of endurance.
For the sake of preaching this sūtra,
we will endure these difficult matters.
We do not cherish our lives,
but only cherish the unsurpassed path.
In the future,
we will protect and uphold what the Buddha has entrusted to us.
The World-Honored One himself will know.
The defiled and evil *bǐqiū* [比丘]
do not understand the Buddha's skillful means,
the Dharma spoken according to circumstances.
With evil mouths and frowning faces,
they will frequently see us expelled,
far away from temples and pagodas.
All these evils,
because we remember the Buddha's instructions,
we will endure these things.
In all villages and cities,
where there are those who seek the Dharma,
we will go to their places
and preach the Dharma entrusted by the Buddha.
We are messengers of the World-Honored One,
fearless in the assembly.
We will skillfully preach the Dharma.
May the Buddha dwell in peace.
Before the World-Honored One,
and all the Buddhas who come from the ten directions,
we make such vows.
The Buddha himself knows our hearts."
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* [妙法蓮華經] Scroll Four
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* [妙法蓮華經] Scroll Five
Tripiṭaka Dharma Master *Jiūmóluóshí* [鳩摩羅什] from the *Qiúcí* [龜茲] Kingdom of the Later *Qín* [秦],
translated under imperial decree.
At that time,
*Wénshūshīlì* [文殊師利] Dharma Prince *púsà móhēsà* [菩薩摩訶薩] said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
These *púsà* [菩薩] are extremely rare,
respecting and complying with the Buddha,
making great vows
to protect, uphold, read, and preach this *Fǎhuá Jīng* [法華經] in the evil world of the future.
World-Honored One!
How can the *púsà móhēsà* [菩薩摩訶薩] preach this sūtra in the evil world of the future?"
The Buddha told Wénshū Shīlì:
"If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva,
in the evil age to come, wishes to preach this Sutra,
he should abide in four dharmas.
First, he should abide in the practice-place and the close-quarters of a Bodhisattva,
and be able to expound this Sutra for sentient beings.
Wénshū Shīlì!
What is called the practice-place of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?
If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the ground of patience,
is gentle, amiable, and compliant, and not sudden or violent,
his mind also not alarmed;
moreover, he practices nothing with regard to dharmas,
but contemplates all dharmas in their suchness,
also not practicing or discriminating,
this is called the practice-place of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
What is called the close-quarters of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva does not draw close to kings, princes, great ministers, or officials;
he does not draw close to the various non-Buddhist Brahmins, the Nirgranthas, and so on;
N. irgrantha
and those who create worldly writings, eulogize non-Buddhist books,
and the Lokāyatas and anti-Lokāyatas;
he also does not draw close to those who have violent games,
wrestling and grappling,
and various transformation shows such as those of the Naṭas;
he also does not draw close to the Caṇḍālas,
and those who raise pigs, sheep, chickens, and dogs,
and the various evil rules of conduct of hunting and fishing.
If such people as these sometimes come,
then he should preach the Dharma for them,
without any expectations.
He also does not draw close to Śrāvaka Bhikṣus, Bhikṣuṇīs, Upāsakas, or Upāsikās who seek enlightenment,
and does not even greet them.
Whether in their rooms,
or in their walking-places,
or in the lecture hall,
he does not dwell with them.
If they sometimes come,
he preaches the Dharma as appropriate,
without seeking anything.
"Wénshū Shīlì!
Moreover, a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva should not, with regard to the female body,
take on the characteristics that can give rise to desires when preaching the Dharma, and also should not delight in seeing them.
If he enters another's home, he should not speak with young girls, virgins, or widows.
Also, he should not be close to the five types of eunuchs, taking them as intimate friends;
he should not enter another's home alone;
if there is a reason that he must enter alone,
he should only single-mindedly recite the name of the Buddha.
If he preaches the Dharma for women,
he should not grin,
and should not reveal his chest;
even for the sake of the Dharma, he should not be too familiar,
how much less for other matters.
He does not delight in keeping young disciples, Śrāmaṇeras, or young children,
and also does not delight in being with the same teacher.
He should constantly delight in sitting in meditation,
being in a quiet place,
cultivating and controlling his mind.
Wénshū Shīlì!
This is called the initial close-quarters."
"Furthermore, a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva contemplates all dharmas as empty,
in their suchness,
not inverted, not moving, not regressing, not transforming,
like empty space, having no own-nature.
All paths of language are cut off,
not arising, not appearing, not originating,
without name, without form, truly non-existent,
boundless, limitless, unimpeded, unobstructed,
but existing due to conditions,
being spoken of due to arising from inversion.
He constantly delights in contemplating the characteristics of dharmas in this way,
this is called the second close-quarters of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate
this meaning, spoke in verse, saying:
If there is a Bodhisattva,
in the evil age to come,
with a fearless mind,
who wishes to speak this Sutra,
he should enter the practice-place,
and the close-quarters.
He should constantly stay away from kings,
and princes,
great ministers, and officials,
those who are violently playful,
and the Caṇḍālas,
and non-Buddhist Brahmins.
Also, he should not be close to
those who are arrogant,
those attached to the Small Vehicle,
those who study the Three Baskets,
Bhikṣus who have broken the precepts,
those who are called Arhats,
and Bhikṣuṇīs who
like play and laughter,
those who seek present cessation,
and the various Upāsikās—
he should not draw close to any of them.
If such people as these,
with good intentions, come
to the Bodhisattva's place,
to hear the Buddha-way,
the Bodhisattva should then,
with a fearless mind,
without harboring expectations,
preach the Dharma for them.
Widows, virgins,
and the various eunuchs—
he should not draw close to any of them,
taking them as intimate friends.
Also, he should not draw close to
butchers and executioners,
hunters and fishermen,
who kill for profit,
sell meat to make a living,
and prostitute women—
he should not draw close to such people as these.
He should not draw close to
violent wrestling,
various games and plays,
and the various prostitutes, etc.—
he should not draw close to any of them.
He should not be alone in a secluded place
preaching the Dharma for women;
when preaching the Dharma,
he must not joke and laugh.
When entering a village to beg for food,
he should take a Bhikṣu with him;
if there is no Bhikṣu,
he should single-mindedly recite the name of the Buddha.
This is then called
the practice-place and the close-quarters;
with these two places,
he can preach in peace and happiness.
Moreover, he does not practice
the superior, middling, or inferior dharmas,
the conditioned or unconditioned,
the real or unreal dharmas;
also, he does not discriminate
whether it is male or female.
Not obtaining the various dharmas,
not knowing and not seeing,
this is then called
the practice-place of a Bodhisattva.
All the various dharmas
are empty and non-existent,
without permanence,
also without arising and ceasing;
this is called the close-quarters
that the wise ones frequent.
Inverting and discriminating,
the various dharmas as existent or non-existent,
real or unreal,
arising or non-arising—
in a quiet place,
he cultivates and controls his mind,
abiding immovably,
like Mount Sumeru.
Contemplating all dharmas
as non-existent,
like empty space,
without solidity,
not arising, not appearing,
not moving, not regressing,
constantly abiding in a single characteristic—
this is called the close-quarters.
If there is a Bhikṣu
after my extinction,
and close-quarters,
when speaking this Sutra,
A Bodhisattva sometimes
enters a quiet room,
and with right mindfulness,
contemplates the Dharma in accordance with its meaning.
Arising from meditation,
for the various kings,
princes, ministers, people,
Brahmins, etc.,
he opens up and expounds,
speaking this Classic,
his mind is peaceful and secure,
without timidity or weakness.
Wénshū Shīlì!
This is called a Bodhisattva
abiding in the first dharma,
able to speak the *Lotus Sūtra*
in the future age.
"Furthermore, Wénshū Shīlì!
After the Tathāgata's extinction,
in the Dharma-ending age, if one wishes to speak this Sutra,
he should abide in the practice of peaceful and joyful conduct.
Whether speaking aloud or reading the Sutra,
he does not delight in speaking of the faults of people or the scriptures.
Also, he does not slight or disparage the various other Dharma masters,
and does not speak of the good or bad points, the strengths or weaknesses of others.
Towards those of the Śrāvakayāna,
one should neither mention their names to speak of their faults and evils,
nor mention their names to praise their virtues.
Furthermore, one should not give rise to feelings of resentment or dislike.
Because one cultivates such a peaceful and joyful mind well,
all who listen will not resist his meaning.
If there are difficult questions,
one should not answer with the teachings of the Śrāvakayāna,
but only use the Mahāyāna to explain and expound,
so that they may attain omniscience."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"Bodhisattvas constantly delight in
peacefully and serenely expounding the Dharma.
In a pure and clean place,
they set out a bed and seat.
Anointing their bodies with oil,
bathing away dust and defilement,
donning new and clean clothes,
pure both inside and out,
peacefully sitting on the Dharma seat,
they expound according to the questions asked.
If there are *bǐqiū*
and *bǐqiūní*,
or *yōupósè*
and *yōupóyí*,
kings, princes,
ministers, officials, and common people,
explain with subtle meanings and a gentle countenance.
If there are difficult questions,
answer according to the meaning,
using causes, conditions, and parables,
expounding and differentiating.
Using these expedient means,
cause all to awaken their minds,
gradually increasing and benefiting,
entering the Buddha Way.
Remove the intention of laziness
and thoughts of indolence,
be apart from all worries and vexations,
and expound the Dharma with a compassionate mind.
Day and night, constantly expound
the unsurpassed teachings,
with all causes and conditions
and countless parables,
enlighten and reveal to sentient beings,
causing all to be joyful.
As for clothing, bedding,
food, drink, and medicine,
within these,
have no expectations.
But with a single mind, think of
the causes and conditions for expounding the Dharma,
vowing to attain Buddhahood,
causing others to be the same.
This is truly of great benefit,
a peaceful and joyful offering.
After my Parinirvana,
if there is a *bǐqiū*
who can expound this
wondrous *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng*,
with a mind free of jealousy and hatred,
all vexations and obstructions,
also without worries and sorrows,
and those who scold and revile,
also without fear
of adding knives, staves, and the like,
also without being expelled,
dwelling in forbearance,
the wise one, in this way, cultivates his mind well,
and can dwell in peace and joy,
as I have said above.
The merit and virtue of this person,
for millions of *yì* of *jié*,
cannot be completely described through calculation and parables."
"Furthermore, Wénshūshīlì
Bodhisattva Mahāsattva! In the future, in the final age when the Dharma is about to perish,
those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this scripture,
should not harbor thoughts of jealousy, flattery, and deceit,
and should not belittle or scold those who study the Buddha Way, seeking their strengths and weaknesses.
If there are *bǐqiū*, *bǐqiūní*, *yōupósè*, *yōupóyí*, those who seek the Śrāvakayāna,
those who seek the Pratyekabuddha Way, or those who seek the Bodhisattva Way,
do not trouble them, causing them to doubt and regret,
saying to these people:
'You are very far from the Way,
and will ultimately not be able to attain omniscience.
Why is that?
Because you are dissipated people, and are therefore lazy in the Way.'
Furthermore, one should also not engage in frivolous discussions about the Dharmas,
or engage in disputes and contentions.
One should cultivate a great compassionate thought towards all sentient beings,
cultivate the thought of a loving father towards all Tathāgatas,
cultivate the thought of a great teacher towards all Bodhisattvas,
and towards the great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
one should always deeply and respectfully bow and pay homage.
Towards all sentient beings,
expound the Dharma equally,
according to the Dharma,
not too much and not too little,
even to those who deeply love the Dharma, do not speak too much."
"Wénshūshīlì!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, in the future, in the final age when the Dharma is about to perish,
attains and completes this third peaceful and joyful practice,
when expounding this Dharma,
none will be able to trouble or disturb him,
he will obtain good fellow practitioners to read and recite this scripture together,
and he will also obtain great assemblies who come to listen and receive.
After listening, they will be able to uphold it,
after upholding it, they will be able to recite it,
after reciting it, they will be able to expound it,
after expounding it, they will be able to write it,
or cause others to write it,
make offerings to the scripture scrolls,
and be respectful, reverent, and full of praise."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"If one wishes to expound this scripture,
one should abandon jealousy, hatred, and pride,
flattery, deceit, and hypocritical minds,
and constantly cultivate honest and upright conduct.
Do not belittle or scorn others,
and do not engage in frivolous discussions about the Dharma,
do not cause others to doubt and regret,
saying, 'You will not attain Buddhahood.'
The Buddha's disciples who expound the Dharma
are always gentle and able to endure,
compassionate towards all,
and do not give rise to indolent minds.
The great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
out of compassion for sentient beings, practice the Way,
one should cultivate a respectful mind,
for they are my great teachers.
Towards all Buddhas, World Honored Ones,
cultivate the thought of an unsurpassed father,
break down the mind of arrogance and pride,
and expounding the Dharma will be without obstructions.
The third Dharma is like this,
the wise should guard and protect it,
with a single mind, peacefully and joyfully practice,
and be revered by countless multitudes."
"Furthermore, Wénshūshīlì!
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, in the future, in the final age when the Dharma is about to perish,
who upholds this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
should cultivate a great compassionate mind among those who are householders and those who have left home,
and cultivate a great compassionate mind towards those who are not Bodhisattvas,
and should have this thought:
'Such people are truly a great loss.
The Tathāgata, with expedient means, expounds the Dharma according to what is appropriate,
but they do not hear, know, or perceive it,
do not ask, believe, or understand it.
Although these people do not ask, believe, or understand this scripture,
when I attain Anuttara-Samyak-Sambodhi,
wherever I may be,
I will use supernatural powers and the power of wisdom to lead them,
causing them to dwell in this Dharma.'
Wénshūshīlì!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, after the Tathāgata's Parinirvana, attains and completes this fourth Dharma,
when expounding this Dharma, there will be no faults or errors,
and he will always be offered to, revered, respected, and praised by *bǐqiū*, *bǐqiūní*, *yōupósè*, *yōupóyí*,
kings, princes, ministers, the people,
Brahmins, householders, and the like.
The gods of the empty sky
will also constantly attend and serve, for the sake of listening to the Dharma.
Whether he is in villages, cities, or secluded forests,
if there are people who come wishing to ask difficult questions,
the gods will constantly protect and guard him day and night for the sake of the Dharma,
and will be able to cause all who listen to be joyful.
Why is that?
This scripture is protected by the divine power of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
Wénshūshīlì!
This *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
in countless lands,
even its name cannot be heard,
how much more so to see, receive, uphold, read, and recite it?"
Wénshūshīlì!
For example, a powerful Cakravartin king,
wishing to subdue all countries with his might,
but the smaller kings do not obey his commands,
at that time, the Cakravartin king raises all kinds of troops and goes to punish and subdue them.
The king, seeing the soldiers who have merit in battle,
immediately rejoices greatly,
and rewards them according to their merit,
sometimes giving them fields, houses, villages, and cities;
sometimes giving them clothing and adornments;
sometimes giving them various treasures:
gold, silver, *liúlí*, *chēqú*, *mǎnǎo*, coral, and amber,
elephants, horses, carriages, servants, and people.
Only the bright pearl in his topknot is not given to them.
Why is that?
Only the king on his head has this one pearl,
if he were to give it away,
all the king's family members would certainly be greatly astonished.
“Wénshūshīlì!
The Thus Come One is also like this.
With the power of *chán* concentration and wisdom, he obtains the land of the Dharma.
He reigns in the triple world,
but the various demon kings are unwilling to submit.
The Thus Come One's worthy and sagely generals fight together with them.
Those who have merit,
their minds are also delighted.
Among the four assemblies, he speaks the various sutras,
causing their minds to be pleased.
He bestows upon them the wealth of *chán* concentration, liberation, non-outflow roots and powers, and all Dharmas.
Moreover, he bestows upon them the city of *nièpán*,
saying that they can attain extinction.
He guides their minds, causing them all to be delighted,
but he does not speak this *Fǎhuá Jīng* for them.
"Wénshūshīlì!
It is like a wheel-turning king who sees that his troops have great merit.
His mind is very pleased.
He has long kept this hard-to-believe pearl in his hair knot and would not rashly give it to others,
but now he gives it to them.
The Thus Come One is also like this.
In the triple world, he is the great Dharma king.
He uses the Dharma to teach and transform all living beings.
He sees the worthy and sagely army
fighting together with the five *yīn* demons, the affliction demons, and the death demon,
having great meritorious achievements,
extinguishing the three poisons,
leaving the triple world,
breaking the demon nets.
At that time, the Thus Come One is also greatly delighted.
This *Fǎhuá Jīng* can enable living beings to reach all-knowing wisdom.
In all the worlds, there are many grudges and it is hard to believe.
It has not been spoken before, but now it is spoken.
Wénshūshīlì!
This *Fǎhuá Jīng* is the foremost teaching of all the Thus Come Ones.
Among all the teachings, it is the most profound.
It is bestowed last,
like that powerful king who has long protected a bright pearl,
and now he gives it to them.
Wénshūshīlì!
This *Fǎhuá Jīng* is the secret treasury of all Buddhas and Thus Come Ones.
Among all the sutras, it is the most superior.
For a long night, it is guarded and not rashly spoken.
Only today is it being expounded to you all."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
Always practicing patience,
having compassion for all,
only then can one expound
the sutra praised by the Buddha.
In the last age,
those who uphold this sutra,
whether at home or leaving home,
and those who are not *púsà*,
should generate compassion.
If these people do not hear
and do not believe this sutra,
then it is a great loss.
I attained the Buddha way
by means of various skillful devices
to speak this Dharma
and cause them to dwell in it.
It is like a powerful
wheel-turning king.
For those who have merit in battle,
he bestows various things,
elephants, horses, chariots,
adornments for the body,
and fields and residences,
villages and towns.
Or he gives them clothing,
various rare jewels,
slaves, and property,
If there is someone brave and strong
who can accomplish difficult tasks,
the king unties from his hair knot
a bright pearl and bestows it on him.
The Thus Come One is also like this.
He is the king of all Dharmas,
with the great power of patience
and a treasury of wisdom.
With great compassion,
he transforms the world according to the Dharma.
Seeing all people
suffering from various afflictions,
desiring to seek liberation,
he fights together with the various demons.
For the sake of these living beings,
he speaks various Dharmas.
With great skillful devices,
he speaks these various sutras.
Having already known that living beings
have obtained their strength,
lastly, he then
speaks this *Fǎhuá*.
It is like the king untying from his hair knot
a bright pearl and giving it to them.
This sutra is the most honored,
the most superior among all sutras.
I always guard it
and do not rashly reveal it.
Now is the right time
to speak it for you all.
After I have passed into extinction,
those who seek the Buddha way,
desiring to obtain peace and security,
and expound this sutra,
should draw near
to these four Dharmas.
Those who read this sutra
will always be without worry and affliction,
and also without sickness or pain.
Their complexion will be fresh and white.
They will not be born into poverty,
lowliness, or ugliness.
Living beings will delight in seeing them,
as if longing for the worthy and sagely.
The children of the heavens
will serve them.
Knives and staffs will not be applied to them,
and poison will not be able to harm them.
If people revile them,
their mouths will be shut.
They will travel without fear,
like a lion king.
Their wisdom and light
will be like the sun's illumination.
If in dreams,
they only see wonderful things.
They will see the various Thus Come Ones
sitting on lion thrones,
with assemblies of *bǐqiū*
surrounding them and speaking the Dharma.
They will also see dragons, gods,
*āxiūluó*, and others,
their numbers like the Ganges' sands,
reverently joining their palms.
They will see themselves
speaking the Dharma for them.
They will also see the various Buddhas,
their bodies with golden colors,
emitting limitless light,
illuminating everything.
With Brahma sounds,
they will expound the various Dharmas.
The Buddha will speak the unsurpassed Dharma
for the four assemblies.
They will see themselves in the midst,
joining their palms and praising the Buddha,
hearing the Dharma and being delighted,
and making offerings.
They will obtain *tuóluóní*,
proving non-retreating wisdom.
The Buddha knows their minds,
that they have deeply entered the Buddha way.
He will then bestow a prediction upon them
that they will attain Right Enlightenment:
"You good men!
In the future,
you will attain limitless wisdom,
the Buddha's great way.
Your lands will be adorned and pure,
vast and incomparable."
There will also be the four assemblies
joining their palms and listening to the Dharma.
They will also see themselves
in mountains and forests,
cultivating good Dharmas,
proving the various true aspects,
deeply entering *chán* concentration,
seeing the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The various Buddhas' bodies will be golden,
adorned with a hundred blessings and marks.
Hearing the Dharma and speaking it for others,
they will always have these good dreams.
They will also dream of becoming kings,
abandoning palaces and retinues,
and the highest and most wonderful five desires,
going to the *dàochǎng*.
Under the *pútí* tree,
they will dwell on a lion throne.
Seeking the Way for over seven days,
they will obtain the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Having attained the unsurpassed way,
they will arise and turn the Dharma wheel,
speaking the Dharma for the four assemblies.
For millions of *jié*,
they will speak the non-outflow wonderful Dharma,
crossing over limitless living beings.
Afterward, they will enter *nièpán*,
like a lamp whose smoke has been exhausted and extinguished.
If in the evil ages of the future,
someone speaks this foremost Dharma,
this person will obtain great benefits,
like the above-mentioned merits and virtues.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had come from other lands,
exceeding eight *héng hé* sands,
rose in the great assembly,
joined their palms in reverence, and said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
If you permit us, after the Buddha's extinction,
in this *Suōpó* world, to diligently apply ourselves and protect, recite, write, and make offerings to this scripture,
we will widely preach it in this land."
At that time, the Buddha told the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:
"Stop, good men!
You do not need to protect this scripture.
Why is that?
In my *Suōpó* world, there are already six hundred thousand *héng hé* sands of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
each Bodhisattva having six hundred thousand *héng hé* sands of attendants.
These people will be able to protect, recite, and widely preach this scripture after my extinction."
When the Buddha spoke these words,
the land of the *Suōpó* world, the three-thousand great-thousand world, all quaked and split open,
and from within it, countless millions of billions of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas simultaneously sprang forth.
These Bodhisattvas all had golden bodies,
the thirty-two marks,
immeasurable light,
and had previously resided beneath this *Suōpó* world, in the empty space of this realm.
These Bodhisattvas, hearing the voice of Śākyamuni Buddha,
arose from below.
Each Bodhisattva was the leader of the assembly,
each bringing six hundred thousand *héng hé* sands of attendants;
not to mention those bringing fifty thousand, forty thousand, thirty thousand, twenty thousand, ten thousand *héng hé* sands of attendants;
not to mention even one *héng hé* sand, half a *héng hé* sand, one-quarter of a *héng hé* sand,
even one part in millions of billions of *nàyóutā*;
not to mention millions of billions of *nàyóutā* attendants;
not to mention hundreds of millions of attendants;
not to mention ten million, one million, even ten thousand;
not to mention one thousand, one hundred, even ten;
not to mention those bringing five, four, three, two, or one disciple;
not to mention those who were alone, delighting in solitary practice.
Such comparisons
are immeasurable and boundless, beyond what calculations or metaphors can comprehend.
After these Bodhisattvas emerged from the earth,
they each went to the precious, wonderful seven-jeweled tower in the empty space, to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna and Śākyamuni Buddha.
Having arrived,
they bowed their heads and paid homage to the feet of the two World Honored Ones,
and also made obeisance to the Buddhas on the lion thrones beneath the jeweled trees,
circling them three times to the right,
joining their palms in reverence,
praising them with various Bodhisattva praises,
and stood on one side,
joyfully gazing up at the two World Honored Ones.
From the moment these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas first sprang forth,
praising the Buddhas with various Bodhisattva praises,
this continued for fifty minor *jié*.
At this time, Śākyamuni Buddha sat in silence,
and the four assemblies also remained silent for fifty minor *jié*;
due to the Buddha's spiritual power,
the great assembly perceived it as only half a day.
At that time, the four assemblies,
also due to the Buddha's spiritual power,
saw the Bodhisattvas filling the empty space of countless millions of billions of lands.
Among these Bodhisattva assemblies were four leaders:
one named Shàngxíng (上行),
the second named Wúbiānxíng (無邊行),
the third named Jìngxíng (淨行),
and the fourth named Ānlìxíng (安立行).
These four Bodhisattvas were the foremost leaders in their assembly,
standing before the great assembly,
each joining their palms together,
gazing at Śākyamuni Buddha and inquiring:
"World Honored One!
Are you free from illness and affliction?
Are you at ease in your practice?
Are those who are to be saved easy to instruct?
Do you not allow the World Honored One to become fatigued?"
At that time, the four great Bodhisattvas spoke in verse:
The World Honored One is at peace,
free from illness and affliction,
teaching and transforming sentient beings,
without weariness.
And are all sentient beings
easy to transform?
Do they not cause the World Honored One
to become fatigued?
At that time, the World Honored One, in the great assembly of Bodhisattvas, said:
"So it is, so it is! Good men!
The Tathāgata is at peace,
free from illness and affliction;
these sentient beings are easy to transform and cross over,
without fatigue.
Why is that?
These sentient beings have constantly received my transformation from lifetime to lifetime,
and have also made offerings and respected past Buddhas,
planting various roots of goodness.
These sentient beings, upon first seeing my body,
and hearing what I say, immediately believe and enter the Tathāgata's wisdom;
except for those who previously cultivated and studied the Small Vehicle.
Such people, I now also cause to hear this scripture,
and enter into the Buddha's wisdom."
At that time, the great Bodhisattvas spoke in verse:
Excellent, excellent!
Great Hero, World Honored One!
These sentient beings
are easy to transform and cross over.
Able to ask the Buddhas about
profound and deep wisdom,
having heard it, they believe and practice;
we rejoice accordingly.
At that time, the World Honored One praised the leading great Bodhisattvas:
"Excellent, excellent!
Good men!
You are able to arouse a mind of rejoicing accordingly in the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Maitreya and the eight thousand *héng hé* sands of Bodhisattva assemblies all thought:
"Since long ago, we have never seen or heard of such a great assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas emerging from the earth,
standing before the World Honored One, joining their palms, making offerings,
and inquiring after the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Mílè (彌勒),
knowing the thoughts of the eight thousand *héng hé* sands of Bodhisattva assemblies,
and also wanting to resolve his own doubts,
joined his palms towards the Buddha,
and asked in verse:
Countless millions of billions
of great assembly Bodhisattvas,
never seen before,
I wish the Two-Footed Honored One would explain,
where do they come from?
By what cause and condition did they gather?
With giant bodies and great spiritual powers,
wisdom beyond comprehension,
their resolve is firm and solid,
possessing great power of patience and endurance,
delightful to sentient beings,
where do they come from?
Each and every Bodhisattva,
with the retinues they lead,
their numbers are immeasurable,
like the sands of the *Héng Hé*.
Some great Bodhisattvas
lead sixty thousand *Héng Hé* sands,
such great assemblies,
single-mindedly seeking the Buddha path.
These great leaders,
sixty thousand *héng hé* sands,
together come to make offerings to the Buddha,
and protect and uphold this scripture.
Leading fifty thousand *Héng Hé* sands, their number exceeds this.
Forty thousand and thirty thousand,
twenty thousand down to ten thousand,
one thousand, one hundred, and so on,
even to one *Héng Hé* sand,
half, and three or four parts,
one part in hundreds of millions,
millions of billions of *nàyóutā*,
ten thousand billion disciples,
even to half a billion,
their number also exceeds the above.
One million down to ten thousand,
one thousand and one hundred,
fifty and ten,
even three, two, or one,
alone without retinues,
delighting in solitary dwelling,
all come to the Buddha's place,
their number increases beyond the above.
Such great assemblies, if one were to count them,
even after *Héng Hé* sand *jié*,
one still could not know them completely.
These great majestic virtue,
diligent Bodhisattva assemblies,
who expounded the Dharma for them,
teaching and transforming them to accomplishment?
From whom did they first arouse their minds?
Praising and extolling whose Buddha-dharma?
Receiving and upholding whose scripture?
Cultivating and studying whose Buddha-path?
Such Bodhisattvas,
with spiritual power and great wisdom,
the four directions quaked and split,
all emerged from within.
World Honored One, in the past,
I have never seen such a thing,
I wish you would explain where they come from,
the name of their land.
I often travel to various lands,
I have never seen this assembly,
in this assembly,
I do not recognize a single person,
suddenly emerging from the earth,
I wish you would explain the cause and conditions.
Now this great assembly,
countless hundreds of thousands of billions,
these Bodhisattvas,
all wish to know about this matter.
The cause and conditions
of the origin and end of these Bodhisattva assemblies,
World Honored One of immeasurable virtue,
I only wish you would resolve the assembly's doubts.
At that time, the Śākyamuni Buddha's manifested Buddhas,
coming from countless millions of other lands,
were sitting in the lotus position on lion thrones under the jeweled trees in the eight directions.
Each Buddha's attendant saw the great assembly of Bodhisattvas,
emerging from the earth in the four directions of the three-thousand-great-thousand world,
and dwelling in the sky.
Each said to their Buddha,
"World Honored One!
From whence did these countless, boundless, asaṃkhya great assemblies of Bodhisattvas come?"
At that time, the Buddhas each told their attendants,
"Good men! Wait a moment.
There is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Mílè —
predicted by Śākyamuni Buddha
to become a Buddha in the future —
who will ask about this matter.
The Buddha will now answer,
and you will naturally hear it because of this."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha said to Mílè Bodhisattva,
"Excellent, excellent!
Āyìduō! You are able to ask the Buddha about such a great matter.
You should all be of one mind,
put on the armor of diligence,
and arouse a firm intention.
The Tathāgata now wishes to reveal and declare the wisdom of all Buddhas,
the power of the uninhibited spiritual powers of all Buddhas,
the power of the lion-like vigor of all Buddhas,
and the power of the awesome and mighty strength of all Buddhas."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse,
"Be diligent and of one mind,
I wish to speak of this matter,
Do not have doubts or regrets,
The Buddha's wisdom is inconceivable.
Now bring forth the power of faith,
Abide in forbearance and goodness,
Dharmas never heard before,
Now you shall all hear them.
I now comfort you,
Do not harbor doubt or fear,
The Buddha speaks no untruths,
Wisdom is immeasurable.
The foremost Dharma attained,
Is profound and difficult to distinguish,
Thus I shall now speak,
You all listen attentively."
At that time, after the World Honored One spoke this verse,
"I now declare to you and this great assembly. Āyìduō!
These great Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas,
countless asaṃkhyas, emerging from the earth,
whom you have never seen before,
after I attained Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi in this Saha world,
taught and guided these Bodhisattvas,
tamed their minds,
and caused them to arouse the intention for enlightenment.
These Bodhisattvas all dwell beneath this Saha world, in the sky of this realm;
they read, recite, and thoroughly understand the various scriptures,
contemplate and discern them, and maintain correct mindfulness.
Āyìduō! These good men do not enjoy being among the crowd and speaking much;
they always enjoy quiet places,
diligently practice and are never idle;
they also do not rely on humans or gods to abide.
They always enjoy profound wisdom, without obstruction,
and they always enjoy the Dharma of the Buddhas, diligently seeking unsurpassed wisdom with one mind."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse,
"Āyì, you should know!
These great Bodhisattvas,
from countless kalpas ago,
have cultivated the wisdom of the Buddhas,
all were transformed by me,
causing them to arouse the great intention for enlightenment.
These are my children,
relying on this world,
constantly practicing dhūta practices,
with minds delighting in quiet places,
abandoning the noisy crowds,
not enjoying much speaking.
Such children,
learn my Dharma,
day and night constantly diligent,
for the sake of seeking the Buddha path,
in the Saha world,
dwelling in the sky below.
Their mindfulness is firm,
constantly diligently seeking wisdom,
speaking various wonderful Dharmas,
their minds without fear.
In the city of Gáyé,
sitting under the Bodhi tree,
I attained perfect enlightenment,
and turned the unsurpassed Dharma wheel.
Then I taught them,
causing them to initially arouse the intention for enlightenment,
now they all dwell in non-retrogression,
and all shall attain Buddhahood.
I now speak truthfully,
you all believe with one mind,
From a long time ago,
I have been teaching this assembly."
became doubtful
and wondered, "How could the World Honored One have taught such a countless, boundless, asaṃkhya of great Bodhisattvas in such a short time,
causing them to dwell in Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi?"
Then they said to the Buddha,
"World Honored One!
When the Tathāgata was a prince,
he left the Shì clan palace,
not far from the city of Gáyé, sat in the Bodhimaṇḍa,
and attained Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
From then until now, only forty years have passed.
World Honored One!
How could you have performed such great Buddha works in such a short time,
using the Buddha's power and merit,
to teach such a countless great assembly of Bodhisattvas,
who will attain Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi?
World Honored One! This great assembly of Bodhisattvas,
even if someone counted for millions of kalpas, could not exhaust their number nor reach their limit.
These beings, from a long time ago,
in the presence of countless Buddhas,
have planted various good roots,
accomplished the Bodhisattva path,
and constantly cultivated pure conduct.
World Honored One! Such a thing is hard for the world to believe.
It is like someone with beautiful complexion and black hair, twenty-five years old,
pointing to a hundred-year-old person and saying,
'This is my child.'
The hundred-year-old person also points to the young person and says,
'This is my father, who gave birth to me.'
This is hard to believe.
The Buddha is also like this.
It has not been long since you attained the path,
but these great assemblies of Bodhisattvas,
for countless millions of kalpas,
for the sake of the Buddha path, have diligently practiced,
skillfully entered, emerged from, and dwelt in countless hundreds of thousands of millions of samādhis,
attained great spiritual powers,
long cultivated pure conduct,
skillfully and gradually practiced various good Dharmas,
and are skillful in questioning and answering.
They are jewels among humans,
extremely rare in all the world.
Today the World Honored One says,
'When I attained the Buddha path,
I first caused them to arouse their minds,
and taught and guided them,
causing them to turn towards Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.'
It has not been long since the World Honored One attained Buddhahood,
yet you are able to perform such great meritorious deeds.
Although we believe the Buddha's expedient teachings,
the Buddha's words have never been false,
and all that the Buddha knows is thoroughly understood.
However, if newly initiated Bodhisattvas hear these words after the Buddha's Parinirvana,
they may not believe and accept them,
and may give rise to the cause and condition for the transgression of destroying the Dharma.
Therefore, World Honored One!
We wish you would explain and dispel our doubts,
so that good men in future generations, after hearing of this matter,
will also not give rise to doubts."
At that time, Mílè Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse,
"In the past, the Buddha came from the Shì clan,
left home near Gáyé,
and sat under the Bodhi tree;
it has not been long since then.
These children of the Buddha,
their number is immeasurable,
have long practiced the Buddha path,
and dwell in the power of spiritual powers,
skillfully learning the Bodhisattva path,
not stained by worldly Dharmas,
like lotuses in water,
emerging from the earth.
They all arise with respectful minds,
dwelling before the World Honored One.
This matter is difficult to fathom,
how can it be believed?
The Buddha's attainment of the path is very recent,
the accomplishments are very many,
we wish you would dispel the doubts of the assembly,
and explain the truth separately.
It is like a young and strong man,
only twenty-five years old,
showing a hundred-year-old child,
with white hair and wrinkled face,
and saying, 'These are born of me;'
the child also says this is my father.
The father is young and the child is old,
the whole world does not believe it."
The World-Honored One is also like this,
having attained the Way for a very long time.
These Bodhisattvas and others,
their resolve is firm and without weakness,
from limitless kalpas past,
they have practiced the Bodhisattva path,
skilled in answering difficult questions,
their minds without fear,
their minds resolute in patience and forbearance,
upright, possessing majesty and virtue,
praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
They are skilled in clearly distinguishing and speaking,
not delighting in assemblies of people,
constantly preferring to be in meditation,
for the sake of seeking the Buddha path,
dwelling in the lower empty space.
We have heard from the Buddha,
and have no doubt about this matter,
we wish that the Buddha, for the sake of the future,
would expound and illuminate this.
If there are those who, regarding this sūtra,
give rise to doubt and disbelief,
they will then fall into evil destinies.
We wish now for an explanation,
how these immeasurable Bodhisattvas,
in a short time,
teach and cause them to generate the aspiration [for enlightenment],
and abide in the ground of non-retrogression?
At that time, the Buddha told the Bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly:
"Good men! You should believe and understand the true and sincere words of the *Rúlái*."
Again, he told the great assembly:
"You should believe and understand the true and sincere words of the *Rúlái*."
Again, he told the great assembly:
"You should believe and understand the true and sincere words of the *Rúlái*."
At this time, the great assembly of Bodhisattvas, with *Mílè* as their head,
joined their palms and said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! We only wish that you would speak of it,
we will believe and accept the Buddha's words."
Having said this three times, they again said:
"We only wish that you would speak of it, we will believe and accept the Buddha's words."
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that the Bodhisattvas had requested him three times without ceasing, told them:
"Listen carefully, to the secret, spiritual power of the *Rúlái*.
All the gods and humans, and *Āxiūluó* in the world, all say:
'Now *Shìjiāmóunífó*, having left the *Shì* clan palace,
not far from *Jiāyé* city, sits at the place of enlightenment,
and attains *ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí*.'
However, good men!
I have actually attained Buddhahood for immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of *Nàyōutā* kalpas.
For example, imagine five hundred, thousands of millions of *Nàyōutā Āsēngqí* great chiliocosms; suppose someone ground them into dust,
and after passing eastward through five hundred, thousands of millions of *Nàyōutā Āsēngqí* lands, dropped one speck of dust,
and continued eastward in this way until all the specks of dust were exhausted.
Good men! What do you think?
Can these worlds be conceived of or calculated to know their number?'"
*Mílè* Bodhisattva and the others all said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One! These worlds are immeasurable and boundless,
not knowable by calculation,
nor reachable by the power of the mind;
all *shēngwén* and *pìzhīfó*, with their unconditioned wisdom, cannot conceive of or know their limit;
we abide in the ground of *āwéiyuèzhì*,
and in this matter we are also unable to reach it.
World-Honored One! These worlds are immeasurable and boundless."
At that time, the Buddha told the great assembly of Bodhisattvas:
Good men!
Now I will clearly proclaim it to you.
If all these worlds, whether touched by specks of dust or not, were turned into dust,
and one speck of dust equaled one kalpa,
the time since I attained Buddhahood
would still exceed hundreds of thousands of millions of *Nàyōutā Āsēngqí* kalpas.
Since that time,
I have constantly been in this *Suōpó* world teaching and transforming [beings],
and also in hundreds of thousands of millions of *Nàyōutā Āsēngqí* lands elsewhere, guiding and benefiting sentient beings.
Good men!
In between, I spoke of *Rándēngfó* and others,
and again said that they entered into *nièpán*;
all of this was skillful means and distinctions.
Good men!
If there are sentient beings who come to my place,
I use my Buddha eye to observe the sharpness or dullness of their roots of faith and other qualities,
and according to what they should be delivered by,
I speak of myself in different places, with different names and ages,
and also declare that I will enter into *nièpán*;
also, with various skillful means, I speak of the subtle Dharma,
which can cause sentient beings to generate joyful minds.
Good men!
The *Rúlái* sees that sentient beings delight in the small Dharma and are of meager virtue and heavy defilements,
and for those people, I say, "I left home when young and attained *ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí*."
But I have actually attained Buddhahood for so long,
but with skillful means, I teach and transform sentient beings,
causing them to enter the Buddha path,
and make such statements.
Good men!
The sūtras proclaimed by the *Rúlái* are all for delivering sentient beings,
sometimes speaking of my own body,
sometimes speaking of others' bodies,
sometimes showing my own body,
sometimes showing others' bodies,
sometimes showing my own affairs,
sometimes showing others' affairs,
all that is spoken is true and not false.
Why is this?
The *Rúlái* truly knows and sees the characteristics of the triple world,
without birth or death, without retreat or emergence,
also without being in the world or passing into extinction,
neither real nor unreal,
neither like nor unlike,
not like how the triple world sees the triple world,
such things as these, the *Rúlái* clearly sees, without error or mistake.
Because sentient beings have various natures, various desires, various practices,
and various recollections, thoughts, and discriminations,
wishing to cause them to generate all kinds of good roots,
with various causes, conditions, metaphors, and words, I preach the Dharma in various ways,
and the Buddha-works I do
have never been paused for even a moment.
Thus,
since I attained Buddhahood,
it has been a very long time,
my lifespan is immeasurable *Āsēngqí* kalpas,
constantly abiding and not ceasing.
Good men!
The lifespan I attained from my original practice of the Bodhisattva path has still not ended,
and is again double the number above.
Yet, I am not truly passing into extinction,
but proclaim, "I will take extinction."
The *Rúlái* uses these skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings.
Why is this?
If the Buddha dwells in the world for a long time,
those of meager virtue will not plant good roots,
[but remain] poor and lowly,
grasping at the five desires,
and enter into the net of recollections, thoughts, and false views.
If they see that the *Rúlái* is constantly present and does not cease,
they will then give rise to arrogance and indolence,
and not generate the thought of encountering the rare and the difficult, or a respectful mind.
Therefore, the *Rúlái* speaks with skillful means:
"Bhikṣus, you should know that it is difficult to encounter the Buddhas appearing in the world."
Why is this?
Those of meager virtue, after passing through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, sometimes see the Buddha,
and sometimes do not see [the Buddha].
For this reason, I say:
"Bhikṣus! The *Rúlái* is difficult to see."
When these sentient beings hear these words,
they will surely generate the thought of encountering the rare and the difficult,
and their hearts will be filled with longing,
thirsting and yearning for the Buddha,
and then plant good roots.
Therefore, the *Rúlái*, although not truly ceasing,
speaks of ceasing into extinction.
Moreover, good men!
The Dharmas of all Buddhas and *Rúlái* are all like this,
for the sake of delivering sentient beings, all is true and not false.
For example, there is a good doctor,
wise and intelligent,
clear and skilled in formulas and medicines,
good at treating all diseases.
That person has many children—perhaps ten,
twenty, or even hundreds.
Due to some matter, he goes far away to another country.
Afterwards, the children drink another's poison,
the poison takes effect and they become muddled and confused,
writhing on the ground.
At that time, their father returns home,
the children who drank the poison,
some having lost their minds,
and some not having lost them,
see their father from afar,
and are all greatly joyful, bowing and prostrating in greeting:
"You have returned safely and peacefully.
We are foolish and mistakenly took poison,
we wish to be saved and cured, and granted longer lives."
The father sees his children's suffering like this,
and according to the formulas and prescriptions,
seeks good medicinal herbs,
with complete color, fragrance, and delicious taste,
pounds, sifts, and mixes them together
and gives them to his children to take,
and says,
"This is a great and good medicine,
with complete color, fragrance, and delicious taste,
you should take it, quickly eliminate your suffering, and have no more illnesses."
Those among the children who have not lost their minds, seeing this good medicine, with both color and fragrance good,
immediately take it,
and their illnesses are completely cured.
The remaining ones who have lost their minds, seeing their father come, although they are also joyful in greeting,
and seek to be cured,
nevertheless, when given the medicine, are unwilling to take it.
Why is this?
Because the poisonous energy has penetrated deeply,
and they have lost their original minds,
and regard this good, fragrant medicine as not delicious.
The father had this thought:
'This son is pitiable,
poisoned by toxins,
his mind is completely inverted.
Although he sees that I am happy and seeks healing,
he is unwilling to take such good medicine.
I should now devise a skillful means to make him take this medicine.'
Immediately, he said:
'You should know! I am now old and declining,
the time of my death has arrived,
this is good medicine, now left here,
you can take it, do not worry that it will not heal you.'
After giving this teaching,
he went to another country, and sent a messenger back to say:
'Your father has died.'
At that time, the sons heard of their father's death,
were greatly distressed and thought:
'If father were here, he would have compassion on us,
and be able to save and protect us,
but now he has abandoned us and died far away in another country.'
Thinking themselves orphaned and without support,
constantly feeling sad,
their minds finally awakened,
and they realized that the color, taste, and fragrance of this medicine were good,
so they took it,
and all their poisonous diseases were cured.
The father heard that his sons were all healed,
and immediately returned,
and made them all see him.
"Good men!
What do you think?
Is there anyone who can say that this good doctor is guilty of falsehood?"
"No, World-Honored One!"
The Buddha said: "I am also like this,
since becoming a Buddha, for immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of *nayuta* *asaṃkhya* of *kalpas*,
for the sake of sentient beings,
with the power of skillful means, I say that I will pass into extinction,
and there is no one who can rightfully say that I am guilty of falsehood."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wanting to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Since I attained Buddhahood,
the *kalpas* I have passed through,
are immeasurable hundreds of thousands,
of millions of *asaṃkhya* of *kalpas*,
I constantly preach the Dharma and teach,
countless millions of sentient beings,
leading them into the Buddha path.
Since then, for immeasurable *kalpas*,
for the sake of saving sentient beings,
I expediently manifest *nirvāṇa*,
but in reality do not pass into extinction,
I constantly dwell here and preach the Dharma.
I constantly dwell here,
with all kinds of supernatural powers,
causing inverted sentient beings,
although near, not to see me.
The multitudes see my extinction,
widely make offerings to my *śarīra*,
all cherish longing and admiration,
and give rise to thirsting and yearning minds.
Once sentient beings have faith and submission,
with honest and upright minds, gentle and pliable,
wholeheartedly desiring to see the Buddha,
not sparing their own lives.
Then I and the *saṃgha*,
together emerge from Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain,
At that time I tell sentient beings:
'I constantly dwell here and do not pass into extinction,
because of the power of skillful means,
I manifest both extinction and non-extinction.'
If there are sentient beings in other lands,
who respectfully believe and delight,
I again in their midst,
preach the unsurpassed Dharma.
You do not hear of this,
but only think that I have passed into extinction.
I see that all sentient beings,
are submerged in suffering and affliction,
therefore I do not manifest my body,
causing them to give rise to thirst and yearning,
because of their longing and admiration,
I then emerge to preach the Dharma.
My supernatural powers are like this,
for *asaṃkhya* of *kalpas*,
I constantly dwell on Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain,
and in other dwelling places.
When sentient beings see the *kalpa* coming to an end,
and being burned by great fires,
my land is peaceful and secure,
always filled with gods and humans.
Gardens, groves, pavilions and halls,
adorned with all kinds of jewels,
jewel trees with many flowers and fruits,
where sentient beings play and enjoy themselves.
The gods strike heavenly drums,
constantly making all kinds of music,
raining *mandārava* flowers,
scattering them upon the Buddha and the great assembly.
My pure land is not destroyed,
but the multitudes see it burning to ashes,
filled with sorrow, fear and all kinds of suffering and affliction.
All such is filled.
These sentient beings burdened with sins,
because of the cause and condition of evil karma,
for *asaṃkhya* of *kalpas*,
do not hear the name of the Three Jewels.
All those who cultivate merit and virtue,
who are gentle, pliable, honest and upright,
will all see my body,
here preaching the Dharma.
Sometimes for this assembly,
I preach that the Buddha's life is immeasurable,
and for those who see the Buddha after a long time,
I preach that it is difficult to encounter a Buddha.
My power of wisdom is like this,
the light of wisdom illuminates immeasurably,
my lifespan is countless *kalpas*,
obtained through long cultivation of karma.
You who are wise,
do not give rise to doubts about this,
you should cut them off completely and forever,
the Buddha's words are truly not false.
Like a skilled doctor with expedient means,
for the sake of curing his mad sons,
although alive, says that he is dead,
no one can say that he is false.
I am also a father to the world,
saving all those who suffer,
for the sake of deluded common people,
although truly existing, I say that I pass into extinction.
Because they constantly see me,
they give rise to arrogant and self-indulgent minds,
are lax and attached to the five desires,
and fall into evil paths.
I constantly know all sentient beings,
whether they practice the Way or do not practice the Way,
according to what is appropriate to be saved,
I preach all kinds of Dharma.
I constantly make this thought,
by what means can I cause sentient beings,
to enter unsurpassed wisdom,
and quickly accomplish the Buddha body.
At that time, the great assembly, hearing the Buddha speak of his lifespan being so long,
immeasurable and boundless *asaṃkhya* of sentient beings obtained great benefit.
At that time, the World-Honored One told the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mílè Púsà Móhēsà:
"*Āyìduō*!
When I spoke of the Thus Come One's lifespan being long,
six hundred and eighty myriads of millions of *nayuta* of Ganges sands of sentient beings,
obtained the *anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*;
furthermore, there were a thousand times as many Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
who obtained the *dhāraṇī* gate of hearing and holding;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of one world,
who obtained the eloquence of delightful speech without obstruction;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of one world,
who obtained hundreds of thousands of millions of immeasurable *旋dhāraṇī*;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of three thousand great thousand worlds,
who were able to turn the irreversible Dharma wheel;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of two middle-sized lands,
who were able to turn the pure Dharma wheel;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of one small-sized land,
who in eight more lives will obtain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of four sets of four continents,
who in four more lives will obtain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of three sets of four continents,
who in three more lives will obtain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of two sets of four continents,
who in two more lives will obtain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
furthermore, there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas equal to the fine dust particles of one set of four continents,
who in one more life will obtain *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
furthermore, there were sentient beings equal to the fine dust particles of eight worlds, who all gave rise to the mind of *anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
When the Buddha spoke of these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas obtaining great Dharma benefit,
in the empty sky, *mandārava* flowers and *mahā-mandārava* flowers rained down,
scattering over the countless hundreds of thousands of millions of jeweled trees, the Buddhas on the lion thrones,
and also scattering over Śākyamuni Buddha and the long-since extinct *Duōbǎo Rúlái* on the lion throne in the seven-jeweled tower,
and also scattering over all the great Bodhisattvas and the fourfold assembly.
Furthermore, fine powder of sandalwood and *沉水香* incense rained down.
In the empty sky, heavenly drums sounded by themselves,
the wonderful sound deep and far-reaching.
Furthermore, a thousand kinds of heavenly clothing rained down,
hanging various garlands, pearl garlands, *maṇi* pearl garlands, *cintāmaṇi* pearl garlands,
throughout the nine directions.
Jeweled incense burners burned priceless incense,
naturally circulating to the great assembly as offerings.
On each and every Buddha, there were Bodhisattvas, holding banners and canopies,
rising in order, up to the Brahma heaven.
These Bodhisattvas, with wonderful sounds, sang immeasurable songs, praising all the Buddhas.
At that time, Mílè Púsà rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder,
joined his palms towards the Buddha,
and spoke in verse:
The Buddha spoke of rare Dharma,
never heard of in the past.
The World-Honored One has great power,
His lifespan is immeasurable.
Countless sons of the Buddhas,
hearing the World-Honored One's explanation,
those who received the benefit of the Dharma,
were filled with joy throughout their bodies.
Some dwelled in the ground of non-retrogression,
some attained *tuóluóní*,
some had unobstructed eloquence,
and myriad *xuán* holding all things in mind.
Some had *dàqiān* worlds, as many as dust motes, *púsà*,
each and every one of them able to turn
the wheel of Dharma of non-retrogression.
Again, there were *zhōngqiān* worlds,
as many as dust motes, *púsà*,
each and every one of them able to turn
the pure wheel of Dharma.
Again, there were *xiǎoqiān* worlds,
as many as dust motes, *púsà*, who
each had eight more lives before attaining Buddhahood.
Again, there were four, three, or two, such *sìtiānxià*, as many as dust motes, *púsà*,
who would generate Buddhahood according to their number.
Some had one *sìtiānxià*, as many as dust motes, *púsà*,
who had one more life before
attaining all-knowing wisdom.
Such beings as these,
hearing of the Buddha's long lifespan,
obtained immeasurable, undefiled, pure fruition.
Again, there were eight world realms,
as many as dust motes, sentient beings,
hearing the Buddha speak of His lifespan,
all generated unsurpassed bodhicitta.
The World-Honored One spoke of immeasurable, inconceivable Dharma,
which greatly benefited many,
like the boundless sky.
Raining down *tiān màntuóluó*, *móhē màntuóluó*,
*Shì*, *Fàn* like the Ganges' sands,
coming from countless Buddha-lands.
Raining down sandalwood and agarwood,
falling in a colorful and scattered manner,
like birds flying down from the sky,
offered and scattered upon all the Buddhas.
Heavenly drums in the empty sky
naturally produced wonderful sounds,
heavenly garments of myriad kinds
spun around and came down.
Incense burners of various treasures,
burning priceless incense,
naturally pervaded everywhere, offering it to all the World-Honored Ones.
The great *púsà* assembly,
holding jeweled banners and canopies,
lofty and wonderful in ten thousand *yì* kinds,
ascended in order to the Brahma Heaven.
Before each and every Buddha,
precious banners hung victorious pennants,
and also with ten million *jì*
sang the praises of all the *Rúlái*.
Such various events
had never occurred before;
hearing of the Buddha's immeasurable lifespan,
all were delighted.
The Buddha's name was heard in the ten directions,
greatly benefiting sentient beings;
all possessed roots of goodness,
to assist unsurpassed bodhicitta.
At that time, the Buddha told *Mílè Púsà mó訶sà*: "*Āyìduō*!
If there are sentient beings who hear of the Buddha's long lifespan,
and even generate a single thought of faith and understanding,
the merit they obtain will be limitless.
If there are good men and good women
who, for the sake of *ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí*,
for eighty *wàn yì nàyóutā* kalpas,
practice the five *bōluómì*—*dānbōluómì*,
*shīlā bōluómì*, *chàntíbōluómì*, *pílíyé bōluómì*, *chánbōluómì*—
excluding *bānruò bōluómì*,
if this merit were compared to the former merit, even one hundredth, one thousandth, one hundred millionth, one hundred millionth, or one *yì*th part would not equal it,
not even calculative numbers and analogies could know it.
If good men and good women have such merit,
there is no possibility that they will retrogress from *ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí*."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
If a person seeks the wisdom of the Buddha,
for eighty *wàn yì*,
*nàyóutā* kalpas,
practices the five *bōluómì*.
In all these kalpas,
giving offerings to the Buddhas,
*yuánjué* disciples,
and all the *púsà* assemblies.
Rare and exquisite food and drink,
fine clothing and bedding,
sandalwood *lì jīngshè*,
adorned with gardens and forests.
Such almsgiving,
all kinds are subtle and wonderful;
exhausting all these kalpas,
to dedicate to the path of Buddhahood.
If again, they uphold the precepts,
pure, without defect or leakage,
seeking the unsurpassed path,
praised by all the Buddhas.
If again, they practice forbearance,
dwelling in a tamed and gentle state,
even if various evils come and add to them,
their minds are not moved.
All those who have attained the Dharma,
harboring increasing arrogance,
being slighted and annoyed by this,
are also able to endure it.
If again, they diligently advance,
their aspirations constantly firm and steadfast,
for immeasurable *yì* kalpas,
with one mind, never resting.
And again, for countless kalpas,
dwelling in quiet, secluded places,
whether sitting or walking,
they eliminate sleep and constantly collect their minds.
Because of these causes and conditions,
they are able to generate all kinds of *chándìng*,
for eighty *yì wàn* kalpas,
dwelling in unwavering minds.
Holding this one-mind merit,
aspiring to the unsurpassed path,
"I will attain all-knowing wisdom,
exhausting all the bounds of *chándìng*."
If a person for hundreds of thousands,
of myriad *yì* kalpas,
practices all these merits,
as described above.
If there are good men and women,
who hear me speak of my lifespan,
and even have a single thought of faith,
their merit surpasses that of the former.
If a person is completely without
all doubts and regrets,
with a profound mind, believing for even a moment,
their merit will be like this.
If there are *púsà*
who for countless kalpas practice the path,
hearing me speak of my lifespan,
they will then be able to believe and accept it.
Such people as these,
receive this sutra at the crown of their heads,
"May I in the future,
live long and deliver sentient beings.
Like the World-Honored One today,
the king among the *Shì*,
roaring like a lion in the *dàochǎng*,
speaking the Dharma without fear.
We in the future world,
all whom we respect,
when sitting in the *dàochǎng*,
will also speak of our lifespan in this way.
If there are those with profound minds,
pure and upright,
learned, able to hold all things in mind,
explaining the Buddha's words according to their meaning,
such people as these
will have no doubts about this."
Again, *Āyìduō*!
If there are those who hear of the Buddha's long lifespan,
and understand the meaning of His words,
the merit these people obtain is limitless,
and they will be able to generate the unsurpassed wisdom of the *Rúlái*.
How much more so if they widely hear this sutra, or teach others to hear it,
if they personally uphold it, or teach others to uphold it,
if they personally write it, or teach others to write it,
if they use flowers, incense, necklaces, banners, pennants, silken canopies,
scented oil, or ghee lamps to make offerings to the sutra scroll,
the merit of these people will be immeasurable and boundless,
and they will be able to generate all-knowing wisdom.
*Āyìduō*!
If good men and good women
hear me speak of my long lifespan,
and deeply believe and understand,
then they will see the Buddha constantly abiding on *Qíshéjué Shān*,
surrounded by great *púsà* and *shēngwén* assemblies, speaking the Dharma.
And they will also see this *Suōpó* world,
its ground of *liúlí*, level and even,
with *yánfú tánjīn* used to mark eight paths,
rows of jeweled trees, all terraces and pavilions made of jewels,
with all the *púsà* assemblies dwelling within.
If there are those who are able to contemplate in this way,
you should know that this is the sign of deep faith and understanding.
Moreover, after the Tathāgata's extinction,
if one hears this sūtra and does not revile it,
but gives rise to a joyful mind, know that this is already a sign of deep faith and understanding,
how much more so for those who read, recite, receive, and uphold it?
Such a person is said to be revering the Tathāgata.
"Āyìduō!
These good men and good women need not again erect stupas and temples for me,
