nor construct Saṃgha residences and offer the four requisites to the Saṃgha.
Why is that?
Because these good men and good women who receive, uphold, read, and recite this scripture
have already erected stupas, built Saṃgha residences, and made offerings to the Saṃgha.
It is as if they have built a seven-jeweled stupa with the Buddha's relics,
tall and wide, gradually diminishing in size up to the Brahmā heaven,
hung with various banners and canopies and jeweled bells,
flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, scented paste, burning incense, various drums, music, flutes, pipes, and harps,
and all kinds of dance performances,
using wonderful sounds to sing and praise.
It is as if they have already made these offerings for limitless, countless millions of kalpas.
Āyìduō!
If, after my extinction, upon hearing this scripture, someone is able to receive and uphold it,
whether writing it themselves or having others write it,
it is as if they have erected Saṃgha residences,
using red sandalwood to build thirty-two palaces and halls,
each eight *duōluó* trees in height,
tall, wide, adorned, and beautiful,
with hundreds of thousands of Bhikṣus residing within,
with gardens, bathing ponds, places for walking meditation, and meditation caves,
clothing, food, bedding, and medicine,
all kinds of delightful things filling them.
Such Saṃgha residences and halls, numbering several hundreds of thousands of millions, are immeasurable in number,
and with these, they make present offerings to me and the Bhikṣu Saṃgha.
Therefore, I say:
'After the Tathāgata's extinction, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite, and explain it for others,
whether writing it themselves or having others write it, and offer the scripture rolls,
there is no need to again erect stupas and temples, nor to build Saṃgha residences and make offerings to the Saṃgha.'
How much more so if someone can uphold this sūtra,
and also practice giving, upholding the precepts, patience, endurance, diligence, one-mindedness, and wisdom,
their virtue is the most excellent,
limitless and boundless.
It is like empty space, which is limitless and boundless in the east, west, south, north, four intermediate directions, above, and below;
the merit of this person is also limitless and boundless in the same way,
quickly reaching all-knowing wisdom.
If someone reads, recites, and upholds this sūtra, explains it for others,
whether writing it themselves or having others write it,
and also erects stupas, builds Saṃgha residences, and makes offerings to and praises the Śrāvaka Saṃgha,
and also uses hundreds of thousands of millions of methods of praise to praise the merits of the Bodhisattvas,
and also for others, using various causes and conditions, explains this *Fǎ Huā* Sūtra according to its meaning,
and is also able to purely uphold the precepts,
dwelling together with those who are gentle and harmonious,
patient and without anger,
with resolute mindfulness,
constantly valuing seated meditation and attaining various deep states of samādhi,
diligently and bravely gathering all good dharmas,
with sharp faculties and wisdom, skillfully answering difficult questions.
Āyìduō!
If, after my extinction, good men and good women receive, uphold, read, and recite this scripture,
and also have such various good merits,
know that this person has already approached the Bodhimaṇḍa,
is close to Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi, and sits beneath the Bodhi tree.
"Āyìduō!
These good men and good women, whether sitting, standing, or walking,
in these places, one should erect a stupa,
and all gods and humans should make offerings to it as to a Buddha's stupa."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
If after my extinction,
one can uphold this sūtra,
this person's fortune is immeasurable,
as described above,
this is to be complete
with all offerings.
Using relics to erect a stupa,
adorned with seven jewels,
the flagpole is very tall and wide,
gradually diminishing to the Brahmā heaven,
jeweled bells in the millions of billions,
the wind stirs and emits wonderful sounds.
And for limitless kalpas,
make offerings to this stupa,
flowers, incense, and all kinds of necklaces,
heavenly garments and various musical instruments,
burning incense, oil, and ghee lamps,
constantly illuminating all around.
In the evil age of the Dharma's decline,
if one can uphold this sūtra,
it is as if, as above,
If one can uphold this sūtra,
it is as if the Buddha is present,
using sandalwood from Ox-Head Mountain,
to erect Saṃgha residences and make offerings.
The halls are thirty-two,
each eight *duōluó* trees in height,
the finest food and wonderful clothing, beds and bedding are all complete,
hundreds and thousands dwell there,
gardens and various bathing ponds,
places for walking meditation and meditation caves,
all kinds are adorned and beautiful.
If one has a believing and understanding mind,
receives, upholds, reads, and writes,
or also causes others to write,
and makes offerings to the scripture rolls,
scattering flowers and powdered incense,
using *xūmàn*, *zhānbo*, *ētímùduōjiā*, scented oil constantly burns.
Such an offering,
obtains immeasurable merit,
like the limitlessness of empty space,
so too is this fortune.
How much more so to uphold this sūtra,
and also practice giving and upholding the precepts,
patience, delight in meditation and samādhi,
without anger or harsh speech,
reverent towards stupas and temples,
humble before all the Bhikṣus,
far removed from arrogance,
constantly contemplating wisdom,
if there are questions and difficulties, without anger,
explain them accordingly,
if one can practice these practices,
the merit is immeasurable.
If one sees this Dharma master,
accomplishing such virtues,
one should scatter heavenly flowers,
cover their body with heavenly garments,
prostrate with head and face at their feet,
giving rise to a mind like the Buddha's.
One should also have this thought:
'Before long, they will reach the Bodhi tree,
attain the unconditioned and non-active,
widely benefiting humans and gods.'
In the place where they dwell,
whether walking, sitting, or lying down,
even if they speak a single verse,
in that place one should erect a stupa,
adorn it to be wonderful and beautiful,
make offerings in various ways.
A Buddha's son dwelling in this place,
is that which the Buddha enjoys,
constantly within it,
walking, sitting, and lying down.
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* Scroll Five
*Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* Scroll Six
By Tripiṭaka Master *Jūmóluóshí* of the *Qiūcí* Kingdom of the Later *Qín*,
translated by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva *Mílè* said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
If there are good men and good women
who, upon hearing this *Fǎ Huā* Sūtra, rejoice accordingly,
how much fortune will they obtain?"
And spoke in verse, saying:
After the World-Honored One's extinction,
if there are those who hear this sūtra,
if they can rejoice accordingly,
how much fortune will they obtain?
At that time, the Buddha told Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva *Mílè*:
Āyìduō! After the Tathāgata's extinction,
if Bhikṣus, Bhikṣuṇīs, Upāsakas, Upāsikās,
and other wise people, whether old or young,
having heard this sūtra and rejoiced accordingly,
depart from the Dharma assembly,
and go to other places,
whether in Saṃgha residences,
or secluded places,
or cities, lanes, villages, fields,
according to what they have heard,
explain it to the best of their ability for parents, relatives, good friends, and acquaintances.
These people,
having heard it and rejoiced accordingly,
further proceed to teach others;
other people, having heard it,
also rejoice accordingly and teach others.
In this way, passing it on, up to the fiftieth person.
Āyìduō! The merit of the fiftieth good man or good woman who rejoices accordingly,
I will now describe it,
you should listen carefully.
If in four hundred million *a僧祇* worlds, beings of the six realms and four kinds of birth—
born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, born from transformation,
whether with form or without form,
with thought or without thought,
neither with thought nor without thought,
without feet, with two feet, with four feet, with many feet,
such beings as are numbered among living beings—
someone seeking fortune,
gives to them all the means of enjoyment according to their desires.
To each and every living being,
gives the entire *yánfú* world filled with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *chēqú*, agate, coral, and amber,
various precious treasures,
and elephants, horses, carriages,
palaces and pavilions made of the seven jewels, and so on.
This great benefactor,
having made such offerings for a full eighty years,
then has this thought:
"I have already provided all beings with the means of entertainment,
as they desire.
However, these beings are all aged and over eighty,
with white hair and wrinkled faces,
and will soon die.
I should instruct them with the Buddha-dharma."
Then he gathered these beings
and announced the Dharma transformation,
instructing, teaching, benefiting, and pleasing them.
In a short time, they all attained the path of Sūrotaāpanna,
the path of Sakṛdāgāmin,
the path of Anāgāmin,
the path of Arhat,
exhausted all outflows,
were all free in deep meditation,
and possessed the eight liberations.
What do you think?
Is the merit obtained by this great benefactor not great?"
Mílè (彌勒) said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
This person's merit is very great,
immeasurable and boundless.
If a benefactor only gives all beings the means of happiness,
the merit is immeasurable;
how much more so if he enables them to attain the fruit of an Arhat!"
The Buddha told Mílè (彌勒):
"I will now clearly tell you,
that if this person uses all means of happiness
to give to the beings in the six realms of four hundred million *asaṃkhya* worlds,
and also enables them to attain the fruit of an Arhat,
the merit obtained is not as great as that of the fiftieth person
who hears a verse of the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* (法華經) and rejoices.
One hundredth, one thousandth, one hundred millionth part cannot compare to it,
even to the extent that calculation and analogy cannot know it.
Āyìduō (阿逸多)!
The merit of the fiftieth person who hears the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* (法華經) and rejoices in turn
is still immeasurable and boundless *asaṃkhya*.
How much more so is the merit of the first person who hears and rejoices in the assembly, whose blessings are even greater,
immeasurable and boundless *asaṃkhya*, beyond comparison.
Furthermore, Āyìduō (阿逸多)!
If a person, for the sake of this Sutra, goes to a monastic residence,
whether sitting or standing, briefly listens and receives,
through this merit,
in the next life, they will obtain excellent and wonderful elephants, horses, carriages,
precious jeweled palanquins,
and ride in heavenly palaces.
If someone is sitting in a place where the Dharma is being expounded,
and another person comes
and encourages them to sit and listen,
or shares their seat to let them sit,
this person's merit will lead them to be reborn in the seat of *Dìshì* (帝釋),
the seat of Brahmā,
or the seat of a *zhuǎnlún shèngwáng* (轉輪聖王).
Āyìduō (阿逸多)! If someone says to another person:
'There is a Sutra called the *Fǎ Huá*, we can go together to listen to it.'
Immediately accepting their teaching, even
if they hear for a brief moment, this person's merit will lead them to be reborn in the same place as a *Tuóluóní* (陀羅尼) Bodhisattva,
with sharp roots and wisdom, for hundreds of
millions of lifetimes they will never be mute,
their breath will not be foul, their tongue will always be free from disease, their mouth will also be free from disease, their teeth will not be dirty, black, or yellow, not sparse,
nor missing, not crooked,
their lips will not droop nor be contracted, not coarse or rough, without sores or pimples,
also not broken, also not slanted,
not thick, not large,
also not dark black, without any unpleasantness.
Their nose will not be flat, also not crooked,
their complexion will not be dark,
also not narrow and long,
also not concave,
without any displeasing features.
Their lips, tongue, and teeth will all be perfectly adorned,
their nose will be tall and straight,
their face will be round and full,
their eyebrows will be high and long,
their forehead will be broad and even,
possessing all the marks of a great person,
in every lifetime,
they will see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and faithfully receive the teachings.
Āyìduō (阿逸多)! You should observe this,
that encouraging one person to go and listen to the Dharma
has such merit.
How much more so is the merit of listening, speaking, reciting wholeheartedly,
and explaining it to others in the assembly,
practicing according to the teachings?"
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
If a person in a Dharma assembly,
is able to hear this Sutra,
even just one verse,
and rejoices in telling it to others,
and thus teaches in turn,
until the fiftieth person,
the last person who obtains blessings,
I will now explain it separately.
If there is a great benefactor,
who provides for countless people,
completely for eighty years,
according to their desires.
Seeing their aging appearance,
with white hair and wrinkled faces,
sparse teeth and dried-up forms,
thinking that they will soon die,
I should now teach them,
and enable them to attain the fruit of the path.
Then, expediently speaking,
the true Dharma of *Nièpán* (涅槃),
the world is not firm,
like foam, bubbles, and flames,
you all should,
quickly generate a mind of aversion and detachment.
When these people hear this Dharma,
they all attain the state of an *Āluóhàn* (阿羅漢),
complete with the six supernormal powers,
the three insights and the eight liberations.
The last, the fiftieth person,
hearing one verse and rejoicing,
this person's merit surpasses them,
it cannot be compared.
Thus hearing in turn,
their blessings are still immeasurable,
how much more so in the Dharma assembly,
the first to hear and rejoice.
If someone encourages one person,
to lead them to listen to the *Fǎ Huá*,
saying this Sutra is profound and wonderful,
difficult to encounter in millions of *jié*,
immediately accepting the teaching and going to listen,
even hearing for a brief moment,
this person's blessings and rewards,
I will now explain separately.
In every lifetime, they will have no mouth ailments,
their teeth will not be sparse, yellow, or black,
their lips will not be thick, contracted, or missing,
without any unpleasant features,
their tongue will not be dry, black, or short,
their nose will be tall, long, and straight,
their forehead will be broad and even,
their facial features will all be upright and dignified,
pleasing to people's eyes,
their breath will have no foul odor,
the fragrance of the *yōubōhuā* (優鉢華),
will always come from their mouth.
If purposely going to a monastic residence,
wishing to listen to the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
briefly hearing and rejoicing,
I will now speak of their blessings.
Reborn in the heavens or among humans,
obtaining wonderful elephants, horses, and carriages,
palanquins of precious jewels,
and riding in heavenly palaces.
If in a place where the Dharma is expounded,
encouraging people to sit and listen to the Sutra,
through this blessed cause and condition, obtaining
the seats of *Shìfàn* (釋梵) and *zhuǎnlún* (轉輪).
How much more so is the merit of wholeheartedly listening,
explaining its meaning and purpose,
practicing according to the teachings,
their blessings are immeasurable.
At that time, the Buddha told the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cháng Jīngjìn (常精進):
"If good men or good women receive and uphold this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* (法華經),
whether reading, reciting, explaining,
or writing it,
these people will obtain eight hundred merits of the eye, one thousand two hundred merits of the ear,
eight hundred merits of the nose, one thousand two hundred merits of the tongue, eight hundred merits of the body, one thousand two hundred merits of the mind.
Using these merits, they will adorn the six senses, making them all pure.
These good men and good women,
with their pure physical eyes born of their parents,
will see all the mountains, forests, rivers, and seas within and without the three thousand great thousand worlds,
down to *Ābí* (阿鼻) hell, up to the peak of existence,
and also see all beings within them,
as well as the causes and conditions of their karma, the places of their karmic retribution, they will see and know everything."
At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse, saying:
"If in a great assembly,
with a fearless mind,
you speak this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* (法華經),
listen to its merits.
This person obtains eight hundred
merits of extraordinary eyes,
by means of this adornment,
their eyes are extremely pure.
The eyes born of their parents,
will see all three thousand worlds,
within and without Mount *Mílóu* (彌樓),
*Xūmí* (須彌) and the iron mountain range,
as well as all other mountains and forests,
great seas, rivers, and waters,
down to *Ābí* (阿鼻) hell,
up to the peak of existence,
all beings within them, will all be seen.
Although not yet obtaining the heavenly eye,
the power of the physical eye is such."
“Furthermore, Cháng Jīngjìn!
If good men and good women receive and uphold this sūtra,
whether they read, recite, explain, or write it,
they will obtain twelve hundred merits of the ear.
With these pure ears,
they will hear all the various languages and sounds within and without the three-thousand-great-thousand world, from the Avīci Hell below to the Summit of Existence above— —
elephant sounds, horse sounds, cow sounds, carriage sounds,
crying sounds, lamenting sounds, conch sounds, drum sounds, bell sounds, chime sounds,
laughing sounds, speaking sounds, male voices, female voices, boy voices, girl voices,
dharma sounds, non-dharma sounds,
suffering sounds, pleasure sounds,
sounds of ordinary people, sounds of sages,
joyful sounds, unhappy sounds,
sounds of devas, sounds of nāgas, sounds of yakṣas, sounds of gandharvas, sounds of asuras, sounds of garuḍas, sounds of kiṃnaras, sounds of mahoragas,
fire sounds, water sounds, wind sounds,
hell sounds, animal sounds, hungry ghost sounds,
bhikṣu sounds, bhikṣuṇī sounds,
śrāvaka sounds, pratyekabuddha sounds,
bodhisattva sounds, buddha sounds— —
In short,
all sounds within and without in the three-thousand-great-thousand world, even without obtaining the divine ear, with the pure and ordinary ears born of parents,
they will all hear and know, distinguishing the various sounds without damaging the ear faculties.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
“The ears born of parents
are pure and without defilement;
with these ordinary ears, one hears
the sounds of the three-thousand world.
Elephant sounds, horse sounds, carriage and cow sounds,
bell, chime, conch, and drum sounds,
zither, harp, and konghou sounds,
the sounds of flutes and pipes,
pure and beautiful singing sounds,
hearing them without attachment,
the sounds of countless people,
hearing them all, one can understand them.
Also hearing the sounds of the devas,
the subtle sounds of songs,
and hearing the sounds of men and women,
the sounds of boys and girls.
In mountains, rivers, steep valleys,
the sounds of kalaviṅka birds,
jīvaṃjīvaka and other birds,
all their sounds are heard.
The sufferings and pains of hell beings,
the sounds of various tortures,
hungry ghosts oppressed by hunger and thirst,
the sounds of seeking food and drink,
the asuras and others,
dwelling by the great sea,
when they speak among themselves,
they emit great sounds.
Those who expound the dharma in this way,
abiding in this place,
hear those sounds from afar,
without damaging their ear faculties.
In the ten directions of the world,
birds and beasts call to each other,
those who expound the dharma
hear them all from here.
In the heavens of the Brahmā realm,
the Ābhāsvara and Śubhakṛtsna,
even up to the Akanishtha Heaven,
the sounds of speech,
the Dharma Master dwelling here
can hear them all.
All the bhikṣu assembly,
and the bhikṣuṇīs,
if they read and recite the sūtras,
or explain them to others,
the Dharma Master dwelling here
can hear them all.
Furthermore, there are bodhisattvas
who read and recite the sūtra dharma,
or explain it to others,
compiling and explaining its meaning,
all such sounds
can be heard.
The Buddhas, the great and holy ones,
who teach and transform sentient beings,
in the great assemblies,
expound the subtle dharma,
those who uphold this *Lotus Sūtra*
can hear them all.
The three-thousand-great-thousand world,
all sounds within and without,
from the Avīci Hell below
to the Summit of Existence above,
all their sounds are heard,
without damaging the ear faculties,
because the ears are sharp and keen,
they can all be distinguished and known.
Those who uphold this *Lotus Sūtra*,
though they have not obtained the divine ear,
but use the ears they were born with,
their merits are already like this.”
“Furthermore, Cháng Jīngjìn!
If good men and good women receive and uphold this sūtra,
whether they read, recite, explain, or write it,
they will accomplish eight hundred merits of the nose.
With these pure nasal faculties,
they will smell all the various fragrances within and without the three-thousand-great-thousand world, above and below— —
the fragrance of *sumanā* flowers, the fragrance of *jātī* flowers,
the fragrance of *mallikā* flowers, the fragrance of *campaka* flowers, the fragrance of *pāṭala* flowers,
the fragrance of red lotus flowers, the fragrance of blue lotus flowers, the fragrance of white lotus flowers,
the fragrance of flower trees, the fragrance of fruit trees,
the fragrance of *candana*, the fragrance of *aguru*, the fragrance of *tamālapattra*, the fragrance of *tagara*,
and ten million kinds of blended incense,
whether powdered, balled, or scented ointment— —
those who uphold this sūtra, dwelling in this place,
can all distinguish them.
Moreover, they can separately know the fragrances of sentient beings— —
the fragrance of elephants, the fragrance of horses, the fragrance of cows, sheep, and the like,
the fragrance of men, the fragrance of women, the fragrance of boys, the fragrance of girls,
and the fragrance of grass, trees, and forests— —
whether near or far,
all fragrances can be heard, distinguished without error.
Those who uphold this sūtra,
though dwelling here,
can also smell the fragrances of the devas in the heavens— —
the fragrance of *pārijāta* and *kovidāra* trees,
and the fragrance of *mandārava* flowers, the fragrance of *mahāmandārava* flowers,
the fragrance of *mañjūṣaka* flowers, the fragrance of *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers,
the fragrance of *candana*, *aguru*, and various powdered incenses,
the fragrance of various mixed flowers— —
the fragrance produced by the combination of such heavenly fragrances,
all are heard and known.
Moreover, they can smell the bodily fragrance of the devas— —
the fragrance of Shì Tí Huán Yīn when he is on the Palace of Victory, enjoying himself with the five desires;
the fragrance when he is in the Hall of Wonderful Dharma, expounding the dharma to the Trāyastriṃśa devas;
the fragrance when he is playing in the various gardens;
and the bodily fragrance of other devas, male and female,
all can be heard from afar.
In this way, gradually up to the Brahmā world,
even the bodily fragrance of the devas up to the Summit of Existence can be heard,
and they can also smell the incense burned by the devas.
And the fragrance of śrāvakas, the fragrance of pratyekabuddhas, the fragrance of bodhisattvas, the bodily fragrance of all the Buddhas,
can also be heard from afar,
knowing where they are.
Though smelling these fragrances,
the nasal faculties are not damaged or mistaken,
and if one wishes to distinguish them to explain them to others,
one’s memory is not mistaken.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
“This person’s nose is pure,
in this world,
whether fragrant or foul, all kinds are known.
*Sumanā*, *jātī*,
*tamālapattra*, *candana*,
*aguru* and cinnamon fragrance,
various flower and fruit fragrances,
and knowing the fragrances of sentient beings,
the fragrance of men and women,
the Dharma expounder, dwelling far away,
knows where they are by the fragrance.
The mighty Cakravartin king,
lesser Cakravartins and their sons,
ministers and palace women,
know where they are by the fragrance.
The jewels worn on their bodies,
and treasures in the ground,
the Cakravartin king’s precious daughter,
know where they are by the fragrance.
The personal ornaments of people,
clothing and necklaces,
various scented ointments,
know their bodies by the fragrance.
The devas, whether walking or sitting,
playing or displaying supernatural powers,
those who uphold this *Lotus Sūtra*,
can know them all by the fragrance.
The flowers, fruits, and seeds of trees,
and the fragrance of ghee and oil,
those who uphold the sūtra, dwelling here,
know where they are.
In deep and dangerous mountain places,
*candana* trees in full bloom,
sentient beings within them,
can know them all by the fragrance.
The Iron Ring Mountains and the great sea, sentient beings in the ground,
those who uphold the sūtra, smelling the fragrance,
know where they are.
The asura men and women,
and their retinues,
when fighting and playing,
can know them all by the fragrance.
In desolate and dangerous places,
lions, elephants, tigers, and wolves,
wild buffaloes, water buffaloes, and the like,
know where they are by the fragrance."
If there are those who are pregnant,
not yet distinguishing whether they are male or female,
without roots or non-human,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
By the power of smelling the fragrance,
they know the initial pregnancy,
whether it will succeed or not,
and give birth to a blessed child in peace and joy.
By the power of smelling the fragrance,
they know what males and females are thinking,
defiled desires, foolish anger,
and also know those who cultivate goodness.
The many hidden treasures in the earth,
gold, silver, and various jewels,
and the copper vessels that hold them,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
All kinds of ornaments,
whose value cannot be recognized,
they know their value by smelling the fragrance,
as well as their origin and location.
The various flowers in the heavens,
*mantuó*, *mànshūshā*,
*bōlìzhìduō* trees,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The various palaces in the heavens,
the differences between upper, middle, and lower,
adorned with various jewels and flowers,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The heavenly gardens, exquisite halls,
the wonderful dharma halls for viewing,
where they rejoice within,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
When the devas listen to the Dharma,
or when they experience the five desires,
whether coming, going, walking, sitting, or lying down,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The clothes worn by the heavenly women,
adorned with beautiful flowers and fragrances,
when they whirl and play,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
Ascending in this way,
even to the Brahma world,
those who enter and exit dhyana, they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The heavens of *Guāngyīn* and *Biànjìng*,
even to the Summit of Existence (*Yǒudǐng*),
their initial birth and final passing away,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The communities of *Bǐqiū*,
are constantly diligent in the Dharma,
whether sitting or walking,
and reciting the sutras,
or under the forest trees,
intently sitting in meditation,
those who uphold the sutras, by smelling the fragrance,
they can know their location.
The *Púsà* with firm resolve,
whether sitting in meditation or reciting,
or expounding the Dharma for others,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
The *Shìzūn* in every direction,
revered by all,
with compassion for the beings, expounds the Dharma,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
Beings before the Buddha,
hearing the sutras, all rejoice,
practicing according to the Dharma,
they can know everything by smelling the fragrance.
Although they have not attained the *Púsà* state, without outflows, the dharma is born in the nose,
but those who uphold this sutra,
will first obtain this nasal characteristic."
"Furthermore, *Cháng Jīngjìn*!
If good men or good women receive and uphold this sutra,
whether reading, reciting, explaining, or writing it,
they will obtain the merit of twelve hundred tongues.
Whether good or bad, beautiful or not beautiful,
and all bitter or astringent things,
on their tongues, all transform into supreme flavors, like heavenly nectar,
nothing is not delicious.
If they use their tongue to expound something in the great assembly,
they will produce a profound and wonderful sound,
that can enter their hearts,
causing them all to be joyful and happy.
Also, the heavenly sons, heavenly women, *Shì*, *Fàn* and various devas,
hearing this profound and wonderful sound, the order of their exposition and speech,
will all come to listen.
And the various *lóng*, *lóng* women, *yèchā*, *yèchā* women,
*qiántápó*, *qiántápó* women,
*āxiūluó*, *āxiūluó* women,
*jiālóuluó*, *jiālóuluó* women,
*jǐnnaluó*, *jǐnnaluó* women,
*móhóuluóqié*, *móhóuluóqié* women,
for the sake of listening to the Dharma, will all come near with respect and offerings.
And *bǐqiū*, *bǐqiūní*, *yōupósè*, *yōupóyí*,
kings, princes, ministers, and retinues,
small *zhuǎnlúnwáng*, great *zhuǎnlúnwáng*, their inner and outer retinues of seven treasures and a thousand sons,
riding in their palaces,
will all come to listen to the Dharma,
because of this *Púsà*'s skillful explanation of the Dharma.
Brahmins, laymen, and the people of the country,
for the rest of their lives, will attend and make offerings.
Also, the various *shēngwén*, *pìzhīfó*, *Púsà*, and Buddhas will constantly rejoice in seeing them.
In whatever direction this person is,
all the Buddhas will turn towards that place to expound the Dharma,
and they will be able to receive and uphold all the Buddha-dharma,
and also emit a profound and wonderful Dharma sound."
At that time, the *Shìzūn*, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
"This person's tongue is pure,
and will never experience a bad taste,
whatever they eat or consume,
will all become nectar.
With a deep and pure wonderful sound,
they expound the Dharma in the great assembly,
using various causes, conditions, and metaphors,
to guide the minds of beings,
those who hear it all rejoice,
and make various supreme offerings.
The devas, *lóng*, *yèchā*,
and *āxiūluó*, etc.,
all with respectful hearts,
come together to listen to the Dharma,
this person who expounds the Dharma,
if they wish to use a wonderful sound,
to pervade the three thousand worlds,
they can reach it at will.
The small and large *zhuǎnlúnwáng*,
and their retinues of a thousand sons,
with palms together and respectful hearts,
constantly come to listen to and receive the Dharma.
The devas, *lóng*, *yèchā*,
*luóchà*, *píshězhē*,
also with joyful hearts,
constantly rejoice to come and make offerings.
The *Fàntiānwáng*, *mówáng*,
*Zìzài*, *Dàzìzài*,
such assemblies of devas,
constantly come to their place.
The Buddhas and their disciples,
hearing the sound of their Dharma exposition,
constantly remember and protect them,
and sometimes manifest their bodies."
"Furthermore, *Cháng Jīngjìn*!
If good men or good women receive and uphold this sutra,
whether reading, reciting, explaining, or writing it,
they will obtain the merit of eight hundred bodies.
They will obtain a pure body,
like pure *liúlí*,
pleasing to the sight of beings.
Because their body is pure,
the beings of the three thousand great thousand worlds, their birth and death,
high and low, beautiful and ugly,
born in good or bad realms,
will all appear within it.
And the *Tiěwéishān*, Great *Tiěwéishān*,
*Mílóushān*, *Móhē Mílóushān* and other mountains,
and the beings within them,
will all appear within it.
Down to *Ābí* hell,
up to the Summit of Existence (*Yǒudǐng*),
all places and beings, will appear within it.
If *shēngwén*, *pìzhīfó*, *Púsà*, and Buddhas expound the Dharma,
their forms and images will all appear within their body."
At that time, the *Shìzūn*, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
"If one upholds the *Fǎhuā* Sutra,
their body will be very pure,
like that pure *liúlí*,
pleasing to the sight of all beings.
Also like a clear and bright mirror,
that clearly sees all forms and images,
the *Púsà* in their pure body,
will see all that exists in the world,
and understand it clearly themselves,
which others cannot see.
In the three thousand worlds,
all the multitudes of beings,
devas, humans, *āxiūluó*,
hell beings, ghosts, and animals,
such forms and images,
will all appear within their body.
The palaces of the devas, etc.,
even up to the Summit of Existence (*Yǒudǐng*),
*Tiěwéi* and *Mílóu*,
*Móhē Mílóushān*,
the various great oceans, etc.,
will all appear within their body.
All Buddhas and Śrāvakās,
Buddha's sons, Bodhisattvas, etc.,
Whether alone or in a assembly,
All appear while expounding the Dharma.
Although they have not yet attained the unconditioned,
The wondrous body of the Dharma-nature,
With a pure and constant essence,
All manifest within it."
"Furthermore, Cháng Jīngjìn!
If a good man or good woman, after the Tathāgata's extinction, receives and upholds this sūtra,
Whether reading, reciting, explaining, or writing it,
Will attain one thousand two hundred mind-born merits.
With this pure mind-root,
Even hearing a verse or a single phrase,
One penetrates immeasurable and boundless meanings,
Having understood these meanings,
One can expound a phrase or verse for a month, four months, or even a year.
Whatever Dharma is spoken, according to its meaning and purpose,
All is not contrary to the true reality.
If speaking of worldly scriptures, governing language, or means of livelihood,
All accords with the Proper Dharma.
The thoughts, actions, and mental activities of beings in the six realms within the three-thousand great-thousand world,
All are known.
Although one has not attained unconditioned wisdom,
Yet one's mind-root is so pure.
Whatever this person thinks, contemplates, or speaks,
Is all Buddha-dharma,
Without any untruth,
And is also what is spoken in the sūtras of the past Buddhas."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
Spoke in verse, saying:
"This person's mind is pure,
Bright, sharp, and without defilement,
With this wondrous mind-root,
Knows the superior, middling, and inferior Dharmas,
Even hearing a single verse,
Penetrates immeasurable meanings,
Explaining them sequentially according to the Dharma,
For a month, four months, or even a year.
Within and without this world, All sentient beings,
Whether gods, dragons, or humans,
Yakṣas, ghosts, or spirits,
Who are in the six realms,
And their varied thoughts,
As a reward for upholding the *Fǎ Huá*,
All are known at once.
The countless Buddhas of the ten directions,
With their hundred blessings adorned,
Expounding the Dharma for sentient beings,
All can be heard, received, and upheld.
Contemplating immeasurable meanings,
Expounding the Dharma immeasurably,
Never forgetting or making mistakes from beginning to end,
Because of upholding the *Fǎ Huá*.
All the characteristics of all Dharmas are known,
According to their meanings and sequential order,
Understanding names and languages,
Expounding them according to what is known.
Whatever this person speaks,
Is all the Dharma of the past Buddhas,
Because of expounding this Dharma,
One is fearless in the assembly.
The mind-root of one who upholds the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* Is pure like this;
Although one has not yet attained the unconditioned,
One already has such characteristics.
This person, upholding this sūtra,
Abides in a rare and wonderful ground,
Causing all sentient beings,
To rejoice, love, and respect.
Able to use thousands and millions
Of skillful means of language,
To distinguish and expound the Dharma,
Because of upholding the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*."
At that time, the Buddha told the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dé Dàshì:
"You should know now!
If a Bhikṣu, Bhikṣuṇī, Upāsaka, or Upāsikā upholds the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*,
And someone speaks evil words, curses, or slanders them,
They will receive a great karmic retribution,
As previously described;
And the merits they obtain are as described previously,
With eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind pure.
Dé Dàshì!
In the distant past,
Passing immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable Asaṃkhya kalpas,
There was a Buddha named Wēi Yīn Wáng, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna,
Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadaṃyasārathi, Śāsta devamanuṣyāṇāṃ,
Buddha, Bhagavān.
The kalpa was named Lísāi, and the country was named Dàchéng.
That Wēi Yīn Wáng Buddha, in that world,
Expounded the Dharma for gods, humans, and Asuras,
For those seeking Śrāvakabodhi,
He expounded the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths,
Saving them from birth, old age, sickness, and death,
Ultimately reaching Nirvāṇa;
For those seeking Pratyekabuddhabodhi,
He expounded the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination;
For all the Bodhisattvas,
Seeking Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi,
He expounded the Dharma of the Six Pāramitās, Ultimately attaining the Buddha-wisdom.
Dé Dàshì!
That Wēi Yīn Wáng Buddha's
lifespan was forty trillion Niyuta Gaṅgā sands kalpas;
The period of the Proper Dharma's duration in the world
Was like the dust particles of one Jambudvīpa;
The period of the Semblance Dharma's duration in the world
Was like the dust particles of the four continents.
After that Buddha had benefited beings,
He then entered Parinirvāṇa.
After the Proper Dharma and Semblance Dharma had become extinct,
In that land, another Buddha appeared,
Also named Wēi Yīn Wáng, a Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid,
Anuttara, Puruṣadaṃyasārathi, Śāsta devamanuṣyāṇāṃ, Buddha, Bhagavān.
In this sequence, there were two trillion Buddhas,
All with the same name.
After the initial Wēi Yīn Wáng Tathāgata had entered Parinirvāṇa,
And the Proper Dharma had become extinct,
During the period of the Semblance Dharma,
Arrogant Bhikṣus had great power.
At that time, there was a Bodhisattva Bhikṣu named Cháng Bùqīng.
Dé Dàshì!
What was the cause and condition for the name Cháng Bùqīng?
This Bhikṣu, whenever he saw—
Whether a Bhikṣu, Bhikṣuṇī, Upāsaka, or Upāsikā—
Would always bow and praise them, saying:
'I deeply respect you all,
And would not dare to slight you.
Why is that?
You are all practicing the Bodhisattva path and will attain Buddhahood.'
This Bhikṣu did not specialize in reading or reciting scriptures,
But only practiced bowing,
Even seeing the four assemblies from afar,
He would still go to bow and praise them, saying:
'I dare not slight you all,
For you will all become Buddhas.'
Among the four assemblies,
Some who were filled with anger
And impure minds,
Would curse and revile him, saying:
'Where did this ignorant Bhikṣu come from?
Claiming: "I do not slight you."
And giving us predictions that we will attain Buddhahood.
We do not need such false predictions.'
He endured this for many years,
Constantly being cursed and reviled,
Without becoming angry,
Always saying:
'You will attain Buddhahood.'
When he spoke these words,
People would sometimes strike him with sticks, wooden staves, tiles, or stones,
He would evade them and stay far away,
Still loudly proclaiming:
'I dare not slight you all,
For you will all become Buddhas.'
Because he constantly spoke these words,
The arrogant Bhikṣus, Bhikṣuṇīs, Upāsakas, and Upāsikās called him Cháng Bùqīng.
When this Bhikṣu was near death,
In empty space, he heard in full the twenty thousand trillion verses of the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* previously spoken by the Wēi Yīn Wáng Buddha,
Was able to receive and uphold them completely,
And immediately attained the above-mentioned purity of the eye-root,
As well as the purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-roots.
Having attained this purity of the six roots,
He further extended his lifespan by two million trillion Niyuta years,
Widely expounding this *Fǎ Huá Jīng* for others.
At that time, the arrogant four assemblies—Bhikṣus, Bhikṣuṇīs, Upāsakas, and Upāsikās—
Who had slighted this person and given him the name Bù Qīng,
Seeing that he had attained great supernatural powers,
The power of joyful and eloquent speech, and the power of great and auspicious tranquility,
Hearing his teachings,
All believed, submitted, and followed him.
This Bodhisattva further transformed a thousand million beings,
Causing them to abide in Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
After his life ended,
He encountered two thousand trillion Buddhas,
All named Rì Yuè Dēngmíng,
And within their Dharmas, he expounded this *Fǎ Huá Jīng*.
Due to these causes and conditions,
He again encountered two thousand trillion Buddhas,
All named Yún Zìzài Dēng Wáng,
Within the Dharmas of these Buddhas,
Receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting,
And expounding this sūtra for the four assemblies,
He attained this constant purity of the eye,
And the purity of the ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind-roots,
Expounding the Dharma within the four assemblies, without any fear in his heart.
Dé Dàshì!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Cháng Bùqīng,
Having made offerings to so many Buddhas,
With reverence, respect, and praise,
Planting various good roots,
Later encountered thousands of millions of Buddhas,
And within the Dharmas of these Buddhas, expounded this sūtra,
Accomplishing merits, will attain Buddhahood."
Great Power!
What do you think?
Was the Bodhisattva Cháng Bù Qīng 常不輕 of that time any different from other people?
He was myself.
If I, in my past lives, had not received, upheld, read, recited, and spoken this sūtra for others,
I could not have quickly attained Anòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提.
Because I, in the presence of former Buddhas, received, upheld, read, recited, and spoke this sūtra for others,
I quickly attained Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提.
Great Power!
At that time, the four assemblies—bhikṣus, bhikṣunīs, upāsakas, upāsikās—
because of their anger and contempt toward me,
for two hundred billion kalpas they did not encounter a Buddha, hear the Dharma, or see the Saṃgha,
and for a thousand kalpas they suffered great pain in the Avīci Hell.
After they had finished these sins,
they again encountered the Bodhisattva Cháng Bù Qīng 常不輕,
who taught and transformed them into Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提.
Great Power,
what do you think?
Were the four assemblies who at that time despised this bodhisattva
any different from other people?
The five hundred bodhisattvas, headed by Bá Tuó Pó Luó 跋陀婆羅, and the five hundred bhikṣus and bhikṣunīs, headed by
Shī Zi Yuè 師子月, and the five hundred upāsakas, headed by
Sī Fó 思佛, who in this assembly are irreversible from Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提, are they.
Great Power!
Know that this *Lotus Sūtra*
greatly benefits all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas
and can enable them to reach Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提.
Therefore, after the Tathāgata’s extinction, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should constantly receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and write this sūtra."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
“In the past there was a Buddha
named Wēi Yīn Wáng 威音王,
whose divine wisdom was immeasurable,
who guided all,
and who was commonly revered by gods, humans, dragons, and spirits.
After that Buddha’s extinction,
when the Dharma was about to end,
there was a bodhisattva
named Cháng Bù Qīng 常不輕.
At that time, the four assemblies
clung to the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva Bù Qīng 不輕
went to their places
and said to them:
‘I do not despise you;
you practice the Way,
and all of you will become Buddhas.’
When these people heard this,
they belittled, reviled, and cursed him;
the Bodhisattva Bù Qīng 不輕
was able to endure this.
When his sins were finished,
at the time of his approaching death,
he heard this sūtra
and his six roots were pure.
Through the power of his supernormal abilities,
his lifespan increased,
and again he widely
explained this sūtra for those people.
All of the Dharma-clinging assemblies
received the Bodhisattva’s teaching and transformation,
enabling them to dwell on the Buddha Way.
When Bù Qīng 不輕 died,
he encountered countless Buddhas;
because he spoke this sūtra,
he obtained immeasurable blessings,
gradually accumulating merit and virtue,
and quickly achieved the Buddha Way.
The Bù Qīng 不輕 of that time
was myself.
The four assemblies of that time,
those who clung to the Dharma,
heard Bù Qīng 不輕 say:
‘You will become Buddhas.’
Because of this cause and condition,
they encountered countless Buddhas.
The bodhisattvas in this assembly,
the assembly of five hundred,
together with the four assemblies,
the men and women of pure faith,
are the ones listening to the Dharma in my presence now.
In a former life,
I exhorted these people
to listen to and receive this sūtra,
the foremost Dharma.
I revealed it and taught them
to dwell in nirvāṇa,
receiving and upholding such
sūtras in life after life.
For billions upon billions of kalpas,
up to the inconceivable,
they then were able to hear
this *Lotus Sūtra*.
For billions upon billions of kalpas,
up to the inconceivable,
the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
then speak this sūtra.
Therefore, practitioners,
after the Buddha’s extinction,
hearing such a sūtra,
should not give rise to doubt.
They should single-mindedly
widely speak this sūtra,
encountering Buddhas in life after life,
and quickly achieve the Buddha Way.”
At that time, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the dust motes of a thousand worlds, who had welled up from the earth,
all with one mind joined their palms before the Buddha,
looked up at his honored countenance,
and said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One! After the extinction of the Buddha,
in the lands where the World-Honored One’s emanated bodies are located and in the places where they pass into extinction,
we will widely speak this sūtra.
Why is this?
We too want to obtain this true and pure great Dharma,
receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and write it, and make offerings to it.”
At that time, the World-Honored One,
before Mañjuśrī and other immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had long dwelt in the Sahā World,
and all the bhikṣus, bhikṣunīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans,
displayed great supernatural powers before all the assemblies,
extended his broad, long tongue up to the Brahmā World,
and from all his pores emitted immeasurable, countless rays of color,
all of which universally illuminated the worlds of the ten directions.
The Buddhas beneath the jeweled trees and upon the lion thrones also did likewise,
extended their broad, long tongues, and emitted immeasurable rays of light.
When Śākyamuni Buddha and the Buddhas beneath the jeweled trees were displaying their supernatural powers,
it lasted for a hundred thousand years,
and then they drew their tongues back.
At the same time, they coughed
and snapped their fingers together,
and these two sounds universally reached all the Buddhas’ worlds in the ten directions,
and the earth all shook in six ways.
The sentient beings within them—
devas, nāgas, yakṣas,
gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas,
humans, and non-humans—
through the Buddha’s supernatural power,
all saw this Sahā World, immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas beneath jeweled trees and upon lion thrones;
and they saw Śākyamuni Buddha together with the Tathāgata Tá Bǎo 多寶,
in the jeweled tower, sitting upon a lion throne;
and they also saw immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all the four assemblies respectfully surrounding Śākyamuni Buddha.
Having seen this,
they were all greatly joyful
and gained what they had never had before.
At that time, all the devas, in empty space, loudly proclaimed:
“Beyond this immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of asaṃkhya worlds,
there is a country named Sahā,
and in it there is a Buddha named Śākyamuni,
who is now speaking for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas a great vehicle sūtra named *The Wondrous Dharma Lotus Flower*,
a Dharma that teaches bodhisattvas,
protected and kept in mind by the Buddhas.
You should deeply rejoice with this,
and you should also bow down and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha.”
Those sentient beings, having heard the voice in empty space,
joined their palms and faced the Sahā World, saying:
“Námó Śākyamuni Buddha! 南無釋迦牟尼佛! Námó Śākyamuni Buddha!” 南無釋迦牟尼佛!
With all kinds of flowers, incense, necklaces, banners, and canopies,
and all kinds of ornaments for their bodies, precious jewels, and wonderful objects,
they all scattered them toward the Sahā World from afar.
The things that were scattered came from the ten directions, like clouds gathering,
turning into jeweled canopies that covered all the Buddhas here.
At that time, the worlds of the ten directions were unobstructed and interpenetrated, like a single Buddha land.
At that time, the Buddha told the great assembly of bodhisattvas, headed by Shàng Xíng 上行:
“The supernatural powers of the Buddhas are like this,
immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable.

If I were to use these supernatural powers to speak of the merit and virtue of this sūtra for immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of asaṃkhya kalpas for the sake of entrusting it to you,
I still could not exhaust it.
To put it concisely,
all the Dharmas possessed by the Tathāgata, all the unimpeded supernatural powers of the Tathāgata,
all the secret treasuries of the Tathāgata, and all the most profound matters of the Tathāgata are declared, shown, and spoken in this sūtra.
Therefore, after the Tathāgata’s extinction,
you should single-mindedly receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and write this sūtra
and practice it as it is spoken.
In whatever country
there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and write this sūtra
and practice it as it is spoken,
wherever the sūtra scroll is located,
whether in a garden, in a forest, beneath a tree, or in a saṃghārāma,
in the house of a layperson,
in a palace hall,
or in a mountain valley wilderness,
in all these places, one should erect a stūpa and make offerings.
Why is this?
Know that this place is the place of enlightenment,
the place where the Buddhas attained Ānòuduōluósānmiǎosānpútí 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提,
the place where the Buddhas turned the Dharma wheel,
and the place where the Buddhas entered parinirvāṇa.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
"All Buddhas, saviors of the world,
abide in great spiritual power.
For the sake of pleasing sentient beings,
they manifest limitless spiritual strength.
Their tongue-signs reach the Brahma heavens,
their bodies emit countless rays of light.
For those who seek the Buddha-path,
they manifest these rare and extraordinary events.
The sounds of the Buddhas' clearing of throats,
and the sounds of their snapping of fingers,
are heard throughout the ten directions,
and the earth shakes in six ways.
Because, after the Buddha's extinction,
one can uphold this sūtra,
all Buddhas are delighted
and manifest limitless spiritual strength.
Because one entrusts and cherishes this sūtra,
and praises those who receive and uphold it,
even throughout limitless kalpas,
it still cannot be fully expressed.
This person's merit and virtue
is boundless and endless,
like the space of the ten directions,
which cannot be measured.
One who can uphold this sūtra
is as if they have already seen me,
and also seen Tàbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
and all the emanations,
and also seen me today,
teaching and transforming all the bodhisattvas.
One who can uphold this sūtra
causes me and my emanations,
and the extinct Tàbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
to all be delighted.
The Buddhas of the ten directions, present now,
as well as those of the past and future,
are also seen and venerated,
and also caused to be delighted.
The secret essential Dharma
that all Buddhas attain when sitting at the place of enlightenment,
one who can uphold this sūtra
will soon attain as well.
One who can uphold this sūtra,
regarding the meaning of all Dharmas, names, and words, enjoys speaking without end,
like the wind in the sky,
without any obstruction.
After the extinction of the Thus Come One,
knowing the causes, conditions, and sequence of the sūtras spoken by the Buddha,
one speaks the truth according to the meaning,
like the light of the sun and moon,
which can dispel all darkness.
This person walks in the world
and can extinguish the darkness of sentient beings,
teaching limitless bodhisattvas,
ultimately dwelling in the One Vehicle.
Therefore, those who are wise,
hearing of this merit and benefit,
after my extinction,
should receive and uphold this sūtra.
This person, regarding the Buddha-path,
will certainly have no doubt."
At that time, Shìjiāmóuní Fó 釋迦牟尼佛 arose from the Dharma seat,
manifesting great spiritual power.
With his right hand, he stroked the crowns of limitless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and spoke these words:
"Throughout limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of asamkhyeya kalpas,
I have cultivated this rare and difficult-to-attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi Dharma,
and now I entrust it to you all.
You all should single-mindedly propagate this Dharma,
widely causing it to increase and benefit."
In this way, he stroked the crowns of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas three times, and spoke these words:
"Throughout limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of asamkhyeya kalpas,
I have cultivated this rare and difficult-to-attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi Dharma,
and now I entrust it to you all.
You all should receive, uphold, read, recite, and widely proclaim this Dharma,
causing all sentient beings to universally hear and know it.
Why is this?
The Thus Come One possesses great compassion,
without any stinginess or avarice,
and is also without any fear,
able to bestow upon sentient beings the Buddha's wisdom, the Thus Come One's wisdom, and natural wisdom.
The Thus Come One is the great benefactor of all sentient beings.
You all should also follow and learn the Dharma of the Thus Come One,
and not give rise to stinginess or avarice.
In the future world,
if there are good men or good women who believe in the Thus Come One's wisdom,
you should expound this *Lotus Sūtra* for them,
causing them to hear and know it,
in order to enable those people to attain the Buddha's wisdom.
If there are sentient beings who do not believe and accept it,
you should, within the other profound Dharmas of the Thus Come One,
instruct, teach, benefit, and delight them.
If you all can do thus,
you will have repaid the kindness of all the Buddhas."
At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, hearing the Buddha speak in this way,
were all greatly delighted, and their bodies were filled with joy.
They increased their reverence even more,
bowing their bodies, lowering their heads,
and joining their palms towards the Buddha.
Together, they spoke these words:
"As the World Honored One commands, we will completely follow and practice.
Yes, World Honored One! May you not have any concerns."
The assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, in this way, three times in succession,
together spoke these words:
"As the World Honored One commands, we will completely follow and practice.
Yes, World Honored One! May you not have any concerns."
At that time, Shìjiāmóuní Fó 釋迦牟尼佛 caused all the emanated Buddhas who had come from the ten directions to return to their native lands,
and spoke these words:
"May all the Buddhas each abide in peace.
The Tàbǎo Fó 多寶佛's stūpa may remain as it was."
At the time of speaking these words,
all the limitless emanated Buddhas from the ten directions—those sitting on lion thrones beneath jeweled trees—
and Tàbǎo Fó 多寶佛,
along with the boundless asamkhyeya great assembly of bodhisattvas such as Shàngxíng 上行,
the four assemblies of śrāvakas such as Shèlìfú 舍利弗,
and all the beings in the world—gods, humans, asuras, etc.—
hearing what the Buddha had said,
were all greatly delighted.
At that time, Sùwánghuā Púsà 宿王華菩薩 said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
How does Yàowáng Púsà 藥王菩薩 roam in the Sahā world?
World Honored One!
How many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayuta of difficult practices and ascetic practices does this Yàowáng Púsà 藥王菩薩 undertake?
Excellent, World Honored One!
May you please explain a little."
The gods, dragons, spirits, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras,
garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, etc.,
and also the bodhisattvas who had come from other lands, and this assembly of śrāvakas,
hearing this, were all delighted.
At that time, the Buddha told Sùwánghuā Púsà 宿王華菩薩:
"In the distant past, countless Ganges sand kalpas ago,
there was a Buddha named Rìyuè jìngmíngdé Rúlái 日月淨明德如來,
worthy of offerings, of right and universal knowledge,
perfect in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, understanding the world, unsurpassed knight, taming and regulating hero, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World Honored One.
That Buddha had eighty billion great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and seventy-two Ganges sand great śrāvaka assemblies.
The Buddha's lifespan was forty-two thousand kalpas,
and the bodhisattvas' lifespans were also equal.
In that land, there were no women, hells, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, etc.,
and no difficulties at all.
The ground was as flat as the palm of a hand,
made of lapis lazuli, adorned with jeweled trees,
covered with jeweled canopies above,
with jeweled banners hanging down.
Jeweled vases and incense burners were all around the borders of the country.
Seven treasures formed platforms,
one platform for each tree,
and the trees were one arrow's flight away from the platforms.
Beneath these jeweled trees, there were all bodhisattvas and śrāvakas sitting.
On top of each of the jeweled platforms, there were hundreds of millions of gods making heavenly music,
singing praises to the Buddha, and using this as an offering.
At that time, that Buddha was expounding the *Lotus Sūtra* for Yīqiè zhòngshēng xǐjiàn Púsà 一切眾生憙見菩薩 and the assemblies of bodhisattvas and śrāvakās.
This Yīqiè zhòngshēng xǐjiàn Púsà 一切眾生憙見菩薩 delighted in practicing ascetic practices.
Within the Dharma of Rìyuè jìngmíngdé Fó 日月淨明德佛,
he diligently walked and practiced, single-mindedly seeking Buddhahood.
After twelve thousand years,
he attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Colors and Forms.
After attaining this samādhi,
his mind greatly rejoiced, and he immediately thought:
'My attainment of the Samādhi of Manifesting All Colors and Forms is all due to the power of hearing the *Lotus Sūtra*.
I will now make offerings to Rìyuè jìngmíngdé Fó 日月淨明德佛 and the *Lotus Sūtra.'
Immediately, he entered this samādhi,
and in empty space, he rained down *mandārava* flowers, *mahāmandārava* flowers,
and finely ground solid black sandalwood,
filling empty space, descending like clouds.
He also rained down sandalwood incense from the shore of the sea—
this incense, six *zhu*, was worth the entire Sahā world—
as an offering to the Buddha.
After making this offering,
he arose from the samādhi, and thought to himself:
'Although I have made offerings to the Buddha with spiritual powers,
it is not as good as making offerings with my body.'
Immediately, he consumed various incenses—sandalwood, olibanum, *turushka*, *priyaka*, aloeswood, and *guggulu*—
and also drank *campaka* flower-scented oils.
After twelve hundred years,
he smeared his body with scented oil,
and in front of Rìyuè jìngmíngdé Fó 日月淨明德佛,
he wrapped his body with heavenly jeweled clothing,
poured on the scented oils,
and, through the power of spiritual penetrations, made the vow that his body would naturally ignite,
its light shining throughout eighty billion Ganges sand worlds.
Among them, all the Buddhas simultaneously praised, saying:
'Excellent, excellent! Good man!
This is true diligence.
This is called a true Dharma offering to the Thus Come One.
If one were to use flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense,
scented oil, heavenly silks, banners, canopies, and sandalwood incense from the shore of the sea,
making offerings with such various things,
it would not be able to compare.
Even if one were to give away countries, cities, wives, and children in donations,
it would also not be able to compare.
Good man! This is called the foremost donation,
the most honored and supreme among all donations,
because one makes Dharma offerings to all the Thus Come Ones.'"
Having spoken these words, they were all silent.
His body burned with fire for twelve hundred years,
and after this time,
his body was completely consumed.
"After the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn makes such offerings,
upon the end of his life,
he will be reborn in the land of the Buddha Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé,
in the household of King Jìngdé, sitting in the lotus position,
suddenly being born by transformation.
He will then speak a verse to his father, saying:
"Great King, you should know now,
that I walked in that place,
and immediately obtained all, the Samādhi of Manifesting All Bodies.
Diligently practice great vigor,
relinquishing this beloved body,
to make offerings to the World Honored One,
in order to seek unsurpassed wisdom."
After speaking this verse,
he will say to his father:
'The Buddha Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé is still present now.
I first made offerings to the Buddha,
and obtained the Dhāraṇī of understanding the languages of all beings,
and also heard the *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra* with eight hundred million nayutas of *gaṅkara*, *vimbara*, *akṣobhya* verses.
Great King! I will now return to make offerings to this Buddha.'
After saying this, he will sit upon a seven-jeweled platform,
ascend into the sky, seven *tāla* trees high,
and go to the place of the Buddha,
bowing his head to the ground at his feet,
joining his ten fingers,
and praising the Buddha with a verse:
"Your countenance is exceedingly wondrous and subtle,
your light shines in the ten directions,
I just offered to you,
and now I return to see you in person."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn, after speaking this verse,
said to the Buddha:
'World Honored One! World Honored One is still in the world.'
At that time, the Buddha Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé
said to the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn:
'Good son! The time for my Nirvāṇa has arrived,
the time for my extinction has come,
you should prepare a bed and seat,
for I will enter Pari-nirvāṇa tonight.'
He further instructed the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn:
'Good son! I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you, and to all the great disciples who are Bodhisattvas,
along with the Dharma of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and I also entrust to you the three thousand great thousandfold world's jeweled trees, jeweled platforms, and the attendant devas.
I entrust all of this to you.
After my extinction, I also entrust all the *śarīra* to you,
you should cause them to be spread abroad, extensively make offerings,
and build several thousand towers.'
After the Buddha Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé instructed the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn in this way,
he entered Nirvāṇa in the later part of the night.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn saw the Buddha's extinction,
and felt grief, sadness,
longing for the Buddha,
and used sandalwood from the shore of the sea as pyre, to make offerings to the Buddha's body, and burned it.
After the fire was extinguished,
he collected the *śarīra*,
made eighty-four thousand jeweled urns,
and built eighty-four thousand towers,
as high as three worlds,
with adorned finials,
hanging various banners and canopies, and suspending many jeweled bells.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn further thought to himself:
'Although I have made these offerings,
my heart is still not satisfied,
I will now make further offerings to the *śarīra*.'
He then spoke to the great disciples who were Bodhisattvas, and to the devas, nāgas,
yakṣas, and all the great assembly:
'You should all concentrate your minds,
I will now make offerings to the *śarīra* of the Buddha Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé.'
After speaking these words,
he then, in front of the eighty-four thousand towers, burned his arms adorned with a hundred blessings,
for seventy-two thousand years as an offering,
causing countless seekers of śrāvakayāna and immeasurable asaṃkhyas of people
to generate the mind of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and all were able to abide in the Samādhi of Manifesting All Colors and Bodies.
At that time, all the Bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, etc.,
seeing that he had no arms,
were worried, saddened, and said:
'This Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn is our teacher,
the one who teaches and transforms us,
and now he burns his arms,
and his body is incomplete.'
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn made this vow in the great assembly:
'If I relinquish both arms,
I will surely attain the golden-colored body of a Buddha,
if this is truly not false,
may my two arms be restored as before.'
After making this vow,
they were naturally restored,
due to the purity and depth of this Bodhisattva's merit and wisdom.
At that time, the three thousand great thousandfold world shook in six ways,
the sky rained precious flowers,
and all humans and devas obtained what they had never had before."
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Sùwáng Huā:
"What do you think?
Could the Bodhisattva Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn be anyone else?
He is the Bodhisattva Yàowáng now.
His relinquishing his body in giving,
is in such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of times.
Sùwáng Huā!
If there are those who generate the mind to attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and can burn a finger, even one toe,
to make offerings to a Buddha's tower,

this is superior to using kingdoms, cities, wives, and children, as well as the three thousand great thousandfold world's mountains, forests, rivers, ponds, and various jeweled objects, to make offerings.
If there is another person who uses seven jewels to fill the three thousand great thousandfold world, to make offerings to the Buddhas,
as well as great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats,
the merit that this person obtains is not as great as receiving and upholding this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra*,
even one four-line verse,
their blessings are the greatest.
Sùwáng Huā!
It is like how among all the flowing streams, rivers,
and waters, the sea is the foremost;
this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra* is also like this,
among all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, it is the most profound and great.
Also, like among earthen mountains, Black Mountains, small Iron Ring Mountains, great Iron Ring Mountains, and the ten jeweled mountains,
among all the mountains,
Mount Sumeru is the foremost;
this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra* is also like this,
among all sūtras, it is the most supreme.
Also, like among the multitude of stars,
the Moon Deva is the foremost;
this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra* is also like this,
among thousands of millions of kinds of sūtras and Dharmas, it is the most illuminating.
Also, like the Sun Deva can dispel all darkness;
this sūtra is also like this, it can break all darkness of unwholesomeness.
Also, like among all the small kings, the Wheel-Turning Sage King is the foremost;
this sūtra is also like this, among all the sūtras, it is the most honored.
Also, like Śakra is the king among the Trayastriṃśa devas,
this sūtra is also like this, it is the king among all the sūtras.
Also, like the Great Brahmā King is the father of all beings;
this sūtra is also like this, it is the father of all sages, both learners and non-learners, and those who generate the Bodhi mind.
Also, like among all ordinary people, the Śrotāpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, Arhat, and Pratyekabuddha are the foremost;
this sūtra is also like this, among all the sūtras and Dharmas spoken by all the Tathāgatas, or spoken by Bodhisattvas, or spoken by Śrāvakas,
it is the foremost.
Those who can receive and uphold this sūtra, are also like this, they are also the foremost among all beings.
Among all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, the Bodhisattva is the foremost;
this sūtra is also like this, among all the sūtras and Dharmas, it is the foremost.
Like the Buddha is the Dharma King of all Dharmas; this sūtra is also like this, it is the king among all the sūtras.
Sùwáng Huā!
This sūtra can save all beings,
this sūtra can cause all beings to be apart from all sufferings and afflictions,
this sūtra can greatly benefit all beings,
and fulfill their wishes.
Like a cool pond! It can satisfy all those who are thirsty,
like the cold obtaining fire,
like the naked obtaining clothes,
like merchants obtaining a leader,
like a child obtaining a mother,
like crossing obtaining a boat,
like the sick obtaining a doctor,
like darkness obtaining a lamp,
like the poor obtaining treasure,
like the people obtaining a king,
like a merchant obtaining the sea,
like a torch dispelling darkness;
this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra* is also like this,
it can cause beings to be apart from all suffering, all sickness and pain,
and can untie all the bonds of birth and death.
If a person can hear this *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtra*,
whether they write it themselves, or cause others to write it,
the merit obtained, even if measured with the Buddha's wisdom, cannot be fathomed.
If one writes this sūtra scroll,
and uses flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense, paste incense, banners, canopies, and clothing,
various kinds of lamps—ghee lamps, oil lamps, various fragrant oil lamps,
*campaka* oil lamps, *sumanā* oil lamps, *pāṭala* oil lamps, *vāriṣika* oil lamps, *nava-mallikā* oil lamps—to make offerings,
the merit obtained is also immeasurable.
Sùwáng Huā!
If there is a person who hears this chapter on the Past Affairs of the Bodhisattva Yàowáng,
they will also obtain immeasurable and boundless merit.
If there is a woman who hears this chapter on the Past Affairs of the Bodhisattva Yàowáng,
and can receive and uphold it,
she will completely end her female body,
and will not receive it again in the future.
If, in the five hundred years after the Tathāgata's extinction,
there is a woman who hears this sūtra,
and cultivates according to the teachings,
upon the end of her life here,
she will immediately go to the Land of Bliss,
where the Buddha Āmítuó, and great Bodhisattva assemblies, surround her dwelling place,
she will be born within a lotus flower, upon a jeweled seat,
and will no longer be afflicted by greed and desire,
nor will she be afflicted by anger and delusion,
nor will she be afflicted by arrogance, jealousy, and various defilements,
she will obtain the Bodhisattva's supernormal powers and the Tolerance of the Non-origination of Dharmas.
Having obtained this Tolerance,
her eye faculty will be pure and clear,
and with this pure and clear eye faculty,
she will see seven million two hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of Ganges' sands of Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
At that time, all the Buddhas from afar together praised, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Good man!
You are able within the Śākyamuni Buddha's Dharma
to receive, uphold, read, recite, and contemplate this sutra,
and speak it for others.
The merit and virtue you obtain is immeasurable and boundless,
fire cannot burn it, water cannot float it away.
Your meritorious virtue, even a thousand Buddhas speaking together could not fully describe.
You are now able to destroy all demon thieves,
ruin the army of birth and death,
and utterly demolish all remaining enemies.
Good man!
Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, with their supernatural powers, together protect you.
Within all worlds of devas and humans, none are like you,
except for the Thus Come One (Tathāgata).
As for all the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and even Bodhisattvas,
none possess wisdom and dhyāna equal to yours."
Sùwáng Huā!
This Bodhisattva has achieved such power of meritorious virtues and wisdom.
If there is someone who hears this chapter on the Former Affairs of the Bhaisajyarāja Bodhisattva
and is able to rejoice and praise it,
that person, in his present life, will constantly emit the fragrance of blue lotus flowers from his mouth,
and will constantly emit the fragrance of sandalwood from Niu Tou from the pores of his body.
The meritorious virtues obtained will be as described above.
Therefore, Sùwáng Huā!
With this chapter on the Former Affairs of the Bhaisajyarāja Bodhisattva, I entrust it to you.
In the five five-hundred-year periods after my extinction,
widely propagate and spread it in Jambudvīpa,
not allowing it to be cut off,
and preventing demons, demon people, devas, dragons, yakshas, kumbhāṇḍas, and the like from taking advantage of it.
Sùwáng Huā!
You should use your supernatural powers to protect this sutra.
Why is that?
This sutra is a good medicine for the people of Jambudvīpa.
If someone is ill and hears this sutra,
the illness will immediately disappear, and they will not age or die.
Sùwáng Huā!
If you see someone receiving and upholding this sutra,
you should fill blue lotus flowers full with powdered incense,
and scatter it upon them.
After scattering it,
make this thought:
'This person will soon take grass and sit upon the Bodhimaṇḍa,
break the armies of demons,
and sound the Dharma conch shell and beat the great Dharma drum,
delivering all sentient beings from the sea of old age, sickness, and death.'
Therefore, those who seek the Buddha path, upon seeing people who receive and uphold this sutra,
should generate such respectful hearts."
While speaking this chapter on the Former Affairs of the Bhaisajyarāja Bodhisattva,
eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas obtained the dhāraṇī of understanding the languages of all sentient beings.
The Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, from within the jeweled stupa, praised the Sùwáng Huā Bodhisattva, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Sùwáng Huā!
You have achieved inconceivable meritorious virtues,
and were able to ask Śākyamuni Buddha about such matters,
benefiting immeasurable numbers of all sentient beings."
