At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha emitted light from the uṣṇīṣa mark of his great person,
and also emitted light from the white hair mark between his eyebrows,
illuminating all Buddha worlds to the east, as many as one hundred eight million nayutas of Ganges Rivers' sands.
Beyond this number, there was a world named Pure Light Adornment.
In that country was a Buddha named Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì Tathāgata,
Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara,
Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā Devamanuṣyāṇāṃ, Buddha, Bhagavat,
reverently surrounded by a limitless and boundless great assembly of Bodhisattvas, for whom he preached the Dharma.
Śākyamuni Buddha's white hair light universally illuminated that country.
At that time, in that entire country of Pure Light Adornment,
there was a Bodhisattva named Wonderful Sound (Miàoyīn),
who had long planted roots of virtue,
and had made offerings to and been close to limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
and had completely achieved profound wisdom.
He had obtained the Samadhi of the Wonderful Banner Sign, the Lotus Flower Samadhi, the Pure Virtue Samadhi,
the Sùwáng Play Samadhi, the Non-causation Samadhi, the Wisdom Seal Samadhi,
the Samadhi of Understanding the Languages of All Sentient Beings,
the Samadhi of Gathering All Meritorious Virtues, the Pure Samadhi,
the Samadhi of Supernatural Power Play,
the Torch of Wisdom Samadhi, the Adornment King Samadhi,
the Pure Brightness Samadhi, the Pure Treasury Samadhi,
the Unequaled Samadhi, and the Sun Rotation Samadhi,
having obtained such hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges River sands' worth of great samadhis.
Śākyamuni Buddha's light illuminated his body.
He then said to the Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì Buddha:
"World Honored One! I shall go to the Sahā World, to bow, be close to,
and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha,
and also see the Dharma Prince Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bhaisajyarāja Bodhisattva,
the Vīradatta Bodhisattva,
the Sùwáng Huā Bodhisattva,
the Superior Practice Bodhisattva,
the Adornment King Bodhisattva,
and the Bhaiṣajyasamudgata Bodhisattva."
At that time, the Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì Buddha told the Miàoyīn Bodhisattva:
"Do not belittle that country and give rise to inferior thoughts.
Good man! That Sahā World is uneven, high and low,
and filled with soil, rocks, and various mountains, filthy and evil.
The Buddha's body is small, and the multitude of Bodhisattvas are also small in form.
But your body is forty-two thousand yojanas,
and my body is six million eight hundred thousand yojanas.
Your body is foremost in being upright and handsome,
with hundreds of thousands of millions of blessings,
and your light is especially wonderful.
Therefore, when you go,
do not belittle that country—
and give rise to inferior thoughts about the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and land."
The Miàoyīn Bodhisattva said to that Buddha:
"World Honored One! My going to the Sahā World now is all due to the power of the Thus Come One,
the Thus Come One's supernatural power play,
and the adornment of the Thus Come One's meritorious virtues and wisdom."
Thereupon, the Miàoyīn Bodhisattva, without rising from his seat and without shaking his body,
entered into samadhi.
With the power of samadhi,
on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, not far from the Dharma seat,
he manifested eighty-four thousand lotus flowers of various treasures,
with stems of Jāmbūnada gold,
leaves of white silver,
filaments of vajra,
and platforms made of *Pentapetes phoenicea* jewels.
At that time, the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī saw these lotus flowers
and said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
What is the cause and condition for this auspicious omen to appear first?
There are several tens of millions of lotus flowers,
with stems of Jāmbūnada gold,
leaves of white silver,
filaments of vajra,
and platforms made of *Pentapetes phoenicea* jewels."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Miàoyīn
intends to come from the country of the Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì Buddha,
with eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas
surrounding him, to this Sahā World,
to make offerings, be close to, and bow to me,
and also intends to make offerings and listen to the Lotus Flower Sutra."
Mañjuśrī said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
What roots of goodness has this Bodhisattva planted?
What meritorious virtues has he cultivated?
That he is able to have such great supernatural powers?
What samadhi does he practice?
May you explain to us the names of these samadhis.
We also wish to diligently cultivate them.
By practicing these samadhis,
we will be able to see this Bodhisattva's form and appearance, size,
dignified manner, and movements.
May the World Honored One, with your supernatural power, cause that Bodhisattva to come
so that we may see him."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"This long-extinct Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna
will manifest his form for you all."
Then the Buddha Prabhūtaratna told that Bodhisattva:
"Good man! Come, the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī wishes to see your body."
Thereupon, the Miàoyīn Bodhisattva disappeared from that country,
and together with eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas, set forth.
The countries they passed through shook in six ways,
and all rained seven-jeweled lotus flowers;
hundreds of thousands of heavenly instruments played music without being struck.
That Bodhisattva's eyes were like the leaves of a great blue lotus flower.
Even if one were to combine hundreds of thousands of millions of moons, his countenance would be even more upright and handsome than that.
His body was true gold in color,
adorned with limitless hundreds of thousands of meritorious virtues,
his majestic virtue was blazing,
and his light shone brightly.
He possessed all the characteristics,
like the indestructible body of Nārāyaṇa.
He entered a seven-jeweled platform,
ascended into the sky,
and rose seven tāla trees above the ground.
The multitude of Bodhisattvas reverently surrounded him,
and he came to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in this Sahā World.
Having arrived,
he descended from the seven-jeweled platform,
and with a necklace worth hundreds of thousands,
he brought it to Śākyamuni Buddha,
bowed his head to his feet,
offered the necklace,
and said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
The Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì Buddha inquires after the World Honored One,
whether you have few illnesses and few afflictions,
whether your rising and reclining is easy and comfortable,
and whether you practice in peace and joy?
Are your four elements in harmony?
Are worldly affairs tolerable?
Are sentient beings easy to deliver?
Is there not much greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, stinginess, and arrogance?
Is there no lack of filial piety towards parents,
no lack of respect towards śramaṇas, no heterodox views, no unwholesome minds,
and no lack of control over the five senses?
World Honored One!
Are sentient beings able to subdue all demon enemies?
Is the long-extinct Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna in the seven-jeweled stupa, coming to listen to the Dharma?
And he also inquires after the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna,
whether he is peaceful and has few afflictions, and whether he can endure and dwell for a long time?
World Honored One!
I now wish to see the body of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna.
May the World Honored One show him to me so that I may see him."
At that time, Śhìjiāmóunífó (釋迦牟尼佛) said to Duōbǎo fó (多寶佛):
"This Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva wishes to meet you."
Then Duōbǎo fó (多寶佛) said to Wonderful Sound,
"Excellent, excellent!
You are able to come here to make offerings to Śhìjiāmóunífó (釋迦牟尼佛) and listen to the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* (法華經), and to see Wénshūshīlì (文殊師利) and others."
At that time, Huádé Púsà (華德菩薩) said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
What good roots has this Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva planted,
what meritorious deeds has he cultivated,
that he possesses such spiritual power?"
The Buddha said to Huádé Púsà (華德菩薩):
"In the past, there was a Buddha named Yúnléiyīnwáng Duōtuó Ājiādù (雲雷音王多陀阿伽度), Āluóhē (阿羅訶), Sānmiǎosānfót陀 (三藐三佛陀),
whose country was named Xiàn Yīqiè Shìjiān (現一切世間),
and whose kalpa was named Xǐjiàn (憙見).
For twelve thousand years, the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva made offerings to Yúnléiyīnwáng fó (雲雷音王佛) with a hundred thousand kinds of music,
and offered eighty-four thousand jeweled bowls.
Because of this cause and result,
he is now born in the Buddha-land of Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì (淨華宿王智), and possesses such spiritual power.
Huádé (華德)!
What do you think?
Was the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva who made musical offerings and offered jeweled vessels to Yúnléiyīnwáng fó (雲雷音王佛) at that time
anyone else?
He is now this Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
Huádé (華德)!
This Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva has already made offerings to and been close to countless Buddhas,
and has long cultivated the roots of virtue.
He has also encountered as many Buddhas as there are sands in the Ganges, hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas.
Huádé (華德)!
You only see the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva's body here,
but this Bodhisattva manifests various bodies and preaches this scripture everywhere for all living beings—
sometimes manifesting as the Brahma King,
sometimes manifesting as Śhìdìhuánīng (帝釋),
sometimes manifesting as Zìzài Tiān (自在天),
sometimes manifesting as Dàzìzài Tiān (大自在天),
sometimes manifesting as a heavenly great general,
sometimes manifesting as Píshāmén Tiānwáng (毘沙門天王),
sometimes manifesting as a Cakravartin King,
sometimes manifesting as various small kings,
sometimes manifesting as an elder,
sometimes manifesting as a householder,
sometimes manifesting as a government official,
sometimes manifesting as a Brahmin,
sometimes manifesting as a Bhikṣu, Bhikṣuṇī, Upāsaka, or Upāsikā,
sometimes manifesting as the wife of an elder or householder,
sometimes manifesting as the wife of a government official,
sometimes manifesting as the wife of a Brahmin,
sometimes manifesting as a boy or girl,
sometimes manifesting as a Deva, Nāga, Yakṣa, Gandharva, Asura, Garuḍa, Kinnara, Mahoraga, human, or non-human,
and preaches this scripture.
He can rescue all those in hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and other difficult places,
he transforms into a female body and preaches this scripture.
Huádé (華德)!
This Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva is able to protect and rescue the living beings of the Sahā world.
This Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva manifests such various transformed bodies in this Sahā world
to preach this scripture for all living beings,
without any loss or diminution in his spiritual powers, transformations, or wisdom.
This Bodhisattva illuminates the Sahā world with various wisdoms,
enabling all living beings to each obtain what they need to know;
and it is the same in the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions.
If they should be saved by the form of a Śrāvaka,
he manifests the form of a Śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by the form of a Pratyekabuddha,
he manifests the form of a Pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by the form of a Bodhisattva,
he manifests the form of a Bodhisattva and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by the form of a Buddha,
he immediately manifests the form of a Buddha and preaches the Dharma for them.
In this way, according to what they should be saved by, he manifests the corresponding form,
and even if they should be saved by extinction,
he demonstrates extinction.
Huádé (華德)!
The Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has perfected the power of great spiritual powers and wisdom,
and his affairs are like this."
At that time, Huádé Púsà (華德菩薩) said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
This Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva has deeply planted good roots.
World Honored One!
In what samādhi does this Bodhisattva abide,
that he is able to transform and manifest himself in this way, saving living beings?"
The Buddha said to Huádé Púsà (華德菩薩):
"Good man!
The name of that samādhi is 'Manifesting All Physical Forms.'
The Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva abides in this samādhi,
and is able to benefit countless living beings in this way."
When this chapter on the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva was being spoken,
the eighty-four thousand people who came with the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva all attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms;
the countless Bodhisattvas of this Sahā world also attained this samādhi and dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, having made offerings to Śhìjiāmóunífó (釋迦牟尼佛) and the Stūpa of Duōbǎo (多寶),
returned to his native land.
The countries he passed through experienced six kinds of earthquakes.
Precious lotus flowers rained down,
and hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of music were played.
Having arrived in his native land,
he, surrounded by eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas,
went to the Buddha-place of Jìnghuá Sùwángzhì fó (淨華宿王智佛),
and said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
I went to the Sahā world to benefit living beings,
and saw Śhìjiāmóunífó (釋迦牟尼佛),
and also saw the Stūpa of Duōbǎo (多寶),
and paid homage and made offerings;
I also saw the Dharma Prince Bodhisattva Wénshūshīlì (文殊師利),
and also saw Yàowáng Púsà (藥王菩薩),
Déqín Jīngjìn Lì Púsà (得勤精進力菩薩),
Yǒngshī Púsà (勇施菩薩), and others,
and also caused these eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas to attain the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms."
When this chapter on the coming and going of the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva was being spoken,
forty-two thousand devaputras attained the forbearance of non-origination of dharmas,
and Huádé Púsà (華德菩薩) attained the *Fǎ Huá* (法華) Samādhi."
Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩), with a heart as clear as crystal, responds infinitely, with his unrestricted divine
powers traveling throughout the Dharma realm, entering lands as small as dust motes to preach the Dharma and deliver beings, fully endowed with wondrous
marks, his vows vast as the sea. Whenever beings have the cause and conditions to generate a pure mind, and just utter his
name, he immediately responds to their voice, and all their desires are fulfilled as wished. The *Universal Gate* chapter of the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Scripture
is the true explanation for delivering beings from suffering. If people can
constantly contemplate this scripture, at the moment a thought arises, they will see the victorious form of Great Compassion, which can
extinguish all sufferings. Its merit and virtue are inconceivable. I think that the way of Heaven rewards
good and punishes evil, so the Buddha shows the consequences of actions, causing people to do good and not dare to do evil.
Heaven and hell are both created by people, not deviating from within the square inch of the heart, so
those who do good ascend to heaven, and those who do evil immediately fall into hell. Loyal ministers,
filial sons, auspicious people, and steadfast scholars have the Buddha in their hearts, so the gods protect them, and karmic obstacles
are all eliminated. Therefore, in life, they do not violate the laws, and in death, they do not fall into the Avīci hell.
As for the fierce and obstinate, they single-mindedly do evil, discarding the five relationships like worn-out brooms, and treading on the criminal law
as if drinking something sweet, preferring to feed the Rākṣasas rather than revering the Buddha's way. But human nature is originally good,
and the evil they do is merely a deviation of their disposition; if they can change their minds and thoughts, cultivate self-reflection,
avoid wrongdoing and fear consequences, then in the space of a moment, evil can be transformed into good. Doing good makes them good people,
and the faults they accumulated in the past will be like a speck of dust in space or a snowflake in a red furnace, completely dissolved
and purified. Even if there is karmic retribution, where will it be applied? I constantly think of this, fearing that
people in the world will have faults and not know how to change, and will thus abandon themselves. Therefore, I present
this scripture, so that virtuous gentlemen will forever strengthen their resolve to abstain from evil, and widely receive immeasurable
blessings. How can there be an end to the merit and virtue of doing good!
The first day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Yǒnglè (永樂)
The *Universal Gate Chapter of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩)* in the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Scripture
Translated into prose by Tripiṭaka Master Jūmóluóshí (鳩摩羅什) of the Yáoqín (姚秦) Dynasty
Translated into verse by Śramaṇa Jānagupta from Northern India of the Suí (隋) Dynasty
At that time, Wújìn Yì Púsà (無盡意菩薩) immediately rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder,
joined his palms, facing the Buddha,
and said:
"World Honored One!
For what reason is Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩) named Guānshìyīn (觀世音)?"
The Buddha told Wújìn Yì Púsà (無盡意菩薩):
"Good man!
If countless hundreds of thousands of millions of living beings are suffering,
and hear of this Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩),
and single-mindedly call his name,
Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩) will immediately observe their voices,
and all will attain liberation.
If there are those who uphold the name of this Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩),
and are placed in a great fire,
the fire will not be able to burn them,
because of the power of this Bodhisattva.
If they are swept away by a great flood,
and call his name,
they will immediately reach shallow ground.
If there are hundreds of thousands of millions of living beings
who, seeking gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *chequ* (車𤦲), agate, coral, amber, pearls, and other treasures,
enter the great ocean,
and if a black wind blows their boats,
causing them to drift to the land of the Rākṣasa demons,
if among them there is even one person who calls the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩),
all these people will be liberated from the difficulty of the Rākṣasas.
For this reason, he is named Guānshìyīn (觀世音).
If someone is about to be harmed,
and calls the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩),
the knives and clubs they are holding will immediately break into pieces, and they will be liberated.
If in the three-thousand great-thousand world system, it is filled with Yakṣas and Rākṣasas who wish to trouble people,
and they hear them calling the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩), these evil ghosts
will not even be able to look at them with evil eyes,
how much less to harm them.
If someone,
whether guilty or not guilty, is bound with handcuffs, stocks, shackles, and chains,
and calls the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩), they will all be broken and destroyed, and they will immediately be liberated.
If the three-thousand great-thousand world system is filled with enemy bandits,
and there is a merchant leader
leading the merchants, carrying heavy treasures, and passing through a dangerous road,
and one of them makes this announcement:
'Good men! Do not be afraid!
You should all single-mindedly call the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩).
This Bodhisattva is able to bestow fearlessness upon living beings.
If you call his name,
you will be liberated from these enemy bandits.'
The merchants heard this,
and all raised their voices, saying:
'Námó Guānshìyīn Púsà (南無觀世音菩薩)!'
By calling his name,
they were immediately liberated.
Wújìn Yì (無盡意)!
The majestic spiritual power of Guānshìyīn Púsà (觀世音菩薩) Mahāsattva is so vast."
If there are sentient beings with excessive lust,
by constantly thinking of and revering Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to leave lust.
If they have much anger,
by constantly thinking of and revering Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to leave anger.
If they have much foolishness,
by constantly thinking of and revering Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to leave foolishness.
Wújìn Yì!
Guānshìyīn Púsà has great awesome spiritual power such as this,
greatly benefiting all,
therefore sentient beings should constantly keep him in mind.
If there are women, supposing they wish to seek a son,
by bowing to and making offerings to Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will then give birth to a son with blessed virtue and wisdom;
supposing they wish to seek a daughter,
they will then give birth to a daughter who is comely and possesses good characteristics.
Having planted roots of virtue in the past,
they will be loved and respected by all.
Wújìn Yì!
Guānshìyīn Púsà has power such as this,
that if there are sentient beings who reverently bow to Guānshìyīn Púsà,
their blessings will not be in vain.
Therefore, sentient beings should all receive and uphold the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà.
"Wújìn Yì!
If there is a person who receives and upholds the names of sixty-two hundred million Ganges-river sands of Bodhisattvas,
and furthermore, throughout their life, makes offerings of food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicine,
what do you think?
Is the merit of this good man or good woman great or not?"
Wújìn Yì said:
"Extremely great,
World Honored One!"
The Buddha said:
"If furthermore, there is a person who receives and upholds the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà,
even as little as bowing and making offerings for a single moment,
the merit of these two people is exactly equal, without any difference,
inexhaustible throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.
Wújìn Yì!
Receiving and upholding the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà
obtains the benefit of such immeasurable and boundless blessed virtue."
Wújìn Yì Púsà said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One! Guānshìyīn Púsà,
how does he roam this Sahā World?
How does he preach the Dharma for sentient beings?
The power of his skillful means, what is its nature?"
The Buddha told Wújìn Yì Púsà:
"Good man!
If there are sentient beings in a land who should be saved by means of a Buddha's body,
Guānshìyīn Púsà will then manifest a Buddha's body and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a Pratyekabuddha's body,
he will then manifest a Pratyekabuddha's body and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a Śrāvaka's body,
he will then manifest a Śrāvaka's body and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a Brahma King's body,
he will then manifest a Brahma King's body and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of Dìshì,
he will then manifest a body of Dìshì and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of Zìzài Heaven,
he will then manifest a body of Zìzài Heaven and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of Great Zìzài Heaven,
he will then manifest a body of Great Zìzài Heaven and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of a Heavenly Great General,
he will then manifest a body of a Heavenly Great General and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of Píshāmen,
he will then manifest a body of Píshāmen and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of a Minor King,
he will then manifest a body of a Minor King and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of an Elder,
he will then manifest a body of an Elder and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of a Upāsaka,
he will then manifest a body of an Upāsaka and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of a Official,
he will then manifest a body of a Official and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of a body of a Brahmin,
he will then manifest a body of a Brahmin and preach the Dharma for them;

if they should be saved by means of the bodies of Bhikṣus, Bhikṣunīs, Upāsakas, or Upāsikās, he will then manifest the bodies of Bhikṣus, Bhikṣunīs, Upāsakas, or Upāsikās and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of the bodies of women of Elders, Upāsakas, Officials, or Brahmins,
he will then manifest a woman's body and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of the bodies of boys or girls,
he will then manifest the bodies of boys or girls and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of the bodies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, or humans and non-humans,
he will then manifest them all and preach the Dharma for them;
if they should be saved by means of the body of one who holds a vajra,
he will then manifest the body of one who holds a vajra and preach the Dharma for them.
"Wújìn Yì!
Guānshìyīn Púsà accomplishes merits such as these,
with various forms,
roaming various lands, delivering and liberating sentient beings.
Therefore, you should wholeheartedly make offerings to Guānshìyīn Púsà.
This Guānshìyīn Púsà Mahāsattva is able to bestow fearlessness amidst frightening emergencies and disasters.
Therefore, this Sahā World all call him the Bestower of Fearlessness."
Wújìn Yì Púsà said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
I will now make offerings to Guānshìyīn Púsà."
He then untied a necklace of various precious jewels from his neck,
worth hundreds of thousands of taels of gold,
and gave it to him, saying:
"O Benevolent One! Accept this Dharma offering of precious jewel necklace."
At that time, Guānshìyīn Púsà declined to accept it.
Wújìn Yì again said to Guānshìyīn Púsà:
"O Benevolent One! Out of compassion for us,
please accept this necklace."
At that time, the Buddha told Guānshìyīn Púsà:
"You should have compassion for this Wújìn Yì Púsà and the four assemblies,
the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and humans and non-humans,
and accept this necklace."
Immediately, Guānshìyīn Púsà, out of compassion for the four assemblies,
and for the devas, nāgas, and humans and non-humans,
accepted the necklace,
dividing it into two portions,
one portion offered to Shìjiāmóuní Fó,
one portion offered to the stupa of Duōbǎo Fó.
"Wújìn Yì,
Guānshìyīn Púsà has such self-mastery and spiritual power, roaming the Sahā World."
At that time, Wújìn Yì Púsà asked in verse, saying:
"World Honored One, replete with wondrous marks,
I now ask you again,
what is the cause and condition
for this Buddha's son to be named Guānshìyīn?
The Honored One, replete with wondrous marks,"
answered Wújìn Yì in verse:
"Listen to the deeds of Guānyīn,
skillfully responding in all directions.
The vast vows are as deep as the sea,
throughout kalpas inconceivable,
attending many thousands of millions of Buddhas,
generating great pure vows.
I will briefly speak for you:
hearing the name and seeing the body,
keeping him in mind will not be in vain,
able to extinguish all suffering that exists.
Suppose someone raises a mind of harm,
pushing one into a great fire pit,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
the fire pit becomes a pond.
Or adrift in a great ocean,
facing the difficulty of nāgas, fish, and various ghosts,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
the waves cannot submerge one.
Or on Mount Xūmí,
pushed and dropped by someone,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
one abides in the sky like the sun.
Or being chased by evil people,
falling onto Vajra Mountain,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
not a single hair can be harmed.
Or encountering encirclement by vengeful bandits,
each wielding a knife to inflict harm,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
they will all immediately give rise to a compassionate mind.
Or suffering from a king's calamity,
facing execution, about to reach the end of life,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
the sword will immediately be broken into pieces.
Or imprisoned in fetters and chains,
with hands and feet bound by stocks and cangues,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
one will naturally obtain release and liberation.
Spells, curses, and various poisons,
by which people wish to harm one's body,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
they will revert upon the originator.
Or encountering evil rākṣasas,
poisonous dragons, and various ghosts,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
at that time, they will all not dare to harm one.
If surrounded by vicious beasts,
with sharp teeth and claws causing fear,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
they will quickly run to boundless directions.
If surrounded by venomous snakes, vipers, and scorpions,
with poisonous gas and fire blazing,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
they will follow the sound and turn back on their own.
If clouds rumble with thunder and lightning flashes,
hail falls and heavy rain pours,
thinking of that Guānyīn's power,
it will be scattered and dissipated at once.
Sentient beings oppressed by difficulties,
their bodies burdened by immeasurable suffering,
Guānyīn's wondrous wisdom and power
can rescue the world from suffering.
Replete with spiritual powers,
widely cultivating wisdom and skillful means,
in all lands of the ten directions,
there is no realm where he does not manifest a body.
In various evil realms,
hells, among ghosts and animals,
the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death,
will be gradually caused to cease entirely.
True contemplation, pure contemplation,
vast wisdom contemplation,
compassionate contemplation and loving contemplation,
constantly wishing to always gaze upon him.
Light that is stainless and pure,
the sun of wisdom shattering all darkness,
able to subdue disasters, wind, and fire,
universally illuminating the world."
The thunder of his compassionate embodiment of precepts,
the subtle, great cloud of his kind intent,
pours down the sweet dew of the Dharma rain,
extinguishing the flames of affliction.
In situations of litigation and legal disputes,
in the midst of fearful military formations,
recite the power of that Guānshìyīn,
and all animosity will dissipate.
Wonderful Sound Guānshìyīn,
Brahma Sound, Ocean Tide Sound,
surpassing all sounds in the world:
therefore, you must constantly remember,
and in every thought, do not give rise to doubt.
Guānshìyīn, pure and holy,
in suffering, distress, and mortal danger,
is able to act as a refuge;
possessing all virtues,
with compassionate eyes beholding all beings,
a gathering of blessings, immeasurable as the sea,
therefore, one should reverently bow." 』"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Chí Dì immediately rose from his seat, stepped forward, and said to the Buddha, "World Honored One!
If there are sentient beings who hear of these deeds of self-mastery of the Bodhisattva Guānshìyīn,
and the universally manifested display of spiritual powers, it should be known that the merit of these people is not small."
When the Buddha spoke this Universal Gate Chapter, eighty-four thousand beings in the assembly all awakened
the unsurpassed, equal to none, *Ānòuduōluósāmiǎosānpútí* heart.

When this *Tuóluóní* Chapter was spoken,

At that time, the Buddha told the great assembly,
"In the distant past,
beyond countless, boundless, inconceivable *āēngqí* eons,
there was a Buddha named Yún Léiyīn Sùwáng Huāzhì Duōtuó Ājiādù, Āluóhē, Sānmiǎosānpútí.
His country was named Light Adornment, and the eon was named Joyful Sight.
In the Dharma of that Buddha, there was a king named Miào Zhuāngyán.
The queen of that king was named Jìng Dé, and they had two sons,
one named Jìng Zàng and the other named Jìng Yǎn.
These two sons had great spiritual power, blessings, and wisdom.
They had long cultivated the path of conduct of Bodhisattvas,
namely, the *dānbōluómì*, *shīlā bōluómì*, *chāntí bōluómì*, *pílíyé bōluómì*,
*chán bōluómì*, *bōrě bōluómì*, skillful means *bōluómì*, loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity,
and even the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment;
they were all clear and thoroughly understood.
Furthermore, they obtained the Bodhisattva Pure *sānmèi*,
the Sun, Star, and Constellation *sānmèi*, the Pure Light *sānmèi*,
the Pure Color *sānmèi*,
the Pure Illumination *sānmèi*,
the Long Adornment *sānmèi*,
the Great Awesome Virtue Treasury *sānmèi*.
They were also thoroughly versed in these *sānmèi*.
At that time, that Buddha, wishing to guide King Miào Zhuāngyán
and out of compassion for sentient beings,
spoke the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*.
Then, the two sons, Jìng Zàng and Jìng Yǎn, went to their mother's side,
pressed their ten fingertips together, and said,
'We wish that mother would go to the place of the Buddha Yún Léiyīn Sùwáng Huāzhì,
and we shall also attend, draw near, make offerings, and bow in worship.
Why is that?
This Buddha is speaking the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* in the midst of all gods and humans; it is appropriate that we listen and receive it.'
The mother told her sons,
'Your father believes in and accepts external paths, and is deeply attached to Brahminical Dharma.
You should go and tell your father, and go together with him.'
Jìng Zàng and Jìng Yǎn pressed their ten fingertips together and said to their mother,
'We are sons of the Dharma King, yet we were born into this family with wrong views.'
The mother told her sons,
'You should be concerned about your father and manifest spiritual transformations for him.
If he is able to see them,
his mind will surely become pure, or he may listen to us and go to the Buddha's place.'"
Thereupon, the two sons, mindful of their father's sake,
sprang into the empty sky, seven *duōluó* trees high,
manifesting all kinds of miraculous transformations—
walking, standing, sitting, and lying down in the empty sky;
water issuing from their bodies,
fire issuing from beneath their bodies,
water issuing from beneath their bodies,
fire issuing from their bodies;
sometimes manifesting great bodies filling the empty sky, and then manifesting small ones,
small ones again manifesting great ones;
disappearing in the sky, suddenly appearing on the ground;
entering the earth as if entering water, walking on water as if walking on land.
They manifested such various miraculous transformations, causing their father's heart to be pure, confident, and understanding.
When the father saw his sons' spiritual power was such,
his heart was greatly delighted, something he had never experienced before,
and he joined his palms together, facing his sons, and said:
'You, who is your teacher, whose disciples are you?'
The two sons replied:
'Great King!
That *Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Fó*,
is now sitting on the Dharma seat under the seven-jeweled Bodhi tree,
widely expounding the *Fǎhuá Jīng* among all the gods and humans in the world,
is our teacher, and we are his disciples.'
The father said to his sons:
'I also wish to see your teacher now,
may we go together.'
Thereupon the two sons descended from the sky,
and went to their mother's place, joining their palms together and saying to their mother:
'Our father now has faith and understanding,
and is capable of generating the *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎosānpútí* heart.
We have already performed Buddha-deeds for our father,
we wish that mother will allow us
to leave home and cultivate the Way at that Buddha's place.'
At that time, the two sons wished to repeat their meaning,
and spoke to their mother in verse:
"May mother release us, To leave home and become *shāmén*,
The Buddhas are very difficult to encounter,
We wish to follow the Buddha and learn.
Like the *yōutánbōluó*, Encountering the Buddha is even more difficult,
Escaping all difficulties is also difficult,
May you allow us to leave home."
The mother then said:
'I allow you to leave home.
Why? Because the Buddha is difficult to encounter.'
Thereupon the two sons said to their parents:
'Excellent, parents!
May we now go to the place of *Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Fó*,
to draw near and make offerings.
Why?
The Buddha is difficult to encounter, like the *yōutánbōluó* flower,
and like a one-eyed turtle encountering a floating wood hole.
And our past blessings are deep and abundant,
we are born and encounter the Buddha-dharma,
therefore, parents, you should allow us to leave home.
Why?
The Buddhas are difficult to encounter, and the time is also difficult to meet.'
At that time, *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng*'s harem of eighty-four thousand people,
were all capable of receiving and upholding this *Fǎhuá Jīng*.
*Jìngyǎn Púsà*, in the *Fǎhuá* samadhi, had long attained thorough understanding;
*Jìngzàng Púsà*, had already, in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of *jié*, thoroughly understood the Samadhi of Leaving All Evil Destinies,
desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave all evil destinies.
The King's consort had attained the Samadhi of the Assembly of All Buddhas,
and was able to know the secret treasury of all Buddhas.
"The two sons, with such skillful means, skillfully transformed their father,
causing his heart to have faith and understanding,
and to be fond of the Buddha-dharma.
Thereupon, *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* together with his retinue of ministers,
*Jìngdé Fūren* together with her retinue of concubines and palace women,
and the King's two sons together with forty-two thousand people,
at one time went together to the Buddha's place.
Having arrived,
they bowed their heads to the ground at the Buddha's feet,
circumambulated the Buddha three times,
and stood to one side.
At that time, that Buddha expounded the Dharma for the King,
instructing, teaching, benefiting, and delighting him.
The King was greatly delighted.
At that time, *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* and his consort, untied the pearl necklace from their necks,
worth a hundred thousand,
and scattered it upon the Buddha,
in the empty sky transforming into a four-pillared jeweled dais,
in the dais was a great jeweled bed, spread with hundreds of thousands of heavenly garments,
upon it was the Buddha sitting in the lotus position, emitting great light.
At that time, *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* had this thought:
'The Buddha's body is rare and wonderful,
with a dignified and extraordinary appearance,
having achieved the first and most subtle color.'
Then *Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Fó* said to the four assemblies:
'Do you see this *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng*, standing before me with his palms joined?
This King will become a *bǐqiū* in my Dharma,
diligently cultivating, assisting the Buddha-Way Dharma,
and will attain Buddhahood,
named *Suōluóshù Wáng*,
his country named *Dàguāng*,
his *jié* named *Dàgāo Wáng*.
That *Suōluóshù Wáng Fó* will have immeasurable *Púsà* assemblies and immeasurable *shēngwén*,
his country will be level and just,
his merits and virtues will be like this.'
The King then immediately entrusted the country to his younger brother,
and together with his consort, two sons, and all his retinue,
left home in the Buddha-dharma and cultivated the Way.
"After the King left home,
for eighty-four thousand years, he constantly and diligently cultivated and practiced the *Miào Fǎhuá Jīng*.
After this,
he attained the *Yīqiè Jìng Gōngdé Zhuāngyán Sānmèi*,
and immediately ascended into the empty sky, seven *duōluó* trees high,
and said to the Buddha:
'World Honored One! These two sons of mine have already performed Buddha-deeds,
using spiritual power and transformations to turn my deviant heart,
causing me to dwell peacefully in the Buddha-dharma,
and to see the World Honored One.
These two sons are my good knowing advisors,
desiring to awaken the good roots of my past lives, and to benefit me, they came to be born in my family.'
At that time, *Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Fó* said to *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng*:
'So it is, so it is!
As you say.
If a good man or good woman, plants good roots,
in life after life they will obtain good knowing advisors,
and those good knowing advisors, can perform Buddha-deeds,
instructing, teaching, benefiting, and delighting them,
causing them to enter *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎosānpútí*.
Great King! You should know that good knowing advisors are great causes and conditions,
namely transforming and guiding one to see the Buddha,
and to generate the *Ānòu Duōluó Sānmiǎosānpútí* heart.
Great King! Do you see these two sons?
These two sons have already made offerings to sixty-five hundreds of thousands of millions of *nàyoutā* Ganges sands of Buddhas,
drawing near with respect and reverence,
and at the places of those Buddhas received and upheld the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
having compassion for sentient beings with deviant views, causing them to dwell in right views.'
*Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* then descended from the empty sky, and said to the Buddha:
'World Honored One! The *Rúlái* is very rare,
because of merit and virtue and wisdom,
the fleshy *jì* on the crown of his head shines brightly,
his eyes are long and wide and dark blue,
the white hair mark between his eyebrows is white like *kēyuè*,
his teeth are white, even, and close together, and always have light,
the color of his lips is red and beautiful like the *pínpó* fruit.'
At that time, *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng*,
having praised the Buddha with such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of merits and virtues,
before the *Rúlái*, with one heart joining his palms,
again said to the Buddha:
'World Honored One! It has never been!
The *Rúlái*'s Dharma, is fully accomplished with inconceivable and subtle merits and virtues,
his instructions and conduct are peaceful, safe, happy, and good,
from this day forward, I will no longer follow my own mind, and will not give rise to evil hearts of deviant views, arrogance, anger, and hatred.'
Having said these words, he bowed to the Buddha and departed."
The Buddha told the great assembly:
"What do you think?
Is *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* any different from anyone else?
He is now *Huádé Púsà*.
That *Jìngdé Fūren*, is now the *Guāngzhào Zhuāngyán Xiàng Púsà* before the Buddha.
Out of compassion for *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng* and his retinue,
she was born in that place.
Those two sons, are now *Yàowáng Púsà* and *Yàoshàng Púsà*.
These *Yàowáng* and *Yàoshàng Púsà*, have accomplished such great merits and virtues,
having already planted roots of merit and virtue at the places of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
and accomplished inconceivable and all good merits and virtues.
If there is anyone who knows the names of these two *Púsà*,
all the gods and people in the world should also bow to them."
When the Buddha spoke this *Miàozhuāngyán Wáng Běnshì Pǐn*,
eighty-four thousand people were far from dust and free from defilement,
and in all the Dharmas obtained the pure Dharma eye.
At that time, *Pǔxián Púsà*, with his unconstrained spiritual power, majestic virtue, and renown,
together with great *Púsà* immeasurable, boundless, and uncountable,
came from the east.
The countries he passed through all shook, raining jeweled lotus flowers,
creating immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of music.
Also, together with countless gods, dragons, *yèchā*, *gāntàpó*, *āxiūluó*, *jiālóuluó*, *jǐnnaluó*, *móhóuluóqié*, humans, non-humans, and others, surrounded by a great assembly,
each manifesting their majestic virtue and spiritual power,
they arrived in the *Suōpó* world at *Qíshéjué* Mountain,
bowed their heads to the feet of *Shìjiāmóunífó*,
circumambulated him seven times,
and said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One, in the Buddha country of *Bǎowēidé Shàngwáng*,
I heard from afar that this *Suōpó* world was expounding the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
and together with immeasurable and boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of *Púsà* assemblies came to listen and receive,
I only wish that the World Honored One would expound it for us.
If a good man or good woman, after the *Rúlái*'s extinction,
how can they obtain this *Fǎhuá Jīng*?"
The Buddha told *Pǔxián Púsà*:
"If a good man or good woman, accomplishes four Dharmas, after the *Rúlái*'s extinction,
they will obtain this *Fǎhuá Jīng*:
first, they are protected and念 by all the Buddhas,
second, they plant roots of merit and virtue,
third, they enter the assembly of right concentration,
fourth, they generate the heart of saving all sentient beings.
Good man, good woman, having accomplished these four Dharmas,
after the *Rúlái*'s extinction, they will certainly obtain this scripture."
At that time, Bodhisattva Pǔxián said to the Buddha:
"World Honored One! In the last five hundred years, in this turbid and evil world,
if there are those who receive and uphold this scripture,
I will protect them,
remove their decay and suffering,
and grant them peace,
so that none who seek to take advantage may find an opportunity.
Whether it be demons, demon sons, demon daughters,
demon subjects, those possessed by demons, yakshas, or rākṣasas,
kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, kiṃnaras, pūtanas,
or vetālas, and all those who trouble people, none shall find an opportunity.
If these people walk or stand,
reciting this scripture,
at that time, I will ride on a white elephant king with six tusks,
and together with a great assembly of Bodhisattvas, I will go to their location,
and manifest myself,
making offerings, protecting them,
and comforting their hearts,
also for the sake of making offerings to the *Fǎhuá Jīng*.
If these people sit and contemplate this scripture,
at that time, I will again ride on a white elephant king and appear before them.
If they forget even a single phrase or verse of the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
I will teach them, recite it with them, and restore their fluency.
At that time, those who receive, uphold, and recite the *Fǎhuá Jīng* will see my form,
be greatly joyful,
and become even more diligent.
Because they see me,
they will immediately attain samādhi and dhāraṇīs,
named the Revolving Dhāraṇī,
the Hundred Thousand Million Revolving Dhāraṇī,
and the Dharma Sound Expedient Dhāraṇī.
They will attain such dhāraṇīs.
"World Honored One! If in the future, in the last five hundred years, in this turbid and evil world,
bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, those who seek,
those who receive and uphold, those who recite, and those who write, desire to cultivate this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
they should, for three seven-day periods, be single-mindedly diligent.
After the completion of the three seven-day periods,
I will ride on a white elephant with six tusks,
surrounded by immeasurable Bodhisattvas,
and with a form that all beings delight in seeing,
I will appear before them and preach the Dharma,
instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them,
and also give them dhāraṇī mantras.
By obtaining these dhāraṇī mantras,
no non-human being will be able to destroy them,
nor will they be deluded or disturbed by women.
I myself will always protect these people.
May the World Honored One allow me to speak this dhāraṇī mantra."
Then, before the Buddha, he spoke the mantra, saying:
"Ā tán dì (1), tán tuó pó dì (2), tán tuó pó dì (3), tán tuó jū shě lì (4), tán tuó xiū tuó lì (5),
xiū tuó lì (6), xiū tuó luó pó dǐ (7), Fó tuó bō shān nì (8), sà pó tuó luó ní ā pó duō ní (9),
sà pó pó shā ā pó duō ní (10), xiū ā pó duō ní (11), Sēng qié pó lǚ chā ní (12),
Sēng qié niè qié tuó ní (13), ā sēng qí (14), Sēng qié bō qié dì (15), dì lì ā duò sēng qié dōu lüè ā luó dì pó luó dì (16),
sà pó Sēng qié sān mó dì qié lán dì (17), sà pó dá mó xiū bō lì chà dì (18),
sà pó sà duǒ lóu tuó jiāo shě lüè ā nǎo qié dì (19), xīn ā pí jí lì dì dì (20).
"World Honored One! If any Bodhisattva hears this dhāraṇī,
they should know the power of Pǔxián's divine abilities.
If the *Fǎhuá Jīng* circulates in Jambudvīpa, and there are those who receive and uphold it,
they should have this thought:
'All of this is due to the power and might of Pǔxián.'
If there are those who receive, uphold, and recite it, correctly remember it,
understand its meaning, and practice according to the teachings,
they should know that these people are practicing the conduct of Pǔxián,
deeply planting good roots in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas,
and their heads are caressed by the hands of all the Tathāgatas.
If they only write it,
when these people's lives end, they will be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
At that time, eighty-four thousand heavenly maidens will play various musical instruments and come to greet them.
These people will immediately adorn themselves with seven-jeweled crowns and enjoy happiness and pleasure among the female attendants;
how much more so for those who receive, uphold, recite, correctly remember,
understand its meaning, and practice according to the teachings.
If there are people who receive, uphold, and recite it, and understand its meaning,
when these people's lives end,
a thousand Buddhas will extend their hands,
so that they will not be terrified, nor fall into evil realms,
and they will immediately go to the Tuṣita Heaven to the place of Bodhisattva Mílè.
Bodhisattva Mílè, surrounded by a great assembly of thirty-two-featured Bodhisattvas,
and attended by hundreds of thousands of millions of heavenly maidens,
will be born among them,
and have such merits and benefits.
Therefore, wise people should single-mindedly write it themselves,
or have others write it,
receive, uphold, and recite it,
correctly remember it, and practice according to the teachings.
"World Honored One!
Now, with my divine powers, I protect this scripture,
and after the Tathāgata's extinction, within Jambudvīpa, I will widely propagate it,
so that it will not be cut off."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Pǔxián!
You are able to protect and assist this scripture,
bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to many sentient beings.
You have already accomplished inconceivable merits,
and possess deep and great compassion.
From a distant past, you have aroused the intent for anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and are able to make such vows of divine power to protect this scripture.
I will use my divine powers to protect those who can receive and uphold the name of Bodhisattva Pǔxián.
Pǔxián!
If there are those who receive, uphold, and recite,
correctly remember, cultivate, and write this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
they should know that these people will see Śākyamuni Buddha,
as if they have heard this scripture from the Buddha's own mouth;
they should know that these people are making offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha;
they should know that these people are praised as 'Excellent' by the Buddha;
they should know that these people's heads are caressed by the hand of Śākyamuni Buddha;
they should know that these people are covered by the robe of Śākyamuni Buddha.
Such people will no longer be attached to worldly pleasures,
nor delight in heterodox scriptures, writings, or penmanship,
nor will they like to be close to such people and all evildoers—
such as butchers, those who raise pigs, sheep, chickens, and dogs, or hunters,
or those who flaunt and sell female beauty—
these people's minds are upright and honest, they have correct recollection,
and they have the power of blessings and virtue.
These people are not troubled by the three poisons,
nor are they troubled by jealousy, arrogance, false arrogance, or exaggerated arrogance.
These people are content with little and know satisfaction,
and are able to cultivate the practice of Pǔxián.
Pǔxián!
If in the last five hundred years after the Tathāgata's extinction,
if there are people who see those who receive, uphold, and recite the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
they should have this thought:
'These people will soon go to the place of enlightenment,
destroy all the hordes of demons,
attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
turn the Dharma wheel,
beat the Dharma drum,
blow the Dharma conch,
and rain the Dharma rain,
and sit upon the lion's Dharma seat in the midst of the assembly of gods and humans.'
"Pǔxián!
If in future generations, there are those who receive, uphold, and recite this scripture,
these people will no longer be attached to clothing, bedding, food, or the necessities of life,
their wishes will not be in vain,
and they will also receive their rewards in this present life.
If there are people who scorn and slander them, saying:
'You are crazy,
doing these things in vain,
and will ultimately gain nothing,'
such sinful retribution will result in them being born without eyes in every life;
if there are those who make offerings and praise them,
they will receive manifest rewards in this present life.
If they see those who uphold this scripture,
and expose their faults and evils,
whether true or untrue,
these people will suffer from white leprosy in this present life.
If there are those who mock and laugh at them,
in every life, their teeth will be sparse and incomplete,
their lips will be ugly, their noses will be flat, their hands and feet will be twisted,
their eyes will be askew,
their bodies will be foul-smelling and dirty,
with festering sores and pus,
dropsy, shortness of breath, and all kinds of severe and chronic diseases.
Therefore, Pǔxián!
If you see those who receive and uphold this scripture,
you should rise to greet them from afar,
and should revere them as you would the Buddha."
When this chapter on "Pǔxián's Encouragement to Diligence" was spoken,
immeasurable and boundless Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā River, attained hundreds of thousands of millions of revolving dhāraṇīs;
Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the dust motes of a three-thousand-great-thousand world, perfected the path of Pǔxián.
When the Buddha spoke this scripture,
Pǔxián and all the other Bodhisattvas,
Śāriputra and all the other Śrāvakas,
as well as all the gods, dragons, humans, non-humans, and others,
in the entire great assembly, were all greatly joyful,
received and upheld the Buddha's words,
paid homage, and departed.

*The Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Sutra*, scroll [number]. Below this, the Dunhuang version has the inscription, "Written respectfully for my deceased younger sister by the faithful gentleman Zhāng Jūnchè in the third year of the Shangyuan era," with fifteen characters. [Note].
A Treatise on the *Fǎ Huá Jīng* [Lotus Sūtra] Composed by the *Shāmén* [Monk] *Sēng Ruì* of the Later *Qín*
Dynasty The *Fǎ Huá Jīng* is the secret treasure of all Buddhas and the true essence of all scriptures. The name "Lotus"
(*Huá*) illuminates its origin, and calling it *Fēntuólì* praises its magnificence. Since its arising is profound and its meaning is exceedingly subtle, few can
enter its gate without a knowledgeable person transmitting it. Now, the essence of all herbs and trees is the basis of their fruits, and the eighty-four
thousand *Dharma* treasuries are the origin of the *Dao* fruits. Therefore, it is used as an analogy. Among all flowers, the lotus is the most supreme. Before the flower
blooms, it is called *Qūmóluó*; as it blooms and begins to
wither, it is called *Jiāmóluó*; and in its prime, it is called *Fēntuólì*. The unopened flower symbolizes the Two Vehicles,
the withering flower represents *Níhuán* [Nirvana], and its unique splendor is sufficient to symbolize this scripture. As for the *Bānruò* [Prajna] scriptures, their depth is unsurpassed,
so those who seek the *Dao* return to them. Their scope is all-encompassing,
so those who seek passage use them to cross over. However, their general approach is to prioritize adaptation to circumstances
and, in the realm of expedient matters, they must rely on skillful means as their tool. The use of skillful
means for transformation, while greatly enlightening beings, is insufficient in terms of true substance. Everything belongs to the *Fǎ Huá Jīng*, and this is indeed fitting.
Examining its profound meaning, it is vast and expansive, encompassing a great deal. Is it merely about explaining reality,
returning to the origin, and completely determining different paths? It is truly about greatly illuminating the principle of enlightenment, encompassing
the past and present. Saying that the Buddha's lifespan is immeasurable means that endless eons are not enough to explain its length;
that the manifested bodies are countless means that myriad forms are not enough to differentiate their essence. Therefore, the measure of life
determines its innumerability, the manifested bodies clarify its lack of true form, *Pǔxián* [Samantabhadra] reveals its non-becoming, and *Duōbǎo* [Prabhutaratna] illuminates its non-extinction.
Surpassing ancient times to arrive at the present, ten thousand generations are like a single
day; grasping the myriad transformations to awaken to the profound, a thousand paths are without different tracks. If this is the case,
then countless births are not enough to expect existence, and eternal stillness cannot be said to be extinction.
Searching for the profound principle to sever the past, one loses effort in original non-being; controlling the reins of the mind with *sānmèi* [samadhi],
one forgets the expectations in the Two Vehicles. Since the scripture flowed into this land, although it has nearly reached a hundred years,
the translators were ignorant of its subtle truths, and the spiritual gates were not opened; those who discussed it deviated from its standards,
and its hidden traces were rarely followed. One could only search and study with white hair, yet none have glimpsed
its gate. *Yáo Sōng*, the *Sīlì Xiàowèi* [Director of the Capital Police] and Left General, the Marquis of *Ānchéng* of the *Qín* dynasty,
emulated the rhyme of the profound gate, dwelling in a mind beyond the world, focusing his sincerity on this scripture, and his faith reached its peak. He often thought
about searching for its text, deeply recognizing the translators' errors. When he encountered the *dharma* master *Jiūmóluó* [Kumarajiva], he had him
transmit and write it, pointing out its great truth. It was like soaring high through the multiple heavens,
climbing Mount *Kūnlún* and looking down. At that time, there were over eight hundred
monks listening, receiving, and understanding, all of whom were outstanding talents and heroes of their time.
It was the eighth year of *Hóngshǐ*, in the year of *Chúnhuǒ*.
*Lǔ* state Grand Madam *Zhāng*, humbly on the
anniversary of her deceased husband, Grand Tutor and Grand Chancellor Lord *Lǐ*, respectfully donates a string of pure coins

to the *Fúzhōu Kāiyuán Sì Dàzàngjīng Sī* [Fuzhou Kaiyuan Temple Great Sutra Depository], to engrave phoenix-lettered cases for the seven fascicles of the *Miàofǎ Liánhuā Jīng* [Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra],
the *Fǎ Huá Sānmèi* [Lotus Samadhi], etc.
I humbly use this superior cause to recommend that his august spirit be reborn in the pure land. Respectfully inscribed on the fifteenth day of the first
month of the twenty-first year of *Shàoxīng*.
